{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ca68660343c8147e751d945925622782"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:0016b176dc386a2ff2bb8aef0a1b5de5","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"A demonstrated undeclared material dependency, missing required totality declaration or non-total operation violates the F_D contract and yields falsified or refusal(constraint) under the applicable assessment. If a valid assessed basis cannot decide totality, return indeterminate and leave eligibility unestablished. If assessment was never performed, there is no assessment result. Before activation, missing grants, basis or context closure retain their own admission outcomes instead of being relabelled as F_D success or failure.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Locator ownership, imports and staleness watch: Every locus is an owning corpus clause. A concept's defining section supplies its owning clause, with context ownership supplied directly or by its member. Imported concepts cite the defining section and identify the importing declaration or stated owner relation in the relation clause; otherwise that clause only locates an externally stated relationship. A concept outside all bounded contexts declared by its member uses the member as source context; §16 indexes it without declaring a new context. An index watch separately records locator path and digest from deciding sources, and locator drift makes dependent surfaces or frames stale without making the index a meaning owner.

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:fb42a8b9db1ba218cdb616fb7361239d"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:07e69ef949f8606b43658eb92f35173d","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1562,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"### 11.7A Conforming agentic development

This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
graph-native worksite. An agentic coder produces governed work by
following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).

Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
to admit (P6).

The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
requirement, design and ticket chain, the constructive evaluation loop of
§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
constitutional process (P0, P6).

The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the
packet carries only the smallest declared authority sufficient to decide
the step, with its source refs, and that conformance is enforced by
admitting the produced artifact rather than by enlarging what the agent
must hold. Compression is prompt input and never the deciding authority
(P0, P6). What a derived surface may decide is owned by
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition and Standalone scope; this section adds only the ODD limit
that follows. A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The walkthrough proves at two levels. The work it produces must be lawful:
correct change class, traceable, admitted. A point where the walkthrough
cannot proceed is a method defect only when a competent agent, correctly
configured and using the declared authority, still cannot decide because
of ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or an undecidable
change class in an owning surface. That defect is repriced into the owning
authority surface, as a failed manual traversal is a graph defect under
§11.7 (P6, P5).

An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

This proof is independent of any automated runtime. A live lane that
depends on external execution conditions, such as an overloaded model API
or a flaky transport, cannot prove the constitutional process sound,
because it conflates process validity with runtime availability. The
walkthrough proves the process; the runtime only executes it (P6, P5).

The validator is the conformance gate. The constitutional process is an
interface contract, and interface conformance is enforced by validating
artifacts against the contract, not by the conformer holding the contract.
This profile does not declare the artifact rules again: tickets,
change-class declarations, design-module derivations and execution
contracts are admitted under SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS, which already require
a drafted classification to be admitted or rejected against deterministic
criteria rather than taken as automatic truth. This profile requires only
that agentic development pass through that admission. The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,
fail-closed and naming the violated rule, exactly as a typed asset is
enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

This keeps the F_P and F_D split at the method layer. The agentic coder is
F_P: it reasons, drafts and proposes within the declared packet. Admission
uses F_D only when the §5 total-domain contract is established, and its own
contract and authority determine what artifact-conformance decision it may
make. An unresolved eligibility assessment stays open under the migration
relation; an unchanged-subject evaluator still preserves that subject. The walkthrough
establishes that the process can be followed; admission establishes that
each act of following it conforms (P6, P0).

Conformance is not approval by usage. A passed admission and a completed
walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification. Shared method
change still follows §9: repeated agentic execution does not make grey
work constitutional. The agentic coder conforms to the method; it does not
amend the method by acting (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F11.%20Core%20law%2F11.7A%20Conforming%20agentic%20development","start_line":1474}],"statement":"A competent correctly configured actor unable to decide from actual owning authority because of missing/ambiguous/contradictory law exposes a method defect for owner re-entry. Ignored authority, stale memory or faulty reasoning is actor error; malformed artifacts still refuse. Runtime API/transport failure is not proof of process validity or invalidity. Retain the distinction between followability, artifact admission, deterministic-kind eligibility and actual execution availability.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: A competent correctly configured actor unable to decide from actual owning authority because of missing/ambiguous/contradictory law exposes a method defect for owner re-entry. Ignored authority, stale memory or faulty reasoning is actor error; malformed artifacts still refuse. Runtime API/transport failure is not proof of process validity or invalidity. Retain the distinction between followability, artifact admission, deterministic-kind eligibility and actual execution availability.

Method role

[SPEC_METHOD](SPEC_METHOD.md) is the general constitutional method: the
baseline for goals, intent, product, requirements, design and lawful
re-entry. This profile is the graph-native ODD product-authoring method
whose primary constructive carrier is GTL-defined graph functions. It holds
two kinds of law: constitutional law for graph-native traversal governance
(assets, vectors, traversal, graph functions), and product-authoring law
for building an ODD product correctly over that substrate (P1, P6).

The profile does not replace a product-specific domain method such as the
world-model profile (WORLD_MODEL, tier 3). Where a product is both ODD and
world-model-driven, this profile governs graph-native structure and ODD
product shape and the world-model profile governs world-model semantics,
publication and composition law. The two compose (P1, P4a).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F2.%20Method%20role","start_line":201},{"end_line":239,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"## 3. Method composition

This profile alone does not suffice for domain-correct product work. It
gives the structural law for how a graph-native ODD product should be
built. It does not give the product's domain semantics, its current intent
and product-definition line, its local capability and constraint
requirements, or its currently ratified design surfaces (P1, P2).

The composition rule: this profile says how to build the product as a
graph-native ODD product; domain methods say what semantic law the product
must honour; the local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design say
what the currently ratified local line is. For a graph-native
software-development ODD product, this profile provides the substrate and
structural law and the product's local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
requirements, design records and GTL surfaces provide the local line. For
a world-model product, this profile provides the substrate and structural
law, the world-model profile provides the semantic law, and the product's
local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design provide the local
line (P1, P2).

An agent that reads only this profile should understand the paradigm.
To build one concrete product correctly it must then read the
product-specific method and the local authority surfaces (P1, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F3.%20Method%20composition","start_line":217}],"statement":"SPEC_METHOD owns general constitutional lifecycle/re-entry; ODD supplies graph-native structure; applicable domain methods supply domain law; current Product Intent/Product/requirements/accepted design supply the local line. WORLD_MODEL applies only when selected for its semantics and publication/composition. A builder needs these actual bound sources, not ODD alone. F12 foundation-to-law family: F12 traces project-binding rules to foundational commitments plus instance premises: independent project authorities; chosen existing layout; shared workspace/machine; recurring terms with different context meanings; and immutable released method versions selected, installed and replaced by projects. P1, P2, P3 and P6 are independent; P0 is recovered; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with the premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable. The family traces imports without owning that law, distinguishes consequences from member-owned interoperability/domain choices and supplies a per-row consumer-locus index.

clauses.statement: Each constraint identifies removed semantic ambiguity and justifies its added reasoning complexity through sufficient contraction of admissible interpretations. Rival authority, failure-classification uncertainty and evidence uncertainty count only as material alternative interpretations, not independent benefits. Greater capability may enlarge the bounded relation resolvable but grants no authority, weakens no invariant and waives no acceptance. Detailed symbolic design is proportional when one bounded model within capacity resolves material alternatives; divergent implementation paths, states, tests, reviews and joins are counterfactual evidence of those alternatives, not another numerator. A prior design removing no material alternative is disproportionate, as are additions duplicating truth, adding reconciliation or expanding reasoning without materially reducing ambiguity. Existing obligations should absorb detail where ownership and meaning survive. Repeated acquisition, assembly, hashing, preparation, status, review and evidence generation require an identified change, decision or assurance need; repetition adds neither validity nor independence, reuse remains conditional, and materially outcome-affecting operational assumptions require cited UP-019 qualification. For governed cost claims, declare allowance, report measured or unmeasured spend, separate concealable cost components, and declare supported dimensions/workloads before qualification. Report volume is not model traffic. No universal quota, ticket/actor count or separate accounting carrier follows.

An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their
material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the
acquired views that project it follow
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)
and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable
positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),
including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection
that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows
[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and
[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;
these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

Purpose and material relation of the assurance relations: they connect
construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared
errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining
evidence whose applicability is established (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FFormal%20representation","start_line":1463},{"end_line":186,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Finite maps and consumer adequacy

Fix the same subject/basis and reports `X={S,F,I}`. Qualified records are
`H={hS,hF,hI}` and views `V={vS,vF,vI}`. Policy readouts are
`D={advance,block_falsified,block_indeterminate}`. The complete functions are:

| X | `build:X→H` | `view:H→V` | Both `j:H→D` and `h:V→D` read out |
|---|---|---|---|
| S | hS | vS | advance |
| F | hF | vF | block_falsified |
| I | hI | vI | block_indeterminate |

The three rows prove pointwise `j=h o view`. Arrow equality here is pointwise
finite-function equality; composition is ordinary composition and identities
return their inputs. The constant subject-only projection cannot factor j:
hS and hI share its output but require different readouts.

The following is a finite mathematical argument and executable structural
check, not a qualified categorical demonstration under FOUNDATIONS.
For the structural counterexample, take the finite chain category with
objects X,H,V,D and exactly the displayed generated function for each ordered
pair in that chain, including all identities and composites. There are ten
arrows; equality compares their endpoints and pointwise action. The target
terminal category has object `*` and only `id_*`. Send every source object
to `*` and every arrow to `id_*`: identities and composition are preserved,
yet that map cannot recover j's distinct readouts. The program exhausts
identity and associative composition checks for this bound fragment and
the terminal map. Those structural checks and the explicit counterexample
support their finite claims, not consumer adequacy of an arbitrary functor.
The full categorical demonstration still requires the applicable a_c
representation and supporting assessment under FOUNDATIONS; these executable
tables do not replace those obligations or discharge unresolved H1.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FFinite%20maps%20and%20consumer%20adequacy","start_line":155}],"statement":"Identity and composition preservation can hold for a map that loses a required consumer readout. State the object and arrow maps, equality, domain and preservation obligations before claiming a categorical functor; even discharged functor laws do not by themselves establish semantic adequacy, information preservation or implementation correctness. No registry, annotation syntax or implementation architecture is mandated merely by these conditions.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Capability requires an independently law-derived oracle, identifying bounded combinations and distinguishing violations from implementation restatement.

Mapping to the current common kind is an explicit eligibility and operation-profile assessment, not an automatic rewrite based on spelling or patch version.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":848,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Deterministic-kind migration

A successor that adopts the total deterministic kind of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
preserves each existing evaluation operation's unchanged subject, admissible
reads, witness/log outputs, permitted writes, stops/results, authority and
invalidation conditions. That profile alone does not
establish the new kind's totality, closed dependencies or declared outcomes.
The old deterministic evaluation/proof definition supplies no general
termination argument. Assess each proposed use against this relation (P3, P6):

| Evidence and declared migration status | Successor disposition |
|---|---|
| Establishes the new totality, closed-dependency and outcome contract | Map to common F_D plus the unchanged operation profile and exact traversal binding. Preserve the evidence and grants. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished, and the owner has identified the missing evidence or a separately declared bounded successor and its remediation obligation | Keep that identified migration pending. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while it remains applicable; it gains no successor F_D standing. A narrower domain or fuel-bounded implementation has its own contract, identity, exhaustion outcomes and affected preservation evidence; it does not retrospectively prove the old operation total or preserve every old continuation. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished and no supported remediation or successor classification has been selected | Retain the exact legacy meaning and evidence with an explicit unresolved successor-classification obligation until its owner disposes it. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while applicable. Grant neither new F_D standing nor an automatic F_P label; the affected successor claim stays open. |

An old deterministic evaluator with unestablished termination or an
undeclared material dependency takes the second or third row, even if it
preserves the judged subject: the second row requires an identified evidence
gap/remediation or selected bounded successor; absent that, the third records
the unresolved classification. Evidence alone need not choose the owner's
remediation. This relation imposes no general decision procedure for totality.
These eligibility/remediation cases are not additional semantic dispositions
under this section. Generic role descriptions and schematic traversal contracts are not concrete
operations with an implementation to qualify; their use still binds the
kind and operation contracts when instantiated.

ODD admission and closure retain their named operation owners under
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5's authority boundary](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds).
Exhaustion
retains the evaluated predicate and its signature/traversal stop mapping,
as [the conformance examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish.

Immutable consumers keep their selected edition's meaning. New consumers
explicitly select the complete successor and operation profiles. A stable
concept URN is not its immutable calculus edition
([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §8](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#8-calculus-identity)). Migration
records the old release, manifest, member and clauses and the applicable row
above. Current URN lookup never reinterprets history. A versioned import or
alias records its justified supersession and grants no broader permission.
Disposition and qualification retain the separate obligations of this
section; unresolved mappings block the affected successor claim.

Broadening operation purpose while strengthening totality, dependency and
evidence requirements is a substantive semantic change. A patch-shaped
version label by itself promises no compatibility. The release's version
assessment identifies the selected predecessor, affected consumer mappings
and remaining obligations. This relation settles no general version-line
policy and waives no acceptance gate.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F9.%20Successor%20baseline%20conservation%20%28STDO-UP-015%29%2FDeterministic-kind%20migration","start_line":799}],"label":"Legacy deterministic-kind migration"}}}

clauses.statement: Legacy deterministic-kind migration: Each legacy F_D use retains its exact original meaning, basis, grants and evidence. Mapping to the current common kind is an explicit eligibility and operation-profile assessment, not an automatic rewrite based on spelling or patch version.

Activated frames declare topology invalidators of coordinates/materiality. Detected material mutation requires reevaluation, revision or recharting before reuse. Material frame revision creates a new coordinate and identifies affected activations/results/coverage; all results bound to the prior revision reopen until recorded re-check establishes independence from change or reevaluation occurs. Silence keeps none closed; ACTIVATION §7 governs reuse.

Every refinement value maps to exactly one core value for its own named predicate, which travels with it. Satisfied under one predicate cannot satisfy another. Phases

The release process has three phases (P0, P3, P6):

1. mutable candidate construction;
2. immutable publication under the selected profile, with RC selector
   advancement only for an RC line; and
3. exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.

An accepted RC needs no second final cut. RC publication immediately makes
the new highest ordinal discoverable through its selector. Stable publication
makes its one exact tag discoverable under the stable profile. Acceptance is
a verdict over the exact immutable subject, not a second carrier. A change
to qualifying bytes requires a higher RC on an applicable RC line or a new

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FReview%20findings%20and%20bug%20items","start_line":536}],"statement":"Reviewer authority is evaluation only: no candidate editing, repair implementation, construction, transformation, admission, publication, candidate mutation, priority, release/MVP disposition, decision, next action or activation. It cannot substitute Worker summary, reconstruct assurance-owned semantics, flatten unbound evidence or silently expand scope. It returns one core result with findings, counterexamples, evidence-bound triage and residuals sufficient for Executive priority/disposition where decidable. Governing invariants are RF-001–RF-017, ACTIVATION §1/§3, EVALUATION §1/§3/§7 and applicable Product/design/identity/release law. TICKETS UP-007 and governing basis determine review requirement and traceability; EVALUATION §3 determines independence and §1/§3/§7 assurance/freeze. The profile adds no universal review or independence test and no second verdict/disposition family; ACTIVATION retains assessment/disposition ownership. Material changes in candidate, authority, basis, evidence population, severity scale, dependency, configuration, scope or independence invalidate review. This excludes candidate mutation and repair; an independently bound grant may authorize only the exact finding-report write under TICKETS §4, retaining its visibility and source linkage.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Reviewer authority is evaluation only: no candidate editing, repair implementation, construction, transformation, admission, publication, candidate mutation, priority, release/MVP disposition, decision, next action or activation. It cannot substitute Worker summary, reconstruct assurance-owned semantics, flatten unbound evidence or silently expand scope. It returns one core result with findings, counterexamples, evidence-bound triage and residuals sufficient for Executive priority/disposition where decidable. Governing invariants are RF-001–RF-017, ACTIVATION §1/§3, EVALUATION §1/§3/§7 and applicable Product/design/identity/release law. TICKETS UP-007 and governing basis determine review requirement and traceability; EVALUATION §3 determines independence and §1/§3/§7 assurance/freeze. The profile adds no universal review or independence test and no second verdict/disposition family; ACTIVATION retains assessment/disposition ownership. Material changes in candidate, authority, basis, evidence population, severity scale, dependency, configuration, scope or independence invalidate review. This excludes candidate mutation and repair; an independently bound grant may authorize only the exact finding-report write under TICKETS §4, retaining its visibility and source linkage.

Work selects a dependency-ready frontier at the required subjects and revisions.
A cycle in declared Product relationships need not be a cycle in the selected
work. A cycle of current prerequisite claims requires an executable resolution:

iteration with its continuation/stop conditions. Naming a lead alone does not
supply a missing prerequisite or establish convergence.

Replacing a constituent or refining it into further Products preserves the
consumer's material contract: meaning, preconditions, effects, failures,
authority, lifecycle, evidence and subsequent obligations. A semantic change
requires an authorized successor relation and affected reassessment. The [ACTIVATION refinement contract](ACTIVATION.md#refinement) governs this
preservation. Matching signatures, labels or a sample output is insufficient (P4a, P6). New capabilities may be

clauses.statement: A finding can block only if it falsifies the claim, exposes competing/ambiguous acceptance-path authority, violates applicable active authority/safety/retained accepted behaviour, or establishes durable material architectural foreclosure of an admitted Product outcome. These are necessary, not all automatically sufficient. Valid falsification of a mandatory claim under a non-waivable hard stop blocks regardless of priority/cutoff. Otherwise the decision owner decides using exact affected claim, governed outcome/decision, hard stops and Product cutoff policy; below cutoff no automatic block follows and accepted residuals stay explicit. Findings meeting none do not block. Outside observations alone neither widen subject, block the bounded claim nor require another ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment. Severity mechanically selects neither priority nor blocking; priority erases neither severity nor hard stops. This member sets no cutoff.

An adopting Product may explicitly select the following response policy in its
frame basis. The labels have no numeric meaning outside that adoption; the

This policy never waives applicable hard stops, mandatory claims, acceptance
conditions, access restrictions or operation grants. Those owners may require
an earlier hold at any priority. A P3–P5 item may outlive a local work claim's
closure only when that claim does not require the unfixed behaviour; assigning
that priority cannot satisfy a false mandatory claim. No review-to-work ratio or additional

items and their actual verification state are owned by

A permitted A → B use does not entail A's access to B's dependencies. Neither
A → B plus B → C nor two routes to a shared leaf imply a union of their grants.
Each onward acquisition, disclosure or delegated effect needs authority for that
actor, purpose and path, including any permitted onward use of returned material.
Existing delegation may authorize a chain explicitly; its scope cannot expand
silently at a recursive step.

A provider may encapsulate internal dependencies behind an adequate contract.
Consumers need not flatten every implementation dependency into a direct edge.
Where an outer claim materially relies on a far-side contract, assumption,
evidence item or acquisition, that reliance and its applicable authority must be
preserved through the boundary. Unknown impact is not evidence of encapsulation.

Durable Product consumption and bounded authorized inspection are different
relations. A Reviewer or diagnostic Worker may inspect a larger causal cone under
an explicit access grant without thereby adopting those internals as a runtime
dependency or gaining a write grant. If findings become a continuing construction
constraint or dependency, their producer, applicability and governing relation
must be retained.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-04%20%E2%80%94%20Recursive%20authority%20and%20information%20eligibility","start_line":917}],"statement":"A→B plus B→C does not authorize A to read, disclose, use, execute or mutate C, nor union the grants of two routes to a shared leaf. Each activation and directed use retains its own eligible information, purpose and grant. Adequate provider encapsulation is allowed: A need not read C merely because B uses it, but material far-side assumptions needed for A’s claim must be retained through a lawful sufficient interface. A separately granted inspection does not create a durable implementation dependency.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Each activation and directed use retains its own eligible information, purpose and grant. A separately granted inspection does not create a durable implementation dependency.

Use the bundled [read_basis.py](../scripts/read_basis.py) with the exact manager,
store and definition already selected by the control intake. It calls the
existing manager's read-only `status --verify` and `resolve`, checks manifest
and member digests, and returns identities plus only requested source sections.
It performs no discovery, admission, access-policy decision or dispatch.

```sh
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py check \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition>
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py read \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition> \
  --member standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md --list-headings
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py read \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition> \
  --member standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md --heading '11. The activation packet'
```

Replace the placeholders with the named routes; do not discover a different
manager/store when one fails. The default store may be used only when the
control binding selects it explicitly. Python 3.11+ is the helper's runtime;

Fix one subject and the one-assessment policy Γ. States are `U` (unassessed),
`S` (satisfied report), `F` (falsified report) and `I` (indeterminate report).
Inputs are `assess_S`, `assess_F`, `assess_I` and `advance`. From U an assess
input records that report; from any assessed state it is refused as already
assessed, preserving state. `advance` preserves state and is allowed only
from S; it returns `block_unassessed`, `block_falsified` or
`block_indeterminate` from the other states. This is the complete transition
and decision rule for every state/input pair. There is no reset input in Γ.
A different contract can permit reassessment or re-entry.

The weak observation “satisfied assessment exists” maps U, F and I to false
and S to true. U and I nevertheless require incompatible first-assessment
decisions. Thus no decision function over that observation can preserve the
fixed policy. In a human handover, “not approved” similarly fails to say
whether to perform the first assessment or preserve a completed undecidable
assessment and follow its declared continuation.

Define `alpha(U)=(subject,basis,null)` and
`alpha(s)=(subject,basis,s)` for s in `{S,F,I}`, with those subject and basis
fixed by Γ. Define `delta_hat` and `T_hat` by the complete rule above on
these records. Every state/input satisfies
`delta=delta_hat o alpha` (with the unchanged input supplied) and
`alpha(T(s,u))=T_hat(alpha(s),u)`. The readouts “satisfied exists”, exact
standing, permitted first assessment and advance decision are preserved.
The program checks all 16 one-step cells and every length-four input
sequence from every state. Exact one-step preservation with the closed
domain and identical next-state basis also composes by induction to every
finite sequence in this model. Approximate models have no such automatic
bound.

All four states remain distinguishable. This is a sufficiency witness with
no state aggregation, not evidence of compression, minimum context,
cross-task context selection, Markov sufficiency outside Γ, or cheaper
operation. Authority and hold distinctions are exact in this example.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FContinuation-sensitive%20sufficiency","start_line":85},{"end_line":153,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Qualified references

For this fixture a complete assessed record carries subject, basis,
standing, producer, obligation/version, authority and invalidators. Exact
local keys `report:S`, `report:F`, `report:I` resolve those records. An
independent copy preserves all required fields and the preceding policy
readout. The pointer `candidate-v1` alone maps every report to the same
bytes/identity; S and I then require different continuations, falsifying
its sufficiency for that consumer. Adding a type name alone cannot repair
missing standing.

The acquisition model takes three report keys and the explicit booleans
accessible, target-present and basis-current. Its complete eight-row oracle
per key is: all four inaccessible cases return `inaccessible`; of the four
accessible cases, both absent-target cases return `missing`, the present but
old-basis case returns `stale`, and only the present/current case returns the
qualified record as `resolved`. This yields 24 tested cells. Unavailable,
missing and stale targets yield no usable record and keep the dependent
sufficiency claim unsupported; their actual gap, invalidation, refusal or
residual follows the consuming operation's owner, not a universal result
mapping added by this fixture. The executable also checks that resolution
does not mutate the record store and that valid readouts survive.

These access flags and version comparisons model an acquisition boundary;
they are not observed filesystem, transport or human-handover behavior.
The currentness test covers the declared basis-version invalidator only.
Other material invalidators require their own scoped evidence. Logical review
checks the human handover and required residual meanings; actual use remains
unperformed. A hash-based realization would additionally state its collision,
authenticity and access assumptions; no digest alone proves semantic
sufficiency. A manual document reference and a mixed handover can use the
same record and policy without any annotation architecture or event log.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FQualified%20references","start_line":122}],"statement":"The example distinguishes U unassessed, S satisfied, F falsified and I indeterminate for one assessment policy; only S advances. The 24 declared access cases exercise the finite policy model, not filesystem enforcement.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

{"family":"relations","record":{"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:1a085883e8a5b9d30061831101efaa24","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:relation-kind:governing:requires","owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","qualifiers":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":577,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md","quote":"### Review findings and bug items

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FReview%20findings%20and%20bug%20items","start_line":536},{"end_line":387,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md","quote":"### Landing, closure and release

Landing makes an exact candidate available at an authorized checkpoint or
integration destination. It is an operation under its existing grant, not
acceptance of the candidate's claims. Work closure applies the stated closing
condition; release applies the separately selected publication and acceptance
conditions of [RELEASE](RELEASE.md). Record these as separate decisions (P6,
P3).

Review supplies QA evidence for those decisions. A pending review does not by
itself hold landing: an admitted candidate may land after its bounded work
and fix pass, while review of that exact candidate runs beside subsequent
authorized work. A required review holds the closure or acceptance claim that
depends on its complete report. A governing landing condition, applicable hard
stop or missing operation authority still prevents landing; availability is
no waiver. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks)
binds the optional profile's repair/recheck cadence (P6, P2).

Permitted downstream work may consume a landed candidate before its review
reports, carrying its exact identity, unresolved conditions and dependency
links. This is provisional use, not admitted truth. A later material finding
invalidates the affected dependent results under
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); unrelated valid results
remain reusable. Repair and re-evaluation follow those dependencies before
further reliance (P4b, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F5.%20Acceptance%2FLanding%2C%20closure%20and%20release","start_line":363}],"kind":"requires","meaning":"Bug-item verification and a closed report do not alone satisfy the separate landing, work-closure or release decision."},"scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"],"source":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ca69fb183db64514704157409ebe758d","target":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:202645bb83ea176a0349095be76b5e7a"}}

clauses.statement: Requirements and design jointly govern code; this edge does not grant requirements-only sufficiency.

Intent and Product each have one canonical WHAT entrypoint; specification may locate multiple requirement/specification surfaces. Canonical how.build_tenants entries carry stable identities and root/design/implementation locations; an optional TENANT_REGISTRY.md is only companion/projection, never another identity/location authority. Common realization law requires explicit adoption across more than one tenant. Ticket lanes minimally include backlog, active and completed. Goals own work-wave truth, tickets own ticket state and comments remain commentary. This member binds locations, while SPEC_METHOD §4/TICKETS select the carrier for a particular work item.

A declared stable cohort may select an exact `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` suffix
instead of the RC-profile suffix. Its contract names the complete required
Product and component set, current-source relationships and qualification
obligations. The historical RC-profile member set above does not limit an
explicitly selected successor cohort. Product identity and independent
third-party version pins remain distinct from the shared cohort version.

When a native package must include its derived documentation, tools or proof
views, construction first freezes the exact semantic source independently of
those generated bytes. The source record inventories every authoritative
member and native contract, classifies derived routes, and names all generated
exclusions with their owners. No authoritative source may be excluded merely
to make a digest agree. Derived candidates bind that source record, its exact
member digests and the intended cut URI. Generated frames remain projections
of their exact owners, not independent semantic authorities (P3, P5, P6).

All required installed assets are built and qualified before the native cut
is frozen. After its annotated tag and installed manifest exist, an external
cohort record binds the source freeze, complete native cut and every derived
Product subject without modifying embedded payload bytes. No asset must
embed its own containing manifest's digest. Source drift invalidates affected
derivations; generation may add only the declared auxiliary bytes. This
source-freeze construction preserves the same exact-subject, complete-ref,
atomic publication and public verification obligations below (P3, P4b, P5).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FSource%20freeze%20and%20stable%20cohort%20construction","start_line":592},{"end_line":691,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Qualification and recovery

Prepublication content qualification binds the exact commit-A STDO tag
and manifest, commit-B source tree, all Product-local target refs, version
markers, Product member inventories, semantic-index bytes and complete
source-corpus digest closure. It proves that the frozen candidate can be
tagged without changing a qualifying byte. After tag and mutable ref
creation, local-ref-graph qualification binds their annotated objects,
peels, target commits, exact push set, and every fetched remote expected
object ID or required absence to that unchanged content result.
Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation from remote refs
and refuses a partial cohort (P6, P3, P5).

A historically published source cut may be the basis of a later
same-version backfill only when separately authorised recovery law names
that exception. Every recovered asset still binds the exact historical cut
and same cut name, and remote completeness remains mandatory. Recovery
cannot move the historical tag, add bytes to its Product subject, or be
represented as an atomic cohort that existed at the original publication.
Normal successor publication uses the atomic cohort process above (P3,
P6).

Adding or changing this cohort law changes qualifying bytes of this
member. It governs only an immutable successor that contains those bytes
and cannot retroactively make an earlier cut a coordinated cohort (P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FQualification%20and%20recovery","start_line":667}],"statement":"Content qualification binds exact A source/native identity, B binding source tree, all Product target refs/version markers/inventories/index bytes/full source closure, and establishes that tagging changes no qualifying bytes. Local-ref qualification binds annotated objects, peels, targets and complete expected push set to the unchanged content result. Post-publication verifies the same relation remotely and refuses partial cohort. Historical backfill preserves exact old cut/name and complete remote set, without moving tags, adding Product bytes or claiming original atomic existence. New cohort law governs only an exact successor cut containing it; stable-v1 uses the source-freeze/native-A/external-B sequence and its own immutable version, while RC profiles retain their higher-ordinal rule.","uncertainty":"No separate recovery law is supplied."},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Content qualification binds exact A source/native identity, B binding source tree, all Product target refs/version markers/inventories/index bytes/full source closure, and establishes that tagging changes no qualifying bytes. Local-ref qualification binds annotated objects, peels, targets and complete expected push set to the unchanged content result. Post-publication verifies the same relation remotely and refuses partial cohort. An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their
material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the
acquired views that project it follow
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)
and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable
positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),
including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection
that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows
[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and
[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;
these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

Purpose and material relation of the assurance relations: they connect
construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared
errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining
evidence whose applicability is established (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FFormal%20representation","start_line":1463},{"end_line":153,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Qualified references

For this fixture a complete assessed record carries subject, basis,
standing, producer, obligation/version, authority and invalidators. Exact
local keys `report:S`, `report:F`, `report:I` resolve those records. An
independent copy preserves all required fields and the preceding policy
readout. The pointer `candidate-v1` alone maps every report to the same
bytes/identity; S and I then require different continuations, falsifying
its sufficiency for that consumer. Adding a type name alone cannot repair
missing standing.

The acquisition model takes three report keys and the explicit booleans
accessible, target-present and basis-current. Its complete eight-row oracle
per key is: all four inaccessible cases return `inaccessible`; of the four
accessible cases, both absent-target cases return `missing`, the present but
old-basis case returns `stale`, and only the present/current case returns the
qualified record as `resolved`. This yields 24 tested cells. Unavailable,
missing and stale targets yield no usable record and keep the dependent
sufficiency claim unsupported; their actual gap, invalidation, refusal or
residual follows the consuming operation's owner, not a universal result
mapping added by this fixture. The executable also checks that resolution
does not mutate the record store and that valid readouts survive.

These access flags and version comparisons model an acquisition boundary;
they are not observed filesystem, transport or human-handover behavior.
The currentness test covers the declared basis-version invalidator only.
Other material invalidators require their own scoped evidence. Logical review
checks the human handover and required residual meanings; actual use remains
unperformed. A hash-based realization would additionally state its collision,
authenticity and access assumptions; no digest alone proves semantic
sufficiency. A manual document reference and a mixed handover can use the
same record and policy without any annotation architecture or event log.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FQualified%20references","start_line":122}],"statement":"Retain every material distinction needed by lawful continuations and readouts, including exact subject/basis, assessment standing, producer, obligation version, authority and invalidators. AC-007 owns hold/gap/two refusal values, core mappings and causes; traversal-specific refinements retain parent core values. Internal consumer summaries state: defects against five closed populations refuse as falsified structural constraints; basis mismatch in model validation/structural admission carries refuse_invalid_basis; application_of targets exact application seed, corrects_event does not erase, missing seed retains hold; invokes_effect requires exact operation grant and authorized_by checks kind/target/territory; unauthorized/stale effect_readiness never dispatches; identity_depends_on and causal occurrence/event graphs are acyclic admitted cause; event_for follows declared scope law, frontier_contains is complete under one exact basis, projects_frontier binds one unchanged frontier. Named residuals include unresolved_cause, unresolved_scope, competing_lineage and stale_frontier. Not every framework event belongs to an occurrence. Representative examples/checkers are neither engines nor semantic authority. No other member applies this profile's rules; an adopting Product does. Consumers add no decisions beyond owning rules.

The examples' reads are their arguments, their model state is explicit, and
their only returned effects are values. Their functions read no clock,
filesystem or mutable global state. The executable harness prints a report;
that reporting effect is outside the modeled functions. The finite bounds
below prove termination independently of observing a successful run.

| Exact traversal | Domain, permission and termination | Complete oracle |
|---|---|---|
| `v_double` | `n∈{0,1,2}`; construction-only grant; one multiplication | Return respectively `{n:0,double:0}`, `{n:1,double:2}`, `{n:2,double:4}`. The value's availability grants no assessment, admission or closure. |
| `v_sorted_full` | Lists of length at most three over `{0,1,2}`; unchanged-subject evaluation; at most two adjacent comparisons | Satisfied iff all adjacent pairs are nondecreasing. Otherwise falsified with the first inversion `{index,left,right}`. `[2,1]` gives `{index:0,left:2,right:1}`. Return a separate witness; an optional witness-log grant may persist it without changing the subject. |
| `v_put_A` | Explicit modeled state `absent/A/B` and grant `allow/deny`; one table lookup | The six cells below specify the returned next state and request/refusal. No physical write is executed. |

| Input state | Allow: next state / decision | Deny: next state / decision |
|---|---|---|
| absent | A / request put_A | absent / refusal |
| A | A / request put_A | A / refusal |
| B | A / request put_A | B / refusal |

The request is a modeled effect proposal, not physical completion. A
denial's evaluated predicate is “this request is authorized”; the table and
code's `refusal` denotes the cause-qualified `permission_denied` signature
stop, which maps to falsified. Unknown physical
completion belongs to the actual effect owner's contract. Likewise, under
a construction-only grant, `v_double(2)` establishes candidate availability
only; a separate judgment, admission or closure claim has no supporting
operation or evidence.

Negative evaluation case: sorting `[2,1]` in place and then calling it an
assessment of the original violates the unchanged-subject profile. The
changed list may be a construction output under a construction grant; its
sortedness is not the original list's sortedness. The executable shows the
mutation and opposite original/successor sortedness results; logical review
applies the evaluation profile to reject the false attribution. Manual
evaluation and mixed human/software witness logging have the same permission
boundary. The script does not implement an authorization or log-admission
mechanism, so it makes no executable claim about that boundary.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FOperations%20and%20permissions","start_line":17}],"statement":"v_double constructs a candidate over n∈{0,1,2}; sorted_full evaluates lists of length at most three over {0,1,2} with at most two adjacent comparisons and retains an inversion witness; in-place sorting is a different construction. put_A uses explicit absent/A/B state and allow/deny input, returns a next-state proposal and has no implicit physical effect. Missing operation permission remains distinct from successful computation. The finite domains and outcome counts scope each check.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Pending review alone does not prohibit a granted landing; required review still holds the closure or release claim that depends on it.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":387,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md","quote":"### Landing, closure and release

Landing makes an exact candidate available at an authorized checkpoint or
integration destination. It is an operation under its existing grant, not
acceptance of the candidate's claims. Work closure applies the stated closing
condition; release applies the separately selected publication and acceptance
conditions of [RELEASE](RELEASE.md). Record these as separate decisions (P6,
P3).

Review supplies QA evidence for those decisions. A pending review does not by
itself hold landing: an admitted candidate may land after its bounded work
and fix pass, while review of that exact candidate runs beside subsequent
authorized work. A required review holds the closure or acceptance claim that
depends on its complete report. A governing landing condition, applicable hard
stop or missing operation authority still prevents landing; availability is
no waiver. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks)
binds the optional profile's repair/recheck cadence (P6, P2).

Permitted downstream work may consume a landed candidate before its review
reports, carrying its exact identity, unresolved conditions and dependency
links. This is provisional use, not admitted truth. A later material finding
invalidates the affected dependent results under
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); unrelated valid results
remain reusable. Repair and re-evaluation follow those dependencies before
further reliance (P4b, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F5.%20Acceptance%2FLanding%2C%20closure%20and%20release","start_line":363}],"label":"Landing, work closure and release"}}}
