Existing RC lines retain RC branches and ordinal selectors; stable-v1 uses a fresh major.minor.patch immutable cut with explicit profile marker. Release identity is distinct from object identity, source revision, mutable discovery and consumer adoption.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":169,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"## 2. Release identities

The release-publication context distinguishes (P3):

- Project Release Namespace: a stable repository-local key assigned by
  the Product release authority to one independently released source
  project;
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;
- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable
  source-project state constructing a possible successor;
- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current
  candidate window;
- Immutable Release Cut: an annotated project-qualified Git tag plus its
  exact Product release subject (FOUNDATIONS §2), under the selected RC or
  stable profile; publication, qualification and acceptance retain their
  respective meanings; it realises the release cut;
- Version-Line Selector: the mutable project-qualified tag alias naming
  the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and
  version line; it realises the version-line selector of FOUNDATIONS §2;
  and
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable release tag never moves (P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities","start_line":144},{"end_line":204,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Project-qualified Git refs

`<project>` is one explicit Project Release Namespace. It matches
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line. It is
assigned by the Product release authority. A directory name, display name,
definition label, package name or matching version cannot infer or
reassign it (P3, P6).

A shared release source uses these exact ref shapes for an RC-profile
publication (P3):

```text
RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>
immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>
version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>
release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>
```

The short Git tag names are therefore `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` and
`<project>/v<version>`. A shared release source does not publish a future
cut or selector under the unqualified `v<version>-rc.<n>` or `v<version>`
refs (P3).

A single-project release source may retain the unqualified ref profile
only while it has exactly one independently released project and its
release record declares that profile. Adding a second independently
released project requires project-qualified refs before either project
publishes another cut (P3).

For the Specification Stack shared source, the allocated namespaces are
`specification_methodology`, `axiom_indexer` and `stdo_representation`.
These keys distinguish release refs; they do not merge the three Products
or imply a dependency or composition relation (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities%2FProject-qualified%20Git%20refs","start_line":171},{"end_line":272,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Project-subtree release identity

In a shared release source, an immutable cut binds all of (P3):

- the Project Release Namespace and owning Product authority;
- the exact qualified Git ref and annotated tag object;
- the peeled commit and repository-root tree;
- the normalised repository-relative Project Subtree root at that commit;
- the Git tree object at that exact Project Subtree root;
- the declared Product member inventory and release-scoped claim bytes;
  and
- the predecessor and successor dispositions required by §9.

The Project Subtree root is a locator inside the exact peeled commit, not
Product identity. Its canonical spelling is the slash-separated Git path
from the repository root, with no leading or trailing slash and no empty,
`.` or `..` component; `.` alone denotes the repository root. Each
non-root component names the exact tree entry bytes traversed at that
commit. Moving a source project changes this locator and its cut identity
without reassigning the Project Release Namespace. If the source project
occupies the repository root, its project-subtree tree equals the
repository-root tree (P3).

A tag over a monorepo commit does not make sibling subtrees Product
members. Unrelated sibling bytes remain carrier state outside the declared
Product subject. Conversely, a member inventory or payload digest without
the qualified ref, commit, Project Subtree root and Project Subtree tree is
not a complete reacquirable release identity (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities%2FProject-subtree%20release%20identity","start_line":245}],"label":"Immutable release cut identity"}}}

Release identity is distinct from object identity, source revision, mutable discovery and consumer adoption.

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:abc877141275aeedee9cb23f37d83ed6"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:225cc175cf584eef5d5d3da8821bf6a7","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":95,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/HOST_BINDING.md","quote":"## Claude: Explicit Session Tool Policy

Claude's documented `PreToolUse` event can deny a tool call before it runs.
The bundled [claude_tool_gate.py](../scripts/claude_tool_gate.py) consumes a
Product-owned, digest-pinned policy of this form:

```json
{
  "kind": "stdo.claude-tool-policy",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "policy_id": "<exact policy identity>",
  "authority_ref": "<existing grant identity and source route>",
  "cwd": "<canonical absolute worksite>",
  "read_paths": ["<canonical absolute permitted control file>"],
  "bash_commands": ["<complete exact permitted command string>"],
  "skills": ["spec:stdo-work"]
}
```

The operation owner supplies the approved reads/commands and checks their
outputs against the actor's acquisition boundary. The adapter does not parse
shell syntax or infer what a command may do. No wildcards apply. A changed
command, unlisted path/skill, redirected path, changed cwd, unknown tool/event,
unsupported parameters, changed policy digest or failed check is denied.
Read ranges may narrow an approved file. Skill calls accept the selected name
without added arguments. Background execution and permission overrides are
unsupported. A trusted allowed command's internal reads, effects and outputs
remain that command's contract; exact string equality does not prove them.

Select the policy and optional audit path through an authorized session
binding. Do not edit global host settings. A session settings fragment is:

```json
{
  "autoMemoryEnabled": false,
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": ".*",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "<absolute Python executable>",
        "args": ["<absolute plugin>/scripts/claude_tool_gate.py", "--policy", "<absolute policy>", "--policy-sha256", "<policy sha256>", "--audit", "<authorized JSONL result path>"],
        "timeout": 10,
        "onFailure": "block"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

The audit option is an explicit append effect; omit it without that grant.
It records decision, policy identity, tool identity and event digest, without
copying tool output. Failure to append when selected denies the tool call.
Keep the policy, adapter and any command implementation outside the actor's
write grant. Register the hook for every tool, with failure blocking selected;
otherwise a crash, timeout or unmatched tool could bypass the intended gate.

Bind the available tool roster to `Read,Skill,Bash` for the supported policy
surface, the explicit plugin root, selected worksite and exact session settings.
With `--restricted`, `--plugin-dir` loads the skill but does not itself make its
shared references readable outside the worksite. Bind `--add-dir` to that exact
already-admitted plugin root as well. If a required direct owner-file read is
outside the worksite, bind only its already-admitted directory or use the
approved source-reader command; do not add a parent, home or whole fixture
tree. These host directory capabilities do not enlarge the business grant:
the gate still admits only its exact policy paths/commands. Expose the selected
directories, policy identity and concrete allowed source-reader/catalog calls
in the actor's authorized session control metadata.

The observed CLI supports session `--plugin-dir`, `--tools`, `--settings`,
`--restricted`, `--add-dir`, `--strict-mcp-config` and `--no-session-persistence`; verify
those capabilities on the selected host before depending on them. Use the
already-selected actor/model. An allow list plus `dontAsk` alone does not
confine built-in read-only shell commands, so it is not this gate's substitute.

This covers the hooked tool calls. It does **not** control existing context,
system/managed instructions, native file mentions expanded before a tool call,
or a permitted program's internal acquisition. The run binding must account
for these routes; in a tool-confined trial, supply no unselected file mentions
and admit the actual plugin/control inputs. If the required claim excludes
unmeasured host context, that claim is unsupported by this adapter. A failed
or denied attempt is not a successful acquisition or completed work result.

Documented interface: [Claude hook reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks),
[CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) and
[memory controls](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory). Session controls were
inspected on Claude Code 2.1.306; actual qualification binds its exact retained run.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/HOST_BINDING.md#Bind%20The%20Actual%20Host%2FClaude%3A%20Explicit%20Session%20Tool%20Policy","start_line":9},{"end_line":7,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/HOST_BINDING.md","quote":"# Bind The Actual Host

The Product supplies the actor's required context/acquisition boundary and
operation grant. Bind the actual session to it before dependent work. These
adapters project an already-authorized policy; they create no admission and
are optional when a Product already selects sufficient tools. Use those
declared tools rather than installing a competing mechanism.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/HOST_BINDING.md#Bind%20The%20Actual%20Host","start_line":1},{"end_line":279,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Host Binding

For a strict selected tool-acquisition boundary, use the concrete
[host adapter and its limits](HOST_BINDING.md). Do not assume the ordinary
host permission prompt or a fresh actor supplies that boundary.

Use the host's actually available delegation or separate-session mechanism.
Record the selected actor/model where exposed, worksite, supplied packet,
inherited history/instructions, available tool/permission settings and return
channel. Respect the admitted context/resource envelope. Unknown required
properties withhold dispatch; optional unobserved properties are explicit
limits. Tool availability alone grants no operation.

- **Codex:** inspect the exposed delegation/session controls. Where the host
  offers conversation inheritance or forking, choose a packet-only context
  when the frame requires it and bind any other automatically supplied
  instructions. A resumed actor retains its earlier context; use it only
  when that context is permitted. Return and wait through the actual actor
  identity, not an invented worker name. If this host has no suitable
  delegation mechanism, return the prepared packet without claiming dispatch.
- **Claude:** select the available subagent/session mechanism and inspect the
  selected agent definition, inherited instructions, tool permissions and
  worksite. Supply the packet and target skill explicitly. A subagent label
  or a resumed session does not establish a clean context. Return through
  the actual task/result mechanism; if its properties cannot meet a required
  boundary, return the unsupported activation rather than silently executing
  in the issuer's context.

Neither host's fresh context alone proves information-flow enforcement or
independent assessment. Independence additionally uses `EVALUATION` §3's
authorship and evidence conditions and the Product's actor-family policy.
Do not broaden permissions, change host configuration or install a runtime
to make a dispatch work without the existing authority for those effects.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FHost%20Binding","start_line":247}],"statement":"The Product supplies the required acquisition boundary and grant. Use already-selected Product tools when they sufficiently realize that boundary; the host adapters are optional in that case and do not justify installing a competing mechanism. For a selected strict tool-acquisition boundary that uses the Claude adapter, bind its explicit session tool policy and hook, actual allowed control/read commands, roots and output behavior. Disable or constrain alternate tools and channels that bypass that selected policy; validate the actual policy/hook/session result rather than infer isolation from a subagent label or ordinary permission prompt. A direct admitted Claude task whose selected Product tools suffice and whose boundary is not strict does not require this adapter. The adapter covers hooked calls, not inherited or previously acquired context, arbitrary information-flow noninterference or semantic independence.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Use already-selected Product tools when they sufficiently realize that boundary; the host adapters are optional in that case and do not justify installing a competing mechanism. For a selected strict tool-acquisition boundary that uses the Claude adapter, bind its explicit session tool policy and hook, actual allowed control/read commands, roots and output behavior. Disable or constrain alternate tools and channels that bypass that selected policy; validate the actual policy/hook/session result rather than infer isolation from a subagent label or ordinary permission prompt. A direct admitted Claude task whose selected Product tools suffice and whose boundary is not strict does not require this adapter. The adapter covers hooked calls, not inherited or previously acquired context, arbitrary information-flow noninterference or semantic independence.

Before reuse classify every inherited module/interface/carrier/projection/proof surface: carry_across is materially unchanged and intentionally adopted, redundant no longer needed, rewrite needed but rebuilt; unclassified implementation is a defect. Declare new line, establish fresh method/goals/intent/product/requirements/design, remove ambient old-line authority, classify constitutional material adopted/superseded/deferred/orphaned, copy only intentionally retained material, and re-derive from new truth. A model `M_b` is a valid model of `a_c` under signature `Sigma`, written
`M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma]`, only when (P6, P1):

1. `Sigma` and the exact `a_c` basis resolve;
2. every record satisfies AC-001 through AC-009;

   and composition satisfies its applicable law, and every claimed functor
   application satisfies AC-015 and its bound kind's §5 contract;
4. interpretation fidelity and residual dispositions bind the exact
   subject;
5. structural evaluation and semantic acceptance remain distinct and both
   required where claimed; and
6. all evidence, provenance, invalidation and re-entry coordinates
   resolve.

the semantic or authority subset unless the model supplies an exact lawful
decision contract for it (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F6.%20Interpretation%20and%20models%2FAC-019%20Valid%20model","start_line":1170}],"label":"Valid-model obligations"}}}

{"family":"relations","record":{"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:27518e1529eab354d8d92a4a7054b6ab","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:relation-kind:governing:requires","owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","qualifiers":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":131,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Issue

1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
   execution contract for every question.
2. **Project the admitted unit.** The packet is a reference/verbatim projection
   of that unit, not a rewritten operating procedure. Use the compact bindings
   below or their equivalent in the existing carrier. Each binding points to
   an exact admitted source clause; any inlined grant or condition is quoted
   verbatim with its origin. The recipient applies the same skill to those
   bindings. Do not rewrite the skill or derive a new decision algorithm.

   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
   |---|---|
   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
   | Unresolved required binding | Missing source, verification or capability; return its cause and required re-entry instead of an executable packet |

   Preserve conditional grants as conditions. Do not add inferred conditionals,
   read/effect grants, retry permissions or closure rules. An effect grant alone
   does not grant acquisition of its output. For example, project these as
   separate existing clauses, without filling a missing clause by inference:

   ```text
   Effect and its condition: <exact admitted clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Output acquisition: <exact permitted output clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Retry / result / stop: <exact admitted clause references or verbatim quotes>
   ```

   Put any proposed new interpretation outside the execution packet and return
   for its required re-entry. Calling it a derivation or a safety rule does not
   make it an inherited grant.

   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence
   tools, use those contracts and retain their actual receipts. Do not replace
   required computation with a hand-written claim or invent tool success. A
   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces
   source/semantic judgment. Tooling availability creates no new dependency.
3. **Check the acquisition the packet prescribes.** Consider command output,
   diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded context as well as direct reads.
   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames
   that command prints is a contradiction. Resolve it before dispatch using
   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.
4. **Bind the host and dispatch.** Apply [Host Binding](#host-binding) and send
   the packet to the selected actor with the instruction to invoke this same
   skill as its recipient. Do not transfer ambient conversation by default
   where the frame excludes it. Record the dispatch/activation identity and
   actual mechanism in the existing carrier through its authorized Writer.
   If no available authorized mechanism meets the required boundary, retain
   the packet and return “not dispatched” with the missing capability. A
   prepared packet is not an active Worker or a work result.

Keep packet readiness separate from returning a response. If a required
control/source verification or capability is unavailable, return the missing
binding and the applicable incomplete/refused outcome; do not issue an
executable intake or label it ready, complete or closed. “Prepared, not
dispatched” applies only when the packet is sufficient and dispatch remains
unperformed; its consumer still checks the exact intake before using it.

The issuer remains in its coordinating frame. It acquires no mutation grant
by arranging the work. Where one same-actor role transition is sufficient and
permitted, bind and record that transition explicitly; do not pretend it
cleared information already acquired (`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §6 and §17).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FIssue","start_line":49},{"end_line":279,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Host Binding

For a strict selected tool-acquisition boundary, use the concrete
[host adapter and its limits](HOST_BINDING.md). Do not assume the ordinary
host permission prompt or a fresh actor supplies that boundary.

Use the host's actually available delegation or separate-session mechanism.
Record the selected actor/model where exposed, worksite, supplied packet,
inherited history/instructions, available tool/permission settings and return
channel. Respect the admitted context/resource envelope. Unknown required
properties withhold dispatch; optional unobserved properties are explicit
limits. Tool availability alone grants no operation.

- **Codex:** inspect the exposed delegation/session controls. Where the host
  offers conversation inheritance or forking, choose a packet-only context
  when the frame requires it and bind any other automatically supplied
  instructions. A resumed actor retains its earlier context; use it only
  when that context is permitted. Return and wait through the actual actor
  identity, not an invented worker name. If this host has no suitable
  delegation mechanism, return the prepared packet without claiming dispatch.
- **Claude:** select the available subagent/session mechanism and inspect the
  selected agent definition, inherited instructions, tool permissions and
  worksite. Supply the packet and target skill explicitly. A subagent label
  or a resumed session does not establish a clean context. Return through
  the actual task/result mechanism; if its properties cannot meet a required
  boundary, return the unsupported activation rather than silently executing
  in the issuer's context.

Neither host's fresh context alone proves information-flow enforcement or
independent assessment. Independence additionally uses `EVALUATION` §3's
authorship and evidence conditions and the Product's actor-family policy.
Do not broaden permissions, change host configuration or install a runtime
to make a dispatch work without the existing authority for those effects.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FHost%20Binding","start_line":247}],"kind":"requires","meaning":"Dispatch of an admitted packet requires the actual host to satisfy every required acquisition and capability boundary."},"scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"],"source":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:7273eee8de3f5344e030eac0d2fd8c38","target":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:abc877141275aeedee9cb23f37d83ed6"}}

If tested, use named cases with known governing relations/expected decisions and withhold conversational/folk-memory aids.

Graph-execution alignment and escalation

When this profile is used inside a product governed by the graph-execution
profile (PROFILES §2), reviewers first ask whether the boundary is an
operative graph traversal (P6, P0). If the boundary represents product
movement from one typed asset state to another, the governing shape is:

1. outcome traversal under the graph-execution profile;
2. the declarative graph carrier structure (GTL and ABG in that profile's
   terms); and
3. deterministic module realisation under this profile.

This profile may govern evaluators and proofs, carrier constructors
and admissions, deterministic transforms inside an edge traversal, effect
shells that publish the traversal result, and projections over
already-admitted carrier truth. It is not used to hide graph functions
inside service methods, edge-traversal semantics inside module
orchestration, continuation or re-entry decisions inside deterministic
controllers, semantic target movement inside constructors, materialisers
or projections, or probabilistic worker boundaries inside imperative
prompt or dispatch code (P0 boundary commitment, P6).

That governance scope does not depend on F_D eligibility. An operation
claiming common `F_D` additionally meets
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds),
with its unchanged-subject profile when it evaluates that subject. The
kind's authority boundary is owned there, not by this profile. A
deterministic transform or effect shell is not automatically
qualified as total deterministic processing, and a modeled effect request
does not establish completion. Existing helpers use the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration), preserving
their original domain and permissions until the successor claim is established.

If a deterministic module appears to own what work is next, what target is
being moved to, what closes the traversal or what graph function is being
performed, the boundary should be repriced against the graph-execution
profile before claiming design-method closure. In such products the module
boundary is a realisation cut inside the graph program; it is not the
program (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F2.%20Graph-execution%20alignment%20and%20escalation","start_line":270}],"label":"Deterministic module boundary"}}}

For this example, the relevant source owners grant these separate uses:

| Relation / actor | Permitted acquisition or export | Exclusion |
|---|---|---|
| A → B report use | B's result, public contract and declared evidence coordinates | No direct acquisition of C's implementation through B |
| B → C decoder use | C's interface and returned exact rows | No onward disclosure of C's private donor implementation |
| A → D report use | Selected AUD basis and its provenance | Other currency internals/administrative records |
| B → D subtotal use | Selected AUD basis and evidence needed for B's unit check | A cannot borrow any wider B-specific grant |
| C construction Worker | C's required behavior, eligible examples and its own new candidate | Forbidden donor implementation H and algorithm summaries derived from H |
| C nonauthor Reviewer | Governing sources first; candidate/proof, plus H for an explicitly authorized comparison | No permission to forward H or its algorithm into Worker context |

The D acquisition can be deduplicated as bytes only if its separate uses retain
purpose, authority and applicability coordinates. Reaching D by two routes does
not merge their permissions. The named owners and synthetic grants above are
premises of the example, not real grants conferred by this file.

Three acquisitions discriminate permission, information eligibility and exposure:

1. Worker asks for `H/source.py`: denied by its information policy and access grant.
2. B returns an otherwise permitted `notes.md` containing a summary of H's internal
   parsing algorithm. The file's location and B's read permission do not establish
   authorized onward disclosure or clean-room eligibility. Delivery is refused;
   if already delivered, the affected clean-room claim is held and exposure is
   retained. Merely deleting `notes.md` cannot restore the same actor's standing.
3. H's owner separately approves export E containing a behavioral CSV contract and
   public input/output examples. The engagement's declared policy explicitly
   permits this class of exported behavioral specification, including its recorded
   derivation; a named assessment establishes E contains no excluded implementation
   detail. The actor's grant permits E and the actual delivered digest is recorded.
   E may then be used. Owner approval alone is insufficient: under a policy that
   excludes all H-derived information, E must still be refused.

A tool process may execute an authorized decoder without delivering its source to
the Worker. Its returned text, diagnostics, caches and retrieval results remain
subject to the same information policy. Unrestricted shell/search/network access
would bypass a mediated acquisition boundary. Receipts for three permitted calls
cannot prove that such a bypass never occurred; any isolation claim binds the
actual host restrictions and prior-exposure limits.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md#Recursive%20Product%20composition%20example%2FAuthority%20and%20information%20across%20depth%20and%20sharing","start_line":64},{"end_line":122,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md","quote":"## Context adequacy and continuation

Fix Γ to the AUD task, one selected actor/grant, these contracts, the same input,
and the decision rule: emit only with current applicable evidence of the basis
join; otherwise hold for reassessment. Both states contain the identical candidate
`AUD 3.50`:

| State | Relevant retained fact | Required continuation |
|---|---|---|
| s1 | Exact join evidence is applicable; no outstanding basis obligation | Emit within the existing grant |
| s2 | An observed basis change makes join applicability unresolved; reassessment is owed | Hold; acquire/reassess the changed condition |

Projection `alpha0(s) = candidate bytes` maps s1 and s2 to the same value and cannot
preserve the required decision. `alpha1` retains the candidate, dependency/basis
identities, applicability, open obligation and the fixed decision contract; it
separates these cases and supports their stated continuations. Source permission
is identical in both states. This is a scoped sufficiency witness, not an optimal
compression result or proof that those fields suffice for arbitrary future work.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md#Recursive%20Product%20composition%20example%2FContext%20adequacy%20and%20continuation","start_line":105}],"statement":"A’s relation to B does not disclose C or transfer B’s C grant; shared D routes keep independent purposes and no union of permissions. {"family":"relations","record":{"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:294282fbcecc6dec9efba3d79ed0ef56","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:relation-kind:governing:requires","owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","qualifiers":{"conditions":["The task is issued or received through a handoff."],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":47,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Control Intake

This is the first path for **issuer, recipient and direct work**. The issuer's
access is its own grant, not the Worker's. A coordinator cannot inspect the
subject merely because its Worker may do so.

1. Read the exact own contract/intake named in the request first. Bind its
   role, allowed control inputs, excluded information, operations and return
   route. Do not begin with directory listings, recursive discovery, memory
   search or neighbouring files. If the request supplies only a packet, its
   authorized control routes are the initial limit; check them against their
   authoritative grant before dependent acquisition. If no exact control
   route is supplied, use only the request's authorized discovery boundary;
   an unresolved boundary returns for clarification rather than being guessed.
2. Read the named Product Definition, accepted frame basis and applicable
   grant/admission through those control routes. An exact definition path
   removes the need to inventory surrounding directories. Verify it with the
   [compact source reader](#compact-source-acquisition) or the already-declared
   equivalent tool; do not print the manager's complete member inventory into
   the actor context. Retain the actual verification identity/result.
3. Check the active host binding before relying on an acquisition exclusion:
   what context is already supplied, which tools and scopes are actually
   enabled, how new reads are confined or supervised, and how results return.
   Use exposed capabilities and the admitted run binding, not exploration of
   home/configuration files. A fresh session is not a read boundary. If the
   required capability is absent, unknown or already violated, stop the
   dependent activation with its cause; do not claim a clean frame and
   continue. The [host binding](#host-binding) states the specific limits.
4. Enter only the branch required by that bound role. Issuer follows Issue;
   recipient follows Receive; a sufficient direct task uses the ordinary
   skill. Read additional sources only for a material question and through
   the admitted routes. The skill's general workflow never widens this intake.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FControl%20Intake","start_line":16},{"end_line":131,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Issue

1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
   execution contract for every question.
2. **Project the admitted unit.** The packet is a reference/verbatim projection
   of that unit, not a rewritten operating procedure. Use the compact bindings
   below or their equivalent in the existing carrier. Each binding points to
   an exact admitted source clause; any inlined grant or condition is quoted
   verbatim with its origin. The recipient applies the same skill to those
   bindings. Do not rewrite the skill or derive a new decision algorithm.

   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
   |---|---|
   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
   | Unresolved required binding | Missing source, verification or capability; return its cause and required re-entry instead of an executable packet |

   Preserve conditional grants as conditions. Do not add inferred conditionals,
   read/effect grants, retry permissions or closure rules. An effect grant alone
   does not grant acquisition of its output. For example, project these as
   separate existing clauses, without filling a missing clause by inference:

   ```text
   Effect and its condition: <exact admitted clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Output acquisition: <exact permitted output clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Retry / result / stop: <exact admitted clause references or verbatim quotes>
   ```

   Put any proposed new interpretation outside the execution packet and return
   for its required re-entry. Calling it a derivation or a safety rule does not
   make it an inherited grant.

   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence
   tools, use those contracts and retain their actual receipts. Do not replace
   required computation with a hand-written claim or invent tool success. A
   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces
   source/semantic judgment. Tooling availability creates no new dependency.
3. **Check the acquisition the packet prescribes.** Consider command output,
   diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded context as well as direct reads.
   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames
   that command prints is a contradiction. Resolve it before dispatch using
   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.
4. **Bind the host and dispatch.** Apply [Host Binding](#host-binding) and send
   the packet to the selected actor with the instruction to invoke this same
   skill as its recipient. Do not transfer ambient conversation by default
   where the frame excludes it. Record the dispatch/activation identity and
   actual mechanism in the existing carrier through its authorized Writer.
   If no available authorized mechanism meets the required boundary, retain
   the packet and return “not dispatched” with the missing capability. A
   prepared packet is not an active Worker or a work result.

Keep packet readiness separate from returning a response. If a required
control/source verification or capability is unavailable, return the missing
binding and the applicable incomplete/refused outcome; do not issue an
executable intake or label it ready, complete or closed. “Prepared, not
dispatched” applies only when the packet is sufficient and dispatch remains
unperformed; its consumer still checks the exact intake before using it.

The issuer remains in its coordinating frame. It acquires no mutation grant

The example separates component contracts, material joins, scoped refinement, per-edge eligibility, currentness and execution readiness.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":3,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md","quote":"# Recursive Product composition example

This finite worked example applies [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §9](../PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#product-composition-contract). Its synthetic contracts and expected deductions are not installed Products or executed qualification evidence (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md#Recursive%20Product%20composition%20example","start_line":1},{"end_line":41,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md","quote":"## Boundaries and concrete contracts

The declared decomposition contains A (Invoice report), B (Subtotal), C (Line
decoder) and D (Currency basis). A consumes B and D; B consumes C and D. C and D
are leaves in this view. D is one shared Product, not a copied child with two
identities. A can be consumed by a still larger Product using the same laws.

```mermaid
graph TD
  A["A: Invoice report"] --> B["B: Subtotal"]
  A --> D["D: Currency basis"]
  B --> C["C: Line decoder"]
  B --> D
```

| Product | Contract at the selected cut | Independently decidable local predicate |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | `decode(text)` returns exact rows `(quantity, unit_minor, currency)` or a defined parse refusal. Input has one comma-separated triple per line, nonnegative integer quantities/prices and a currency token. No rounding or unit conversion. | Parsed fields equal the input fields; malformed or fractional integers refuse. |
| D1 | `basis(currency)` returns an admitted minor-unit exponent: `AUD → 2`; unknown currency refuses. The contract states the units, not just a numeric lookup. | The returned basis matches this selected currency contract. |
| B1 | Uses C1 and D1 to return `amount_minor = Σ quantity × unit_minor`, currency, exponent and exact dependency/evidence coordinates. Mixed currencies refuse. | Sum and units are correct for the original decoded rows and selected basis. |
| A1 | Uses B1 and D1 to render the amount with its currency; verifies matching basis and applicability before emission. | The displayed monetary amount equals the input's monetary amount under the declared currency basis. |

For finite evaluation here, there are at most 100 rows; quantities are 0–100,
prices are 0–1,000,000 minor units, currency is AUD, and integer arithmetic is exact.
Changing those conditions requires a new scoped claim. Operational contracts also
retain each error rather than returning a fabricated amount.

Input `2,125,AUD\n1,100,AUD` yields C1 rows `(2,125,AUD),(1,100,AUD)`, D1 exponent 2,
B1 amount 350 minor units and A1 display `AUD 3.50`. B is entered directly with its
own definition/frame and declared C1/D1 capability closure; A and A's frame are
unneeded. C can likewise be constructed/evaluated from its own contract and test
inputs without B. The surrounding orchestration is optional to those claims.

If C later implements its decoder using an internal parser or further Products,
B need not acquire all their implementations. C's adequate exported contract can
encapsulate them. Material far-side assumptions or evidence needed for B's claim
must still be carried or acquired lawfully; silence is not a preservation proof.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md#Recursive%20Product%20composition%20example%2FBoundaries%20and%20concrete%20contracts","start_line":5}],"label":"Recursive invoice composition example"}}}

Landing, closure, release and explicit Product gates have one owner,
[EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#landing-closure-and-release). For this profile,
an admitted step lands its candidate after its selected work and fix pass.
Where review is required or selected, one bounded QA review covers that exact
declared subject and may run beside the next authorized step. It is not a
standing permission for another review of every local change. The Executive
records review size and its reason in the existing work carrier; any ratio is
Product-selected, and none is imposed here (P6, P2).

Sizing does not shrink a declared claim. Preserve the exact evaluated
population and conjunction; a sample supports its stated scope and leaves
uncovered required coverage explicit. A budget or ratio cannot turn that
residual into a completed whole-subject review (P6, P5).

Each test-reproducible repair binds a reproduction that fails on the faulty
subject and passes on the repaired subject, with the full suite declared for
that repair scope passing. A repair without a reproduction states that gap and
requires the independent recheck below; a green total does not fill the gap.
Tests may verify a repair without becoming independent assessment. A fix pass
closes on that evidence and its other applicable conditions unless independent
recheck is required by one of these conditions (P6, P5):

1. the candidate reaches a boundary whose governing basis requires or claims
   independent review, including any Product, release, qualification, risk or
   admitted-work addition;
2. the pass repairs a hard stop or a capture whose source-fidelity claim is
   material to the outcome;
3. a repair has no reproducing test; or
4. a selected review left part of its declared subject uncovered.

For a required recheck, activate one fresh Reviewer for the bounded fix pass,
with its affected claims, prior findings, reproductions and remaining coverage.
Fresh means a new bounded assessment activation with the independence of
EVALUATION §3, not independence inferred from a new context or actor name.
Partitioning follows the declared conjunction, not extra serial rounds. The
covered fixes remain unresolved for the dependent closure claim until that
report arrives and the required predicates are satisfied; tests alone cannot
substitute for this required review. A later material finding is a new input
to the next bounded disposition, not an unbounded review loop (P6, P2).

The Executive preserves Reviewer severity, assigns priority under the selected
policy and hands the linked items to the lawful repair Writer. Pending review
alone holds no landing. An open required review holds its dependent closure,
and release retains all its selected conditions. Downstream use and later
invalidation follow EVALUATION §5; access and artifact-effect grants remain
unchanged (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#EXECUTIVE_BASELINE%2F12.%20Complete%20engagement%20transition%2FQA%20cadence%20and%20repair%20rechecks","start_line":1384}],"label":"Proportionate QA and repair recheck"}}}

clauses.statement: Proportionate QA and repair recheck: A new independent review is selected for its exact claim, subject, coverage and risk under owning conditions, rather than after every edit or by an assumed review ratio.

Installed release manifest schema: Draft 2020-12 schema urn:stdo:schema:installed-release-manifest:1 defines a closed deterministic installed-inventory object with kind, schema_version, release, standards and auxiliary. It admits immutable RC cuts and profile-qualified stable-v1 cuts, with Git object IDs, exact SHA-256 members and source/installed roots.

The design module or ticket must record scope, permitted operations, forbidden or explicitly bounded mutation, visible scaffold/debug label when user-facing, authoritative replacement, retirement condition and owning ticket, and a non-closure condition preventing release while the scaffold remains. An exempt scaffold cannot become production UX by accumulation: retire it, reprice it into governed UX or keep it outside product closure.

The severity convention selected for this review flow is **1 highest to 5
lowest**. The Reviewer grades the consequence of the demonstrated defect if
it manifests, using these qualitative anchors. The Product-owned frame basis
binds the convention and its Product-specific evidence criteria: affected
claims, users/paths, consequence, dependencies and supported containment (P6).

| Severity | Consequence anchor |
|---|---|
| 1 | Critical loss of the governed outcome or of essential safety, authority or integrity across its affected scope. |
| 2 | Major failure of essential behaviour, with substantial affected users, paths or dependencies and no adequate ordinary containment. |
| 3 | Material but bounded failure whose disposition depends on its downstream impact and wider blast radius. |
| 4 | Limited local failure with supported containment or a practical workaround and little effect outside that local scope. |
| 5 | Minor actionable defect with minimal functional consequence for the declared outcome. |

Severity 3 requires an explicit assessment of downstream dependencies and
blast radius. Material impact on dependent work normally calls for repair;
contained local impact may be deferred with a recorded reason and responsible
owner. The Executive makes that disposition from the evidence and its grant,
preserving the Reviewer's grade; a departure from the normal repair response
also records its reason. Unknown dependent impact is not evidence of
containment. Mandatory claims, hard stops and acceptance conditions still
determine boundary effects under EVALUATION §5. Severity 3 is not priority P3,
and no severity value automatically supplies priority, a block or permission
to defer (P6, P2).

An older or alternative Product-selected scale keeps its identity and evidence
criteria. Selecting this convention is explicit; any translation is declared
and justified rather than inferred from matching numbers. Historical findings
retain the scale and grade under which they were assessed. A no-finding result

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:e72647bd59200028152866bc759f1965"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:34acd3909e2bab07ae79cfb64247edc0","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":83,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Exhaustion

`v_copy` accepts lists of length at most two over `{0,1}` and fuel in
`{0,1,2}`. It copies one element per fuel unit; only a complete copy is its
candidate. It terminates after at most two copies. `v_sorted` accepts lists
of length at most three over `{0,1}` and the same fuel. It inspects one
adjacent pair per fuel unit, stopping at the first inversion, when every
pair has been checked, or when fuel ends. It terminates after at most two
comparisons. Its one declared outcome is a closed assessment report containing
the exact input/basis, inspected-pair evidence and any residual; such a
report can carry the `assessment_exhausted` stop with its indeterminate
result. The stop/report is one declared outcome; its availability to an
enclosing step is assessed separately.

| Selected application and observation | Assessed predicate and result | Work result | Signature and traversal stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_copy([0,1],1)` retains prefix `[0]`, with no complete candidate | Complete copy is available: falsified | `incomplete` → falsified for output availability | `copy_exhausted` maps to falsified, cause fuel ended before the required output |
| `v_sorted([0,1,0],1)` inspects `(0,1)`, with the second pair unexamined | Whole list is sorted: indeterminate on admitted inspected-pair evidence | `candidate_ready` → satisfied for the closed report and transition evidence being available only | `assessment_exhausted` maps to indeterminate, cause performed assessment has insufficient evidence |
| An activated assessing step spends its budget in setup and never invokes `v_sorted` | No assessment result | `incomplete` → falsified for the step's own output availability; the unperformed assessment remains residual work | No traversal application exists and therefore no `v_sorted` judgment or stop exists; the enclosing step retains its own stop and cause |

The two declared exhaustion stops have different predicates and parent core
values. Neither maps to satisfied. A report's availability and its assessed
predicate are not one judgment. Lists of length zero or one are sorted
without inspecting a pair. An observed inversion falsifies sortedness even
when later pairs remain unexamined. No result is inferred from a planned
invocation. These are distinct bounded traversals, not totality proofs for
an unbounded operation. The setup-before-invocation row is a logical-review
case under ACTIVATION §3, not a result of the executable example.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FExhaustion","start_line":56},{"end_line":1679,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md","quote":"### Resource limits

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

- Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
  declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
  frame and its owning scope
  ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
  A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
  measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
  No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
- Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
  where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
  outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
  the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
  context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
  the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
  counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
  reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
  selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
  questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
  reported separately.
- Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
  truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
  exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
  reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
  applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
  bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
  ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
  owner of the grant or binding that set it.
- Values. The value of each limit, and the units and boundaries the
  selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
  binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
  one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
  A value is stated before the activation it limits.
- Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
  adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
  invariant (P2, P6).

Purpose and material relation: the configuration (§1), context
construction (§2) and frame qualification
([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource
limits, so the law for declaring, measuring and honouring them is stated
once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.
The material relation is whether an undeclared, unmeasured or exceeded
limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. The rule applies
RF-014's prohibition of silent omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a
resource control applies only through a selected frame, and UP-014's
selection rule.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F6.%20Cost%20and%20proportionality%2FResource%20limits","start_line":1627}],"statement":"Incomplete copying falsifies the availability predicate and returns incomplete. A closed sortedness report may be available as candidate_ready/satisfied for report availability while its sortedness assessment is indeterminate. Setup that never invokes the evaluator produces no assessment result or exhausted traversal stop. Preserve these predicates and scopes; no exhausted stop maps to satisfied merely because work stopped.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Incomplete copying falsifies the availability predicate and returns incomplete. A closed sortedness report may be available as candidate_ready/satisfied for report availability while its sortedness assessment is indeterminate. Setup that never invokes the evaluator produces no assessment result or exhausted traversal stop. Preserve these predicates and scopes; no exhausted stop maps to satisfied merely because work stopped.

Equal visible candidates can require different lawful next actions when standing, evidence, obligations or authority differ.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1498,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","quote":"### Formal representation

An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their
material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the
acquired views that project it follow
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)
and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable
positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),
including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection
that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows
[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and
[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;
these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

Purpose and material relation of the assurance relations: they connect
construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared
errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining
evidence whose applicability is established (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FFormal%20representation","start_line":1463},{"end_line":120,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Continuation-sensitive sufficiency

Fix one subject and the one-assessment policy Γ. States are `U` (unassessed),
`S` (satisfied report), `F` (falsified report) and `I` (indeterminate report).
Inputs are `assess_S`, `assess_F`, `assess_I` and `advance`. From U an assess
input records that report; from any assessed state it is refused as already
assessed, preserving state. `advance` preserves state and is allowed only
from S; it returns `block_unassessed`, `block_falsified` or
`block_indeterminate` from the other states. This is the complete transition
and decision rule for every state/input pair. There is no reset input in Γ.
A different contract can permit reassessment or re-entry.

The weak observation “satisfied assessment exists” maps U, F and I to false
and S to true. U and I nevertheless require incompatible first-assessment
decisions. Thus no decision function over that observation can preserve the
fixed policy. In a human handover, “not approved” similarly fails to say
whether to perform the first assessment or preserve a completed undecidable
assessment and follow its declared continuation.

Define `alpha(U)=(subject,basis,null)` and
`alpha(s)=(subject,basis,s)` for s in `{S,F,I}`, with those subject and basis
fixed by Γ. Define `delta_hat` and `T_hat` by the complete rule above on
these records. Every state/input satisfies
`delta=delta_hat o alpha` (with the unchanged input supplied) and
`alpha(T(s,u))=T_hat(alpha(s),u)`. The readouts “satisfied exists”, exact
standing, permitted first assessment and advance decision are preserved.
The program checks all 16 one-step cells and every length-four input
sequence from every state. Exact one-step preservation with the closed
domain and identical next-state basis also composes by induction to every
finite sequence in this model. Approximate models have no such automatic
bound.

All four states remain distinguishable. This is a sufficiency witness with
no state aggregation, not evidence of compression, minimum context,
cross-task context selection, Markov sufficiency outside Γ, or cheaper
operation. Authority and hold distinctions are exact in this example.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FContinuation-sensitive%20sufficiency","start_line":85}],"label":"Continuation-sensitive sufficient state"}}}

clauses.statement: Universal intake triage: Universal intake triage is the single entry for substantive change, determining substance, affected product boundary/scope, lawful class, re-entry point, affected downstream surfaces/evidence, and release-scope fit or repricing.

Reproduction must use RuntimeEventLog, execution basis, event-backed IntentLineage, ProductAssetModel publication basis/event refs, selected outcome identity/admitted bounded refs, GapPressureRow, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog, admitted evidence, ledger, closure decision, NextActionBasis and visible policy refs. Inability to reproduce signals hidden state. Each governing carrier must carry causal predecessor refs: outcome/bounded refs→binding; lineage→model→gap→binding→priority→selected-action projection→construction intent→evidence→ledger→closure decision→next-action basis→post-action projection. Both projection occurrences must be predecessor-reachable; the latter also uses fresh eval_gap. Construction intent preserves authority refs. Reproduction must be reachable without external joins; a broken chain fails replayability.

may be carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing when project
policy allows it; it may be escalated to explicit human adjudication when
project policy requires it; the threshold between those actions is

may therefore choose different ambiguity-handling policies: a lower risk

higher one permits more bounded probabilistic decision-making. In either

all ambiguity before work"; it is "make ambiguity visible, govern it

sufficiently constrained".","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F5.%20Ambiguity%20governance%20and%20lifecycle","start_line":1220}],"statements":["Projects choose different declared risk appetites and ambiguity policies.","Policy may permit bounded probabilistic carrying/decision or require escalation to admitted human adjudication.","Progressive reduction, rather than elimination of all ambiguity before work, is permitted."]},"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:065a5bcdf5d590bf751ee354a48a1fb4","urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ec3fe457ff545609a3a932efc40f4772","urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:53d521b9660dfaf47fd92b1cf8d4deec"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","forbidden_variation":{"grounding":[{"end_line":1234,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","quote":"The default governance model: ambiguity

clauses.statement: A review's core result determines the described triage-payload class and consumption restrictions; the payload is distinct from the result and decision.

Source.repository is a URI reference; selector is a declared stdo channel URI and has no operative authority without exact resolution/adoption. Basis requires exact immutable RC or stable release URI and 64 lowercase hex manifest digest. RC ordinal is positive without leading zero; stable major/minor/patch syntax follows the selected release profile. Constitutional entrypoints carry basis and URI references and resolve relative to that named basis; these objects disallow extra fields. Reference arrays retain declared uniqueness and empty versus nonempty distinctions. Syntactic validity does not prove same-cut consistency, installed byte identity, a valid grant or semantic sufficiency.

clauses.statement: Executive consumes results of the declared evaluations for a bounded next decision; consumption alone supplies no new authority.

D_ext is exactly {external_preserved,external_introduced,external_removed}; W_ext exactly {external_resolution,domain_resolution,codomain_resolution}; Q_ext exactly {external_identity,reference_domain,external_target_kind,resolved_target_identity,basis_relation,resolution_basis,evidence_identity}. For every d∈D_ext,q∈Q_ext, T.d[].q uses ResolutionRefDomain(q); for every w∈W_ext,q∈Q_ext, T.external_resolution_witnesses[].w.q does likewise. Witness domain_model and codomain_model each resolve one external ModelContentIdentity/B_adopted; witness evidence resolves one Evidence/B_adopted. Every Q_ext coordinate has cardinality one and no local target: external_identity and resolved_target_identity resolve the sibling external_target_kind under the sibling basis_relation over sibling resolution_basis; reference_domain resolves Sigma:ReferenceDomain/B_profile; external_target_kind resolves Sigma:ExternalTargetKind under B_profile or B_adopted; basis_relation resolves Sigma:BasisRelation/B_profile; resolution_basis resolves TraversalOccurrenceProfileBasis, AxiomaticCalculusBasis or ProductAdoptionBasis under B_profile, B_calculus or B_adopted; evidence_identity resolves Evidence/B_adopted. Each D_ext member is a finite duplicate-free Resolution_M list; external_resolution_witnesses is a finite duplicate-free ExternalResolutionPreservationWitness list. Coordinates have exactly Q_ext; witnesses have exactly the seven stated fields and decision equal. Missing/extra nested fields, unresolved nested identities, coordinate/basis mismatches, duplicate coordinates or witnesses outside the exact preserved population refuse model validation.

Coordinated release-matched asset cohorts

A Product authority may declare an explicit cross-Product Release-Matched
Asset Cohort when one source corpus and its required distributed or
derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set. The declaring
relation names every required Product and asset, the exact source
dependency, its owning authorities, the qualification boundary and the
publication transaction. Path co-location, equal version text or a common
actor cannot infer the relation (P3, P6).

For the existing RC-profile cohort, every required member uses one exact version suffix
`<version>-rc.<n>`. Product-local cut names and refs render it as
`v<version>-rc.<n>`; embedded asset-version fields render the same suffix
without `v`. Qualification normalises only that leading cut-name marker
and requires exact suffix equality. Equal versions establish release
matching only. They do not collapse Product identities, member
inventories, tags, acceptance judgments or release authorities (P3, P6).

For a release-matched STDO stack, the closed cohort contains all of (P3,
P4b):

1. the exact STDO standards corpus cut;
2. the distributed `spec` plugin and host assets carried by that STDO cut;
3. the exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product used to validate and project
   the index;
4. the exact STDO Representation Product; and
5. its released `a_c.STDO` axiomatic program and logical constraint map
   or equivalent semantic index, with the complete source-STDO member
   inventory, member digests, member-set digest and exact cut identity
   used to derive it.

The cohort is incomplete when a required member is missing, stale,
differently versioned, built from another source cut, or unable to
reproduce its declared source-member and digest closure. A change to any
source member covered by the index invalidates the old derived candidate
for the successor cohort. The index is regenerated, mechanically
validated, independently qualified where required, and released under the
same new cut name. A stale index may remain immutable history; it cannot
accompany the changed source as the current cohort (P3, P5, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts","start_line":552},{"end_line":994,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"### PC-07 — Change, evidence and reliance

Each cross-boundary use binds the actual selected sources and material execution
basis, including uncommitted bytes where relevant. A moving selection identifies
how advancement is detected and which reliance must be reassessed. Git is one
possible carrier, not a mandatory identity system.

Changes and new counterexamples propagate through material assertion, execution
and evidence-use dependencies under [FOUNDATIONS Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse). Historical
evidence remains about its original subject. Reuse on a changed subject needs an
established applicability or preservation relation; rereading alone does not
establish it. A new release does not invalidate a still-selected older release,
and a changed hash alone establishes neither semantic incompatibility nor
continued validity. Unknown impact holds the dependent assurance or widens
assessment; it does not require unrelated work to restart.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-07%20%E2%80%94%20Change%2C%20evidence%20and%20reliance","start_line":980}],"kind":"requires","meaning":"A coordinated cohort still evaluates the actual current Product relations, source and evidence dependencies; same-version packaging alone does not establish their semantic adequacy."},"scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"],"source":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:e17011ff678c1e1fc0723e12d17e820d","target":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:bcb769c763230c0182097d3cc494c488"}}
