Landing makes an exact candidate available at an authorized checkpoint or
integration destination. It is an operation under its existing grant, not
acceptance of the candidate's claims. Work closure applies the stated closing
condition; release applies the separately selected publication and acceptance
conditions of [RELEASE](RELEASE.md). Record these as separate decisions (P6,
P3).

Review supplies QA evidence for those decisions. A pending review does not by
itself hold landing: an admitted candidate may land after its bounded work
and fix pass, while review of that exact candidate runs beside subsequent
authorized work. A required review holds the closure or acceptance claim that
depends on its complete report. A governing landing condition, applicable hard
stop or missing operation authority still prevents landing; availability is
no waiver. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks)
binds the optional profile's repair/recheck cadence (P6, P2).

Permitted downstream work may consume a landed candidate before its review
reports, carrying its exact identity, unresolved conditions and dependency
links. This is provisional use, not admitted truth. A later material finding
invalidates the affected dependent results under
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); unrelated valid results
remain reusable. Repair and re-evaluation follow those dependencies before
further reliance (P4b, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F5.%20Acceptance%2FLanding%2C%20closure%20and%20release","start_line":363},{"end_line":404,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md","quote":"### Declared Product acceptance gates

A Product-owned frame basis, or a work contract explicitly delegated that
choice by the basis, may declare a gated handoff between two Products. It
names both Product identities, the directed relation, exact candidate/claim,
required review and coverage, acceptance conditions and decision owner. Until
that review has covered its declared subject and the acceptance conditions
are satisfied, the downstream Product cannot accept the candidate as an
admitted input or close claims dependent on that acceptance. Authorized
provisional work and repair may continue under the preceding section (P6,
P2).

The gate's declaration is explicit; co-location, a dependency or this available
mechanism creates none. Existing user-acceptance, release/go-live and other
Product boundaries retain their own conditions. This member declares no
particular Product gate or extra capture-review hold on landing (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F5.%20Acceptance%2FDeclared%20Product%20acceptance%20gates","start_line":389}],"statement":"State which decision is requested and apply its actual grants, hard stops and conditions. Bootstrap

Every product defined under this method begins from
`templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json`, copied to the product's
definition root as `stdo_default.json` for a singleton default project or
as `stdo_<label>.json` for a named product definition. An existing project
fills the URI bindings over its current layout; adoption requires no
moving, renaming or duplicating of existing authority or realisation
surfaces (P2, P3).

The default scaffold binds:

- a shared versioned STDO store, addressed through the exact
  `constitution.stdo.basis`, as the installed distribution of the selected
  process constitution;
- `specification/GOALS.md` as current work-wave orientation;
- `specification/INTENT.md` as domain direction;
- `specification/PRODUCT.md` as the current product-definition surface;
- `specification/requirements/` as the live requirement surface;
- `build_tenants/` as the root for shared and tenant-local realisation
  surfaces; and
- `.ai-workspace/` as the sprint, ticket and comment carrier root.

These are template defaults, not universal path law; the definition's URI
bindings select the actual project carriers (P2).

The authority split is (P6, P3):

- mutable methodology authoring lives in the method's own source workspace
  (the standards of its source project) and governs only a future
  candidate cut;
- released methodology authority is the exact immutable STDO version
  selected by the consumer;
- installed methodology distribution lives in the toolchain manager's
  shared versioned store by default and matches the basis URI and manifest
  digest;
- project-owned constitutional surfaces live at the definition's `what`
  bindings; and
- project-owned realisation and work surfaces live at its `how` and
  `ticketing` bindings.

A project creates no competing local methodology root, such as a default
`specification/standards/`, and binds no mutable or partial method source
as if it were the selected immutable release (P6).

Method authority is singular: the selected immutable STDO release
authority, projected into the installed distribution located by the
overlay; and the project constitutional authority at the definition's
bound WHAT surfaces (P6). When editing or repricing methodology, the
mutable source path is authoring authority for the candidate being
constructed; it is not operative consumer law before release and explicit
selection (P3, P6). When operating inside a governed workspace, the
resolved installed basis is the operative distribution of the selected
immutable release until the consumer explicitly adopts another cut. A
project-local exact copy stays lawful when explicitly bound and verified;
it is not the default, and file proximity cannot select it (P6, P3).

The corresponding default folder shape is:

```text
stdo_default.json

specification/
├── GOALS.md
├── INTENT.md
├── PRODUCT.md
└── requirements/
    └── *.md

build_tenants/
├── common/
└── default/

.ai-workspace/
├── sprints/
├── tickets/
│   ├── backlog/
│   ├── active/
│   └── completed/
└── comments/
```

This is a starter topology, not a conformance requirement. A monorepo may
place several `stdo_<label>.json` definitions at one root and bind each to
a different WHAT. A hierarchical repository may place one or more
definitions at any nested project root. Recursive discovery (§9) finds both
shapes; explicit composition, never directory nesting, relates their
products (P3, P2).

A project need not start with a complete `requirements/` tree on day zero.
Requirements may be sourced from any legitimate constitutional input
regardless of its path, including `GOALS.md`, `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
existing requirement documents, imported standards or policy material,
prior project versions, and migration or repricing source material. Most
projects begin by deriving `INTENT.md` from `GOALS.md`, then `PRODUCT.md`
from `INTENT.md`, then the first requirement surface from the product
definition; that is the usual starting point, not the only lawful source
(P2).

The bootstrap sequence is (P3, P6, P2):

1. Install the STDO toolchain manager once, resolve the applicable release-profile
   discovery route (§4), and explicitly select one immutable release cut.
2. Install that complete cut in the shared release store and retain its
   deterministic installed-manifest digest.
3. Copy `PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json` from that exact cut to the
   product definition root as `stdo_default.json` or `stdo_<label>.json`.
4. Assign the stable `product.definition_id` for the mutable WHAT
   definition line, its source-project locator and its bounded-context
   declaration; keep it distinct from every immutable Product and release
   identity.
5. Bind `constitution.stdo.source`, its non-operative selector, the exact
   basis URI and manifest digest, every additional constitutional
   authority and the relevant basis-qualified entrypoints; confirm that
   the set collectively defines axioms, ontology, epistemology, taxonomy
   and semantics for the governed scope (§3).
6. Bind the agent bootstrap entrypoint and portable targets relative to
   the resolved `product.source_project`, then let the manager preflight
   every target and install or refresh only their marker-bounded
   discovery blocks.
7. Bind, or explicitly empty, the local axiom, override and
   disambiguation collections (§6).
8. Bind at least one accepted collective reference-frame basis, its
   admitting authorities and its exact governed scope (§7).
9. Write or confirm the current Goals carrier, run the goals to intent to
   product steps, and bind the resulting Intent and Product entrypoints.
10. Gather, derive, classify and bind the live specification or
    requirement surfaces without creating a co-equal rival.
11. Bind at least one build tenant, including its root, design and
    implementation surfaces, and bind any shared realisation law (§8).
12. Bind the Goals carrier, the ticket lanes, the comments root and the
    optional sprint root.
13. Bind every known product-composition edge explicitly, including its
    target definition identity, relation authority and non-empty contract
    set (§9). Bind the standalone/composed outcome, material recursive
    reliance and each actor's information boundary under PC-01–PC-07;
    separate authorized inspection from durable consumption.
14. Validate the JSON shape, assert URI and URI-reference syntax,
    synchronise and verify the exact installed basis, then resolve every
    URI and perform the cross-definition identity, composition,
    constitutional-sufficiency and authority-congruence checks. Mechanical
    resolution alone establishes neither the grants nor context adequacy
    of an admitted activation; unresolved material conditions remain open.

Once a bound requirement set is the live constitutional surface, no rival
monolithic requirements document should remain co-equal authority with it. This
keeps requirement truth structurally clear, derivable and non-monolithic
without prescribing its folder (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F12.%20Bootstrap","start_line":1077}],"statement":"The ordered sequence is: (1) install manager once, resolve an applicable release discovery route and explicitly select one immutable RC or profile-verified stable cut; (2) install the complete cut and retain deterministic manifest digest; (3) copy its exact template to the named/default definition; (4) assign stable mutable-WHAT definition ID, source-project locator and bounded context, distinct from every immutable Product/release ID; (5) bind constitution.stdo.source, non-operative discovery selector, exact basis URI/digest, additional authorities and basis-qualified entrypoints, confirming collective axioms/ontology/epistemology/taxonomy/semantics; (6) bind bootstrap entrypoint and portable targets relative to resolved product.source_project, preflight every target and install/refresh only marker-bounded discovery blocks; (7) bind or explicitly empty local axiom/override/disambiguation collections; (8) bind at least one accepted collective frame basis, admitting authorities and exact scope; (9) confirm/write Goals, run goals→intent→product and bind Intent/Product; (10) gather/derive/classify/bind live requirements without a co-equal rival; (11) bind at least one tenant with root/design/implementation and any shared realisation law; (12) bind Goals, ticket lanes, comments and optional sprint root; (13) explicitly bind every known composition edge with target ID, relation authority and non-empty contracts; (14) validate shape, assert URI syntax, synchronise/verify basis, resolve every URI and perform identity/composition/sufficiency/congruence checks.","uncertainty":"This records the sequence as data rather than executing it. The complete manager implementation and a concrete installed or adoption instance are not established by the supplied source contracts."},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: A lawful composition dominates another only if every material dimension is comparable or evidenced non-discriminating, it is no worse on all comparable dimensions and strictly better on at least one. A potentially reversing material unknown prevents dominance and remains a gap. Dominated candidates cannot be selected; thus a local rebuild dominated by an existing lawful composition is inadmissible. Unused feature breadth alone proves no dominance and may add lifecycle cost. The existing trade-off owner may choose an undominated lawful composition only using declared exact-Product/basis priorities and risk tolerances, recording their resolution of the frontier. Unresolved priorities leave a design gap. Fewest dependencies, smallest edit/line count or richest features are not necessary selection criteria. Each rejected material candidate records decisive evidence or falsifier; unsupported preference is not closure.

Adoption should not await winning standardisation. Preferred incremental wedge: comprehend one bounded source slice, publish a fragment, stitch an adjacent fragment, answer a difficult incumbent-pipeline question, emit conventional and covariant outputs together. The practical obligation demonstrates both output classes from one semantic substrate rather than immediate central convergence. Mature lines should also demonstrate deterministic compilation retaining traceability and challengeability.

clauses.statement: Required functionality does not determine counts of entities, functions, operations, carriers or modules. Every performed evaluation returns an F3 core value directly or through its defined refinement; records, including exclusions, are not results. Modules bound traversal reasoning and are classified by recommended roles; the head's binding applies tier-2 assurance law unchanged. Semantic functions should be total or as close as language/problem allow; immutable typed values are preferred. Effects should be explicit at the edge, controllers should not hide semantic authority and coupling should be reduced through dependency shape. A boundary governing, observing or evaluating another actor publishes state, boundary and admissible routes, not strategy unless ratified responsibility includes strategy. Cleanup is lawful only when boundary-local and neutral in behaviour, authority, visibility and effect; leaving an opened boundary better is a should, and cross-boundary opportunities are owner repricing input. Credible recurrence triggers commonisation review, never automatic merge. Before closure, reconstruct the exact claim's function, reuse accepted evidence only under reuse law, and block closure for falsifying issues or applicable hard stops; outside-claim discoveries do not enlarge scope. Each interface family has one source truth consumed downstream; retaining an old authority path behind a new interface is bridge debt, while compatibility needs its own authority and proof. Review checks governing rules; unanswered required relations withhold conformance, and evidence-based diagnosis goes to the actual owner. Missing authority/observation alone proves neither excessive coupling nor imperative design. Prompt clauses enforcing design law need provenance and evidence of continued causal effect. Adoption applies consistently across the named boundary; partial adoption identifies boundary/rule family and cannot claim completion whose evidence was skipped. Consumer-bound ABG-role runtime identity generators, validators and normalisers may publish defaults only within that role; defaults confer no authority and the identity owner may override them.

Release version boundary

Release version is not the same thing as object identity (P3). Under the release law
([RELEASE §1 and §2](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities), with
[SPEC_METHOD §6](SPEC_METHOD.md#6-lineage-and-release)):

- an immutable release cut is the only exact operative release
  identifier;
- an RC-profile mutable version-line selector only names the highest-ordinal
  published immutable cut on its line (FOUNDATIONS §2); a stable profile
  discovers its immutable tag directly under RELEASE §2;
- release version is a release-process fact; and
- release version is not the live constitutional identity of every
  object in the project.

So the method distinguishes object identity, release identity,
publication or revision coordinates, and mutable discovery selectors.
These may relate, but they are not interchangeable (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/IDENTITY.md#IDENTITY%2F9.%20Release%20version%20boundary","start_line":329}],"label":"Release versus object identity"}}}

clauses.statement: Release versus object identity: Object identity, release identity, publication/revision coordinates and mutable discovery are distinct. Immutable cut is exact release identity; RC selectors and stable discovery do not replace selected cut authority. Release version does not become every constitutional object’s live identity.

It is distinct from Product priority, promotion-boundary effect and owner disposition. Historical and alternative scales retain their own identities and are not silently translated.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":499,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md","quote":"#### Selected 1–5 severity convention

The severity convention selected for this review flow is **1 highest to 5
lowest**. The Reviewer grades the consequence of the demonstrated defect if
it manifests, using these qualitative anchors. The Product-owned frame basis
binds the convention and its Product-specific evidence criteria: affected
claims, users/paths, consequence, dependencies and supported containment (P6).

| Severity | Consequence anchor |
|---|---|
| 1 | Critical loss of the governed outcome or of essential safety, authority or integrity across its affected scope. |
| 2 | Major failure of essential behaviour, with substantial affected users, paths or dependencies and no adequate ordinary containment. |
| 3 | Material but bounded failure whose disposition depends on its downstream impact and wider blast radius. |
| 4 | Limited local failure with supported containment or a practical workaround and little effect outside that local scope. |
| 5 | Minor actionable defect with minimal functional consequence for the declared outcome. |

Severity 3 requires an explicit assessment of downstream dependencies and
blast radius. Material impact on dependent work normally calls for repair;
contained local impact may be deferred with a recorded reason and responsible
owner. The Executive makes that disposition from the evidence and its grant,
preserving the Reviewer's grade; a departure from the normal repair response
also records its reason. Unknown dependent impact is not evidence of
containment. Mandatory claims, hard stops and acceptance conditions still
determine boundary effects under EVALUATION §5. Severity 3 is not priority P3,
and no severity value automatically supplies priority, a block or permission
to defer (P6, P2).

An older or alternative Product-selected scale keeps its identity and evidence
criteria. Selecting this convention is explicit; any translation is declared
and justified rather than inferred from matching numbers. Historical findings
retain the scale and grade under which they were assessed. A no-finding result
carries no severity grade; it is not severity 5 (EVALUATION §4; P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#EXECUTIVE_BASELINE%2F5.%20Profile%20terms%2FTechnical%20triage%2C%20severity%2C%20priority%20and%20boundary%20effect%2FSelected%201%E2%80%935%20severity%20convention","start_line":468}],"label":"Selected 1–5 review severity"}}}

clauses.statement: Selected 1–5 review severity: Where explicitly selected, severity runs from 1 highest to 5 lowest and describes technical impact. It is distinct from Product priority, promotion-boundary effect and owner disposition. Historical and alternative scales retain their own identities and are not silently translated.

Material content. For the obligations it serves, the binding
   identifies:
   - the operations, each with its inputs, outputs, effects and outcome
     values; each outcome value maps to exactly one core value under
     [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and an intended
     external effect, one of uncertain completion included, is recorded as
     [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) states;
   - the composition laws, and the transformations the calculus permits;
   - the resource measures;
   - the operational assumptions on which conformance depends, among them
     those about actors, tools, availability and failure.

   Human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources are
   measured where a selected obligation needs them. Each measure states its
   unit and its boundary: what is counted, and where measurement starts and
   stops. A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no
   conformance claim. The size of a selected context is measured as
   [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)
   step 3 measures it, against the capacity the binding declares for the

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:e17777d4ad97c92bf9f2402e9341ee1c"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:421a2f3fa75817ae6e4ba72b2268eeca","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":222,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md","quote":"## Construct And Prove

Use the accepted Project Reference-Frame Basis to determine applicable
evaluations, including those required by an affected owner. A known false
condition omits that evaluation; an unknown condition is unresolved, not
false: it needs a bounded resolution or an explicit residual, and the claim
that depends on it is withheld until evidence or the owning decision
resolves it (ACTIVATION §1 Applicability). Missing required
results cannot count as satisfied. Availability of a frame does not require activating it.

When that basis permits direct Writer use and one sufficient context/grant
covers the outcome, construct directly without an additional coordinating
activation, Reviewer or durable ticket. Activate the coordination the
applicable configuration selects for a material dependency, authority or
context boundary. While occupying Executive, do not edit files or
Git state; the same actor must first enter a separately bound Writer activation.
An actual independence requirement still needs an independent capable actor.
One exact Writer grant may cover its declared construction, status and checkpoint
sequence. Record actual role transitions; unchanged status alone does not need
a new activation or wholesale rehash. Refresh bindings on material change.

1. Work inside the smallest coherent causal cone and exact write territory.
   Read material producers, consumers and owners across that cone within the
   access grant; narrow write territory is not a narrower reasoning boundary.
   Return cross-territory repairs to their owner.
   Preserve solution space where variation cannot change a governed property.
2. Implement and self-review the bounded change.
3. Derive tests through:

   ```text
   work carrier -> triage -> re-entry -> requirement/design/module/closure law
   ```

4. Use the cheapest focused falsifier adequate for the claim. Add integration,
   installed-development, harnessed sandbox, or live sandbox evidence only
   where the Product claim requires it. A real probabilistic boundary requires
   a live lane.
5. Reconcile authority, design, implementation, tests, and displaced rival
   paths before claiming a candidate.
   Consume established facts while their exact subject, basis, scope,
   provenance and validity apply. Function boundaries alone do not invalidate
   them; mutation, rollback, authority/basis change and actual trust boundaries
   retain their applicable checks. For material computational composition or
   recurrence, inspect the complete path and its accumulated work under the
   owning design and optional frame refinement. Qualify declared workloads and
   operational assumptions rather than inferring adequacy from local green.
   Retire superseded responsibility; retained mechanisms need a supported
   obligation, owner, purpose, scope and cost, and temporary ones a removal
   trigger. Audit affected test predicates against the supported operating and
   threat model; an excluded threat cannot require a replacement guard.
6. Return the exact candidate and stop at a delegated return boundary.
   Product-owned decision authority, or an
   authorized Executive when that profile is adopted, decides whether Product,
   qualification, release, risk, or admitted-work law requires independence
   and separately activates `stdo-review`.

For a selected repair pass, apply [the selected review flow](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#review-flow-from-the-selected-basis):
bind linked findings/items, exact repaired subject, failing-before/passing-after
reproduction and the declared suite. Identify tests versus any required
independent recheck honestly. Keep authorized landing separate from work
closure and release; a local repair does not automatically add a review round.

Keep reusable judgments and owner rulings in the existing carrier: exact
question, subject/basis, supporting computed evidence, actor and authority,
conclusion, scope, uncertainty and revising observation. Preserve the original
owner ruling separately from interpretation. Invalidate the affected claim
when one of the invalidators of `ACTIVATION.md` section 7 occurs; retain
unrelated valid results. Reuse does not
manufacture an owner ruling or satisfy required independent assessment.

On repricing, retain, supersede, defer or withdraw each affected obligation with
its owner/evidence links in this carrier. Present the short consequence delta;
"continue" does not accept an undisclosed architectural change. An authorized
preservation checkpoint can keep unfinished work with its predecessor,
territory, concurrent-writer disposition and durable evidence; it claims no
acceptance or publication.

Evaluate closure as the conjunction of satisfied applicable obligations,
valid supporting evidence, required judgments/rulings and absence of an active
non-closure condition. A review event is not completion. Record a satisfied
bounded result under the existing state-mutation grant; withhold only the
affected claim when a condition is missing. Qualification, publication and
consumer adoption retain their separate conditions.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md#STDO%20Work%2FConstruct%20And%20Prove","start_line":140},{"end_line":230,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md","quote":"## Return

Return the exact candidate/checkpoint, changed paths, affected authority,
execution-contract admission mechanism/result/evidence, focused and broader
proof, non-changes, residuals, and closed or withheld work result. Do not
claim acceptance beyond the grant, discard a surviving obligation, or silently
continue beyond a delegated return boundary.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md#STDO%20Work%2FReturn","start_line":224}],"statement":"Construct from the first changed authority layer: current requirements precede accepted design and implementation when their meanings change. Preserve sole operative truth and lifecycle disposition, causal trace and acceptance criteria; code is evidence rather than authority. Begin with the cheapest adequate falsifier, then broaden for the selected claim and risk through unit, integration, deterministic sandbox, live external or installed public paths as applicable. Green evidence on a substitute subject or boundary cannot close the claim. Worker self-review stays construction output; independent assessment and owner disposition remain separate when required. Apply selected landing/QA/recheck/report rules without inventing gates or review ratios. Record exact candidate, evidence, surviving obligations and effect uncertainty on the authorized durable surface; return to consumer and stop where the admitted relation stops. Counts and review occurrence do not establish closure, release or adoption.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Resets, repair loops, moving subjects, proof masking and duplicated authority are possible misfit signals, not verdicts or a universal architecture.

Expected outcomes are durable published domain artifacts, composed models, primary entity cuts, applicable inspectable Markov overlays, explicit treatment/covariance semantics, grounded epistemic correspondence overlays, temporal reference artifacts, familiar projections, applicable deterministic execution artifacts and a basis for AI reasoning over institutional meaning.

A published RC cut exists to provide one exact subject for review, replay
and possible acceptance. To publish it, the project (P3, P5, P6):

1. confirms the triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry;
2. declares the exact Product release subject and release-scoped claim
   set;
3. reconciles the release note and other release-facing assets to that
   subject;
4. runs the proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks;
5. commits the exact carrier;
6. resolves and records the exact Project Release Namespace, Project
   Subtree root and Project Subtree tree;
7. creates one annotated immutable `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` tag and
   an annotated `<project>/v<version>` selector tag over that same commit
   in a shared release source;
8. atomically pushes the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector
   and optional release branch where the transport supports it;
9. verifies remotely that the immutable tag, selector and release branch
   resolve to the highest published RC commit; and
10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to
    reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout.

Each published RC tag is immutable. Further work increments `<n>` on the
same version line when the intended line remains applicable. It does not
require a minor-version increment merely because review found a bounded
repair. A published higher RC without matching selector advancement is an
invalid, fail-closed release state; it never authorises resolution of the
older cut as the version-line latest (P3, P5).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FImmutable%20RC%20publication","start_line":330},{"end_line":426,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Monotonic version-line advancement

On an RC-profile line, version-line advancement makes the newly published highest RC for one
Project Release Namespace discoverable (P3, P5):

1. identify the exact new immutable RC tag, ordinal and peeled commit;
2. confirm that no higher RC ordinal already exists on that line;
3. confirm the project-qualified selector is absent or currently resolves
   to a lower RC ordinal on the same project line;
4. atomically create or force-update the annotated `<project>/v<version>`
   selector to the new highest RC commit;
5. create or update `release/<project>/<version>` to the same commit when
   that optional carrier is used;
6. push the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector and optional
   release branch atomically where the transport supports it; and
7. verify remotely that the selector peels to the highest RC commit and
   that the matching immutable annotated RC tag exists.

Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated
RC tag, any higher ordinal already exists, the selector would move to a
lower RC, or the selector and release branch would not align to the same
highest commit (P5).

Forward movement is strictly monotonic by RC ordinal. A later defect is
repaired through a higher immutable RC, not by moving an old RC tag or
rolling the selector backward. The selector is therefore equivalent to
`v<version>-rc.latest`, while every concrete RC tag remains addressable
(P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FMonotonic%20version-line%20advancement","start_line":399}],"statement":"For an RC-profile line, confirm triaged scope and exact Product subject; reconcile assets and pre-RC checks; commit the exact carrier; bind namespace/subtree; create annotated immutable RC and selector on the same commit; atomically publish the complete required refs where supported; remotely verify annotation and highest ordinal alignment.   the actual task/result mechanism; if its properties cannot meet a required
  boundary, return the unsupported activation rather than silently executing
  in the issuer's context.

Conformance asks whether implementation realises the module or design boundary; UAT asks whether the composed product satisfies its claimed requirement or scenario.

clauses.statement: Use admitted evidence about the subject. completed → satisfied requires full intended effect and established end. not_effected → falsified requires evidence that the declared outcome is unattained and no later completion can attain it: examples include no effect beginning, an effect ending short, a bounded interval closing partly undone, or prior action destroying what the outcome needs; name any part that occurred. completion_unknown → indeterminate when neither other value is established, including lost response without observed counterexample or full effect observed while it may still act; name the deciding observation. Lost response, absent record or no context trace is not evidence of not_effected. End is established by subject evidence that action ceased or never began; if an effect began without established end, record the needed observation separately. End does not decide not_effected: a closed incomplete interval can falsify outcome while action continues. Counterexample and end residual remain independent. Before repetition or dependent action, reconcile uncertain completion sufficiently for that action; not_effected with unknown end licenses neither absence assumptions nor repetition.

product, requirement, design, runtime, data-contract or governance
boundaries it excludes; the change classes it expects to contain; the
local proof or compliance debt, if any, that may be deferred during the
sprint; the closure trigger and closure law; and the paydown or repricing
path for debt discovered at close.

Sprints exist because proof cost is not uniform. For some work, especially
projection-surface and user-interface iteration, proving every micro-change
before the next change can cost more than making the bounded change visible
and correcting it at close. That optimisation is lawful only when the
deferred cost remains local, visible, bounded and repayable. Deferred
compliance inside a sprint is escrow, not acceptance: it satisfies no
method, release or product closure until it is paid down, explicitly
accepted under the governing method, or repriced into the appropriate

predicate is `satisfied`; a false predicate is `falsified`, the
basis-bound fact that makes it false being the counterexample; a missing
or ambiguous premise is `indeterminate`, or `out_of_frame` where the
premise needs a relation the frame does not declare, and never
`falsified`. An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
`falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value, and the obligation
leaves the required coverage of a dependent conjunction under the cited
authority of that applicability result. An obligation whose applicability is
unresolved stays in that required coverage. A predicate that its owner
declares as a disjunction that includes non-application, such as "meets
the axiom or does not apply", may be `satisfied` because the obligation
does not apply; that `satisfied` is for the declared disjunction only and
never counts toward the predicate that the obligation holds","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FApplicability","start_line":466}],"statement":"Owning evaluation/scope predicates determine obligations from sufficient basis-bound facts. Missing/ambiguous premise is indeterminate, or out_of_frame if it needs an undeclared relation, never falsified. Exclusion has no obligation result/core value, removes only that obligation from conjunction coverage and waives no acceptance criterion; unresolved applicability remains in coverage and withholds dependent claim until evidence/owner decision resolves it. Owner-declared disjunction including non-application may be satisfied by exclusion, but that satisfaction belongs only to the disjunction, never the obligation-holds predicate. Missing, stale, wrong-subject/basis or incapable required results cannot satisfy conjunction; other applicable constraints remain even when detected by only one evaluation. clauses.statement: Owning evaluation/scope predicates determine obligations from sufficient basis-bound facts. True applicability is satisfied and requires evaluation/result; false is falsified with its basis-bound counterexample and excludes only that obligation under cited authority. Missing/ambiguous premise is indeterminate, or out_of_frame if it needs an undeclared relation, never falsified. Exclusion has no obligation result/core value, removes only that obligation from conjunction coverage and waives no acceptance criterion; unresolved applicability remains in coverage and withholds dependent claim until evidence/owner decision resolves it. Owner-declared disjunction including non-application may be satisfied by exclusion, but that satisfaction belongs only to the disjunction, never the obligation-holds predicate. Frame/tool/family availability alone triggers no activation. Residual semantic applicability judgment retains judgment/evidence identity rather than masquerading as computation. Missing, stale, wrong-subject/basis or incapable required results cannot satisfy conjunction; other applicable constraints remain even when detected by only one evaluation. Finite declared qualification fixtures must distinguish true/false/unknown premises, missing/wrong-subject results and sufficient positive result; always-skip/always-activate rules fail those distinct expectations. Members/profiles/projects reuse this exclusion owner rather than redefining it.

Each child records parent contract, purpose, material entities, identity and lifecycle relations, semantic owners, direct sibling seams, applicable invariants and prohibited competing paths. It is neither an organisational nor a runtime hierarchy.

Result rules, owners and consumer register: The source's family F3 trace register connects result and combination rules to commitments, added choices, owners and consumers. Its instance premises are declaration of predicate, subject and basis; combination of evaluations, steps or members into a decision; and a need for finer outcomes. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are treated as independent; P5 is derived from P0 and P6, and P4b from P0 and P2. The register attributes the core names and non-success division to Results; refined meanings to their definers; conjunction choices to its applying member/profile; acceptance to EVALUATION §5; step stops to ACTIVATION §3; transformation record fields to AC-013; composition-law need to the governing evaluation under RF-010; latitude to the contract owner; shared implementation to accepted design; categorical claims to their claimant.

The profile claims institutional systems often retain values while losing interpretive context. Records require function, provenance and treatment context; mappings treat governed meaning; catalogs and schemas project deeper semantics. A channel or mutable selector discovers candidates but does not itself determine or update the consumer basis.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":482,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"## 4. Selector and consumer adoption

An RC-profile version-line selector answers only (P6, P3):

> Which highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut currently exists on
> this version line?

It never answers:

> Which exact STDO cut governs this consumer?

A Product Definition may retain `stdo://channels/<version>` as its
discovery selector, but its operative basis is the exact
`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/` or stable
`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/` URI and installed-manifest digest,
the installed release basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4. Moving the Git
version-line selector does not update any consumer. Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable cut. RC resolution requires an
annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled
selector ref fails closed and cannot be interpreted as a lightweight
selector whose tag object is its commit (P6, P3, P5).

For an RC line, channel resolution enumerates the published RC tags for the selected
Project Release Namespace, including preserved unqualified historical cuts
during a namespace transition, selects the greatest positive ordinal,
requires that cut and the current selector to be annotated tags peeling to
the same commit, and fails closed when the selector lags or points
elsewhere. Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal
is below the Product Definition's current exact basis. A consumer that
intentionally retains an older cut names that immutable RC URI and digest
explicitly and uses exact-basis operations such as `sync`; it does not
express that choice through the latest-version channel (P5, P6).

For a stable line, channel resolution returns its verified stable-v1 cut
without ordinal comparison or a separate selector. A legacy bare selector is
never admitted as a stable exact basis; an ambiguous profile is refused. The
same digest-bound adoption operation applies to either profile (P3, P5, P6).

Presentation and mutation are separate invocations. The read-only plan,
the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest. Mutation requires that exact digest as the
operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product
Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the
acceptance. A fleet uses the same law with one aggregate digest over all
exact per-definition plans. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not
external presentation and cannot authorise itself. The plan's hashing rule
and the manager's command boundaries are PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4 (P6, P3).

This split lets operators refer to `v<version>` for the latest published
RC without repeatedly incrementing the version line, while every governed
project retains reproducible exact-cut authority and changes only through
explicit adoption (P2, P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F4.%20Selector%20and%20consumer%20adoption","start_line":428}],"label":"Explicit exact consumer adoption"}}}

clauses.statement: Explicit exact consumer adoption: Consumer adoption is a separate authorized Product Definition transition binding one exact immutable release URI and installed-manifest digest. A channel or mutable selector discovers candidates but does not itself determine or update the consumer basis.

clauses.statement: The actor exercising admitted work authority selects assurance for stated risk, obligations and resource limits, identifying material consequences, coverage, uncertainty and conditions of action/acceptance. Additional evidence strengthens claims only within applicability/dependence accounts, not by test count or preference for more checks. Quantification declares population/uncertainty, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. Bayesian denominator must be nonzero; agreement/disagreement likelihoods under both faulty and non-faulty conditions matter, and formulas invent no missing inputs. Conditional miss terms need defined conditioning events; invent no conditional for zero-probability prefixes. Dropping previous-miss conditioning requires model-declared conditional independence. One minus joint miss is conditional chance of at least one detection, not whole-product correctness; agreement need not increase confidence. Sampled-case or injected-defect calibration applies only through a justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric confidence stays unresolved. Cheaper assurance cannot waive required safety, authority or acceptance conditions.

Digest authenticity does not establish the claim; an unknown effect remains unknown until sufficiently reconciled.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":198,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Evaluate The Return

The issuer checks activation identity, exact subject/basis, result variant,
evidence scope and invalidators before relying on the return. It acquires
only the return projection its own frame permits; a link to a full artifact
does not authorize reading it. A digest authenticates bytes, not their claims.

Reconcile an effect whose completion or end remains unknown before retry or
any dependent action (`ACTIVATION` §3 Effects and §5). A timeout, missing
message or lost context is not evidence that no effect occurred. Retain valid
progress; do not replay a step merely because its actor changed.

Apply the governing result/disposition relation and determine whether the
exact candidate requires independent review. Issue `stdo-review` separately
where required. Reviewer severity remains its technical assessment; the
decision owner assigns priority and boundary effect within its grant
(`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §12 steps 4–7). Do not turn a closed result into implicit
authority to repair, accept, publish or start the next stage.

A proposed next action is not an executable activation. Before calling it
already authorized or issuing it, bind the actual operation grant and the
settled subject/pass grouping required by that contract. If either is missing,
return the proposal and exact unresolved binding; do not presume a Writer grant
or combine unsettled passes. This checks the existing intake, not a new gate.

For an admitted sequence, each continuation uses the previous closed result
and current bindings. Retain the boundaries the contract actually declares:
neither a new human check-in at every pass nor review only at the end is a
universal rule. Refresh affected bindings on material change, not every
unchanged status observation (`ACTIVATION` §1 Roles and delegation; §7).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FEvaluate%20The%20Return","start_line":169}],"label":"Consumption of a closed return"}}}

Digest authenticity does not establish the claim; an unknown effect remains unknown until sufficiently reconciled.

clauses.statement: Disjointness, evaluation independence and assurance independence: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is procedural separation of activations that neither consume nor influence one another's unclosed working results; they may share subject or manifold and later contribute closed results to one conjunction. Assurance independence is claim-relative separation prescribed by assurance law, including non-authorship, acquisition, exposure, actor and configuration conditions. Disjointness does not imply independent evaluation, independent activation does not imply disjointness, and the unqualified word independent establishes none of the three.

Post and category vocabulary: A post is working commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff or repricing confidence. It may influence later specification/design but is not constitutional truth. Its category is one of REVIEW (critique), STRATEGY (proposed technical/method direction), GAP (precise insufficiency/contradiction), SCHEMA (data/event/interface/contract shape), HANDOFF (bounded context/task-state transfer) or MATRIX (explicit decision-option comparison).

clauses.statement: Each refined result maps to exactly one core value for its own named predicate, retaining vocabulary, residual and re-entry. Judgment decisions answer whether the judgment's first listed decision holds for the unchanged subject on the exact basis; stops answer whether the application can reach its declared result on that basis; effect dispositions answer whether the intended effect occurred. A stop does not answer construction availability ('a candidate is available'). Co-emitted values such as stale and hold can map differently because their predicates differ. Where cause changes mapping, cause is part of the refined value, not a new kind; records supply rather than choose that cause.

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:a8cafeeacc2f8bc2deda01690eaaf31b","urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:24e74b3ee72197fa9936bf64a5b690b6"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:5554a2f9263db57bd2c8e480eafe8015","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919},{"end_line":1115,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-016 Typed composition

Two traversals compose only when the first result type and judgment
satisfy the second traversal's exact domain and preconditions (P4a):

```text
F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v]
```

Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. It cannot
flatten probabilistic proposal, deterministic construction or evaluation and human
decision into one undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no
universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H` sequence; each application owns its lawful
topology (P4a, P4b, P6). FOUNDATIONS §3 P4a consumes this law.

A deterministic constructor feeding a deterministic evaluator still has
two exact traversal identities and retains both results and stops. A claimed
projection of their continuation follows the consumer-relative sufficiency
law in [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation); composition
alone establishes neither adequate observations nor a Markov property.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds%2FAC-016%20Typed%20composition","start_line":1095}],"statement":"Compose only when the first result type and judgment satisfy the second exact domain and preconditions. Current-promotion effects use EVALUATION §5: falsifying issue, competing/ambiguous authority, unlawful current boundary or omitted applicable requirement/design/predecessor claim, and durable architectural foreclosure supply its four domain triggers. Wording cannot narrow away active applicable authority. Absorb local clean-up/commonisation only when needed to make the claim true, preserve singular authority, satisfy accepted design or avoid foreclosure. Other clean-up, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary opportunities remain out-of-claim repricing inputs; they do not automatically widen scope, block the bounded claim or require follow-up. Owner-admitted repricing enters at the smallest lawful re-entry point; unclaimed future capability and optional clean-up are not implicit work.

It verifies exact installed manifest/member digests and returns only requested sections or a verified heading catalog, without discovery, admission, access-policy decision or dispatch.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":330,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Compact Source Acquisition

Use the bundled [read_basis.py](../scripts/read_basis.py) with the exact manager,
store and definition already selected by the control intake. It calls the
existing manager's read-only `status --verify` and `resolve`, checks manifest
and member digests, and returns identities plus only requested source sections.
It performs no discovery, admission, access-policy decision or dispatch.

```sh
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py check \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition>
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py read \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition> \
  --member standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md --list-headings
python3 -B <plugin-root>/scripts/read_basis.py read \
  --stdo <existing-manager> --store <selected-store> \
  --definition <exact-definition> \
  --member standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md --heading '11. The activation packet'
```

Replace the placeholders with the named routes; do not discover a different
manager/store when one fails. The default store may be used only when the
control binding selects it explicitly. Python 3.11+ is the helper's runtime;
its absence is an unavailable capability, not permission to install it.
`checked` verifies that source projection, not the work. `refused` and
`incomplete` supply no positive verification; retain the reason and re-enter
only the affected route. A missing or ambiguous heading has no guessed fallback.

Use `--list-headings` on an already-permitted member to discover its exact
selectors rather than guessing a heading or dumping the owner. The catalog
returns verified member identity plus heading names, levels, lines and
uniqueness; it supplies no section bodies. Catalog acquisition itself must be
permitted. The policy binding should expose its actual approved catalog/read
commands and source routes to the actor, so it need not invent commands.

The reader supports column-zero ATX headings, comment openers and fenced examples.
Quoted/list/indented heading or fence containers, unsupported HTML/setext
structures and unfinished comments/fences refuse the entire projection. This
closed selector domain is not a general Markdown parser. Refusal supplies no
partial section; an alternative exact verified route still needs its own grant.

For a handoff, begin with the packet section above. Acquire `EXECUTIVE_BASELINE`
§12's particular activation/return subsection only when its decision is needed.
For recovery, select `ACTIVATION`'s applicable Effects or work-state subsection.
Do not load whole owners or whole frames merely because their names appear in
this reference. An already-verified applicable fact need not be rederived for
each skill name. Use other exact source routes only when the question requires
them, keeping scope and uncertainty visible.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FCompact%20Source%20Acquisition","start_line":281}],"label":"Compact exact-basis source acquisition"}}}

clauses.statement: Occurrence identity binds only pre-admission facts: exact profile basis, pre-existing application identity, traversal identity, functor-kind identity, subject-binding identity, intended-outcome identity, declared lineage inputs and declared identity-dependency inputs. Application traversal/functor fields equal the occurrence's; lineage/dependency populations are those of relation congruence. Post-effect observations, effect evidence, judgments, admitted events, timestamps, admission ordinals and projection results stay outside the seed and may refer back only after their own identities exist. Mirroring relation records are minted after occurrence identity, do not enter its seed, and reproduce its endpoints exactly. Two applications of the same traversal to the same subject are two occurrences. Retry/continuation creates a new occurrence only on traversal reapplication; later controller steps, observations, waits and correlation records do not thereby become occurrences. Each retained bracketed AC-016 application has its own occurrence; an applied composite has an aggregate occurrence; component links do not imply material cause. Required intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stops remain explicit.

The contract makes FOUNDATIONS §2 Interpretation exact for one subject and signature and declares every listed coordinate: exact calculus basis; subject identity, inventory and bytes or semantic addresses; signature and compatible extension; mapping to every applicable record population, including the eight named populations; interpreter identity, capability, provenance and stops; structural evaluation; semantic selection and acceptance authority; source re-entry and invalidation. Construction grants no acceptance. Structural proof of shape, references, identity or basis does not establish retention of every material meaning; semantic acceptance remains separate.

1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
   execution contract for every question.
2. **Project the admitted unit.** The packet is a reference/verbatim projection
   of that unit, not a rewritten operating procedure. Use the compact bindings
   below or their equivalent in the existing carrier. Each binding points to
   an exact admitted source clause; any inlined grant or condition is quoted
   verbatim with its origin. The recipient applies the same skill to those
   bindings. Do not rewrite the skill or derive a new decision algorithm.

   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
   |---|---|
   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
   | Unresolved required binding | Missing source, verification or capability; return its cause and required re-entry instead of an executable packet |

   Preserve conditional grants as conditions. Do not add inferred conditionals,
   read/effect grants, retry permissions or closure rules. An effect grant alone
   does not grant acquisition of its output. For example, project these as
   separate existing clauses, without filling a missing clause by inference:

   ```text
   Effect and its condition: <exact admitted clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Output acquisition: <exact permitted output clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Retry / result / stop: <exact admitted clause references or verbatim quotes>
   ```

   Put any proposed new interpretation outside the execution packet and return
   for its required re-entry. Calling it a derivation or a safety rule does not
   make it an inherited grant.

   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence
   tools, use those contracts and retain their actual receipts. Do not replace
   required computation with a hand-written claim or invent tool success. A
   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces
   source/semantic judgment. Tooling availability creates no new dependency.
3. **Check the acquisition the packet prescribes.** Consider command output,
   diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded context as well as direct reads.
   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames
   that command prints is a contradiction. Resolve it before dispatch using
   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.
4. **Bind the host and dispatch.** Apply [Host Binding](#host-binding) and send
   the packet to the selected actor with the instruction to invoke this same
   skill as its recipient. Do not transfer ambient conversation by default
   where the frame excludes it. Record the dispatch/activation identity and
   actual mechanism in the existing carrier through its authorized Writer.
   If no available authorized mechanism meets the required boundary, retain
   the packet and return “not dispatched” with the missing capability. A
   prepared packet is not an active Worker or a work result.

Keep packet readiness separate from returning a response. If a required
control/source verification or capability is unavailable, return the missing
binding and the applicable incomplete/refused outcome; do not issue an
executable intake or label it ready, complete or closed. “Prepared, not
dispatched” applies only when the packet is sufficient and dispatch remains
unperformed; its consumer still checks the exact intake before using it.

by arranging the work. Where one same-actor role transition is sufficient and

a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure whose internal
state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket. The term is
substrate-neutral: the same topology is expected wherever a constraint

engineered institutional systems descended from both. The working claim

in an institutional system is the same kind of stable constraint
structure hypothesised for biological systems, re-expressed through
another substrate.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct","start_line":369},{"end_line":592,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","quote":"The

clauses.statement: Before reading, measure selected context in the declared capacity's unit, bytes or tokens, over the selected execution binding's boundary; record measurement, capacity and comparison. Fit covers only that boundary; outside context is not measured and receives no fit claim. The step's fit judgment requires recorded complete active inputs or a supported upper bound including host-supplied context; without either it is indeterminate unless a counterexample such as measured excess establishes falsified. A correct task result retains its bounded standing but cannot supply missing fit. This conditional measurement applies whatever question the step governs, is not a budget or universal gate, and proves fit only; adequate attention requires actual-use evidence. Other envelope dimensions and time, spend and resource limits retain their own laws.
