Naming

The shared-source RC-profile naming shape is (P3):

- RC branch: `rc/<project>/<version>`;
- immutable RC tag: `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>`;
- optional release branch: `release/<project>/<version>`; and
- mutable version-line selector tag: `<project>/v<version>`.

For example, on an RC line:

- candidate branch: `rc/example/3.0.0`;
- first immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.1`;
- second immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.2`;
- latest-release branch: `release/example/3.0.0`; and
- latest-published selector: `example/v3.0.0`.

A stable example is `example/v3.0.2`, with the stable-v1 marker and no
separate selector. The published tag is immutable.

The unqualified RC profile remains lawful only under the single-project and
historical-conservation conditions of §2. Projects may choose another
spelling only in a release source whose ref policy proves collision
freedom and preserves the same project namespace, mutable carrier,
immutable cut and mutable selector distinctions (P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F5.%20Naming","start_line":484},{"end_line":532,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Release-scoped assets

An immutable release cut may carry release-scoped surfaces such as (P3, P6):

- release notes;
- release and installed-distribution manifests;
- dependency declarations;
- package or installed-carrier metadata;
- qualification receipts; and
- branch and tag identity declarations.

Before publication, each used surface is reconciled to the exact cut
subject. After publication, changing one of those bytes requires the
applicable immutable successor: a higher RC or a new version after stable. The
version-line selector has no content-reconciliation phase because it adds
no new Product bytes (P3).

Exact version and cut identity belong in release-scoped carriers and
consumer basis bindings (P3). How a live constitutional surface, Product
and requirements surfaces included, uses version labels is the
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Specification surface rule](SPEC_METHOD.md#specification-surface-rule).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F6.%20Release-scoped%20assets%20and%20the%20Product%20subject%2FRelease-scoped%20assets","start_line":512},{"end_line":550,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Product subject and repository carrier

Before qualification, the project declares (P3, P6):

- its Project Release Namespace and exact Project Subtree root;
- the exact Product member set or artifact constituting the release
  subject;
- the release-scoped claim surfaces describing that subject; and
- co-located mutable source-project fields excluded from both.

A repository commit carries those declared sets but does not make every
co-located file or sibling Project Subtree a Product member. The exact
Project Subtree tree and Product member inventory distinguish the subject
from the wider carrier. Once the immutable cut is published, no post-review
carrier delta is admitted into that cut. Publication-caused ticket or
source-work bookkeeping is recorded afterward on the continuing source
branch and cannot move the immutable cut tag (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F6.%20Release-scoped%20assets%20and%20the%20Product%20subject%2FProduct%20subject%20and%20repository%20carrier","start_line":534}],"statement":"Name immutable cuts and project-qualified refs under the selected profile; release branches and selectors, where allowed, remain mutable convenience/discovery carriers. Release-scoped assets match the same exact cut and declared Product subject. Bind their inventory and public identities independently of repository carrier contents; documentation presence, packaging equivalence, source checks or artifact download alone do not establish installed usability or semantic acceptance.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Release-scoped assets match the same exact cut and declared Product subject. Bind their inventory and public identities independently of repository carrier contents; documentation presence, packaging equivalence, source checks or artifact download alone do not establish installed usability or semantic acceptance.

Transport repository and discovery selector are not substitutes; entrypoints route into the selected complete constitutional set without narrowing its authority.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":223,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"## 3. Constitutional-set sufficiency

A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1):

- axioms: irreducible starting truths, invariants and refusal conditions;
- ontology: the kinds of things treated as real and their material
  identities, relations, boundaries and lifecycle;
- epistemology: how claims become knowable or acceptable, including
  admissible evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification and
  decision authority;
- taxonomy: the classifications and kind distinctions that prevent
  category collapse; and
- semantics: the governed meaning of terms, relations, states, operations
  and outcomes.

These are sufficiency dimensions of the complete set, not filename classes,
required folders or a one-document-per-dimension partition. One document
may cover several dimensions and one dimension may be distributed across
several owning documents (P2).

`constitution.stdo.basis` locates the complete selected STDO constitutional
set; `constitution.additional_authorities` locates every additional
constitutional set or source. The STDO basis identifies one complete
immutable release cut and its exact installed-release manifest, never a
hand-selected subset. Each `constitution.entrypoints[]` member names the
basis against which its URI resolves. Entry points are derived navigation
and can neither narrow nor replace a complete selected constitution (P3,
P6).

This rule promotes no concrete design ontology into constitutional WHAT.
Product-level ontology that fixes Product meaning belongs in, or is cited
by, the bound WHAT. An accepted design ontology of a realisation boundary
(the design profile's) stays semantic-design authority for that boundary,
derives from constitutional WHAT and the applicable domain methods, and
cannot invent missing Product meaning (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F3.%20Constitutional-set%20sufficiency","start_line":187},{"end_line":350,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis
is the pair (P3):

```text
(immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)
```

The URI identifies one immutable annotated release cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status
and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8
JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line
endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path
order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible
rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).

The STDO Toolchain Manager is the bounded executable realisation that (P2,
P3):

- installs each immutable cut once in a shared, versioned release store;
- resolves logical `stdo://releases/...` URIs to verified installed bytes;
- inventories and verifies complete installed distributions;
- synchronises the exact basis already selected by a Product Definition;
- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a release-profile discovery
  route and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly
  accepted;
- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and
- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product
  Definitions.

The store may live at any machine-local path. Its registry maps logical
release URIs to installed paths and manifest digests and owns neither
Product selection nor method meaning. A consumer repository therefore needs
no project-local standards copy and no prescribed folder structure, and
several Product Definitions on one machine may select different installed
cuts concurrently (P3, P6). Every manager-owned component from the
configured store root downward is a physical directory or regular file of
its declared type; a symlink, junction, reparse point, device, socket or
other redirection or special entry fails closed. Verification inventories
every filesystem entry type, directories included, rejects any entry not
derived from the manifest's exact file paths, and never follows an
unmanifested alias (P5, P3).

`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.
`constitution.stdo.selector` is a `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery
route whose profile semantics are owned by [RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption).
An RC line resolves its mutable selector; a stable line resolves its exact
immutable cut without a second selector. Neither discovery nor the transport
source is operative authority.
`constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256`
are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).

The manager observes these command boundaries (P6, P5):

- `install` admits one explicitly named immutable release cut without changing
  any Product Definition;
- `sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by
  the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector;
- `adopt --dry-run` resolves the selected release profile and immutable cut, and
  presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest,
  current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic
  adoption-plan digest, without mutation;
- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit
  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound
  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes
  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses
  mutation;
- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with
  respect to Product Definitions; and
- fleet adoption emits, and requires explicit acceptance of, one aggregate
  plan digest over every per-definition plan; all fleet writes require
  explicit whole-selection authorisation and infer no composition or
  inheritance from directory nesting.

Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag-to-commit mismatch, manifest-digest
mismatch, missing, extra or changed installed members, ambiguous Product
Definition discovery, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, URI escape,
physical store redirection, undeclared filesystem entry types and malformed
bootstrap markers fail closed (P5). Every `stdo:` schema locator is parsed
before schema loading under URI scheme case-insensitivity and names the
same immutable cut as `constitution.stdo.basis`; spelling variation cannot
cross that basis. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias,
schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the
Product Definition (P6, P3).

`constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one
basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such
as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the
manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative
path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent
traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail
closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its
explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the
first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced;
the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay
project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all
existing bytes as an exact prefix. The bootstrap routes agents to the
applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning
sources; it can neither restate nor override them (P6, P3, P5).

Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as
version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals:
`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`,
`site-packages`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `target`, `.gradle`, `.tox`,
`.nox`, `.cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`,
`__pycache__`, `.genesis` and `.stdo`. A discovered Product Definition may
not itself be a symlink. These exclusions are discovery law, not evidence
that an excluded tree lacks another independently governed Product (P5,
P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F4.%20Shared%20installed%20release%20basis%20and%20toolchain%20manager","start_line":225}],"label":"Selected installed Product basis"}}}

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ca69fb183db64514704157409ebe758d"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:634ec16a1e1fc53db0bc5fcf70167e34","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":577,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md","quote":"### Review findings and bug items

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FReview%20findings%20and%20bug%20items","start_line":536},{"end_line":335,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md","quote":"### Result and triage projection

Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
and stay distinct values even where a
Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6).

The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).

| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
|---|---|---|
| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
severity alone (P6, P2).

The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
§3).

Recording the assessment is a separate artifact effect. Where the activation
grants it, the assessor may write the exact named findings carrier under
[TICKETS §4 Review findings and bug items](TICKETS.md#review-findings-and-bug-items).
That grant adds no candidate-repair authority or acquisition route. A review
has covered its declared subject only when every planned predicate has been
evaluated or lawfully removed from that subject; a partial return preserves
the unperformed coverage. Closing the review activity does not satisfy a
falsified or unresolved work claim (P6, P5).

Purpose and material relation: every configuration keeps severity,
priority, boundary effect and disposition separate. The rule applies to any
assessor and decision owner; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md)
binds its Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EVALUATION.md#EVALUATION%2F4.%20Review%20results%2FResult%20and%20triage%20projection","start_line":281}],"statement":"One review with findings uses one report, unless a sufficient existing direct carrier already supplies the exact record; no findings require no bug report and direct work gains no redundant ticket. Bind report path/identity, source linkage, visibility and exact report-write grant before writing. Reviewer may create only that granted report, not repair the candidate or change Product priority. Track open, fixed and verified separately, retain failing-before/passing-after and required independent evidence, and preserve restricted visibility through all links and projections.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Bind report path/identity, source linkage, visibility and exact report-write grant before writing. Reviewer may create only that granted report, not repair the candidate or change Product priority. Track open, fixed and verified separately, retain failing-before/passing-after and required independent evidence, and preserve restricted visibility through all links and projections.

These cases apply [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §9](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#product-composition-contract)
and the [worked recursive example](examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md). Their
presence establishes no execution or whole-method qualification (P6).

| Case | Subject and mechanism | Required distinction |
|---|---|---|
| PC-C01 Resolution | A valid edge and isolated missing-target, wrong-identity, missing-anchor and missing-contract variants | Valid references resolve; each broken required reference or identity fails its mechanical check. This is not grant or semantic validation. |
| PC-C02 Standalone recursion | Enter B with its declared C/D closure, without enclosing A; D is also shared by A | B's scoped local outcome remains enterable; shared identity preserves separate use/authority coordinates. |
| PC-C03 Integrated outcome | B uses D1's AUD exponent 2 while A uses D2's exponent 3 | Local availability cannot satisfy the incompatible monetary join; the outer claim is withheld. |
| PC-C04 Replacement | Cbad keeps the interface but rounds prices; Dplus preserves AUD and adds JPY | Reject Cbad; retain only justified AUD applicability for Dplus; new JPY obligations and grants are separately selected. |
| PC-C05 Authority across depth | A→B and B→C, with no A access to C internals; two differently scoped paths to D | No transitive grant or union at D. Adequate encapsulated internals need no flattened direct edge. |
| PC-C06 Derived exposure | Allowed notes/tool output contain a forbidden donor algorithm; an approved behavioral export has separately established policy eligibility | The summary remains prohibited; allow the export only under both lawful authority and the receiver's information policy. |
| PC-C07 Exposure and host | Revocation follows delivery; mediated receipts coexist with an unrestricted shell route | Preserve prior exposure and hold the affected claim; deleting a file does not unexpose an actor, and partial logs do not prove isolation. |
| PC-C08 Adequacy and change | Same candidate bytes, current join evidence versus unresolved changed basis; an unrelated leaf stays valid | Distinct continuations survive the context; reassess affected reliance while retaining justified evidence and original historical subjects. |
| PC-C09 Cycles | B consumes immutable A0 fixtures versus B1/A1 waiting for each other's current acceptance | Explicit seeded work can proceed; a lead name alone cannot close an unexecutable prerequisite cycle. |

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:62c03e6b02ba6e5c63e0e2e4c0dad571"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:64012a9975e6cb04e58437544da6c919","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":350,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis
is the pair (P3):

```text
(immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)
```

The URI identifies one immutable annotated release cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status
and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8
JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line
endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path
order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible
rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).

The STDO Toolchain Manager is the bounded executable realisation that (P2,
P3):

- installs each immutable cut once in a shared, versioned release store;
- resolves logical `stdo://releases/...` URIs to verified installed bytes;
- inventories and verifies complete installed distributions;
- synchronises the exact basis already selected by a Product Definition;
- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a release-profile discovery
  route and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly
  accepted;
- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and
- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product
  Definitions.

The store may live at any machine-local path. Its registry maps logical
release URIs to installed paths and manifest digests and owns neither
Product selection nor method meaning. A consumer repository therefore needs
no project-local standards copy and no prescribed folder structure, and
several Product Definitions on one machine may select different installed
cuts concurrently (P3, P6). Every manager-owned component from the
configured store root downward is a physical directory or regular file of
its declared type; a symlink, junction, reparse point, device, socket or
other redirection or special entry fails closed. Verification inventories
every filesystem entry type, directories included, rejects any entry not
derived from the manifest's exact file paths, and never follows an
unmanifested alias (P5, P3).

`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.
`constitution.stdo.selector` is a `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery
route whose profile semantics are owned by [RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption).
An RC line resolves its mutable selector; a stable line resolves its exact
immutable cut without a second selector. Neither discovery nor the transport
source is operative authority.
`constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256`
are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).

The manager observes these command boundaries (P6, P5):

- `install` admits one explicitly named immutable release cut without changing
  any Product Definition;
- `sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by
  the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector;
- `adopt --dry-run` resolves the selected release profile and immutable cut, and
  presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest,
  current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic
  adoption-plan digest, without mutation;
- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit
  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound
  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes
  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses
  mutation;
- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with
  respect to Product Definitions; and
- fleet adoption emits, and requires explicit acceptance of, one aggregate
  plan digest over every per-definition plan; all fleet writes require
  explicit whole-selection authorisation and infer no composition or
  inheritance from directory nesting.

Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag-to-commit mismatch, manifest-digest
mismatch, missing, extra or changed installed members, ambiguous Product
Definition discovery, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, URI escape,
physical store redirection, undeclared filesystem entry types and malformed
bootstrap markers fail closed (P5). Every `stdo:` schema locator is parsed
before schema loading under URI scheme case-insensitivity and names the
same immutable cut as `constitution.stdo.basis`; spelling variation cannot
cross that basis. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias,
schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the
Product Definition (P6, P3).

`constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one
basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such
as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the
manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative
path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent
traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail
closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its
explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the
first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced;
the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay
project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all
existing bytes as an exact prefix. The bootstrap routes agents to the
applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning
sources; it can neither restate nor override them (P6, P3, P5).

Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as
version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals:
`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`,

not itself be a symlink. These exclusions are discovery law, not evidence
that an excluded tree lacks another independently governed Product (P5,

clauses.statement: Record every ambiguity outcome. resolved → satisfied only for a recorded decision under policy permitting lawful probabilistic processing or human adjudication. carried → falsified for resolution when policy permits continuation with known open ambiguity; retain a residual naming resolving evidence or decision. escalated → out_of_frame when policy/risk appetite reserves decision to human authority absent from the step; name it. blocked → falsified when unresolved ambiguity and policy or hard stop halt work; name the halting condition and what lifts it. Carried and blocked are known openness, not evidence-indeterminate resolution. Preserve their domain details, and never support a dependent claim as if carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity were resolved.

Require explicit owner authorization and a carrier naming exact source/target concept refs and context identities; kind; direction and material lawful inverse; preserved/changed meaning, loss/refusal conditions; both semantic owners without authority transfer; both selected bases; scope/provenance; lifecycle/invalidation. The owner is distinct from the owning clause resolved by a concept reference. Meaning change/narrowing/loss cannot be called import. Equivalence needs governing-authority equality, not spelling or opposite translations. Disambiguation neither equates concepts nor imports by itself. No kind widens authority. Specialisation additionally specifies exact target, preserved/narrowed meaning, excluded source instances and absent/lawful inverse; its label alone establishes nothing. The source relates these kinds to AC-012 without making that reference an executed calculus operation.

It defines the
current goals for the active body of work before repricing deeper
constitutional layers. It works from intent before implementation. It
defines the current product definition in explicit present-tense terms
before decomposing it into detailed requirements. It defines the full
constitutional what in requirements, not merely a feature list. It prefers
declaring desired truth and lawful boundaries over prescribing step-by-step
imperative procedure. It makes design the explicit structural bridge
between requirements and code. It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent. It treats
spec-driven development as a disambiguation pipeline: each major gate
reduces the space of lawful interpretations before downstream realisation
proceeds.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F2.%20The%20chain%2FManifesto","start_line":276}],"label":"Specification-driven method"}}}

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:f8330f7c47820f3f98091902db96e2c3"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:6c5c82d1fd18416de2dc0187b8ba484b","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":397,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Exact-cut qualification

Qualification binds (P6, P3):

- the Project Release Namespace, qualified immutable release ref, annotated tag
  object, peeled commit, repository tree, Project Subtree root and tree,
  and declared Product member set;
- the exact release-scoped claim bytes;
- the governing Product and release basis;
- each claimed property and its observation boundary;
- evidence subjects, owner verdicts and unresolved gaps; and
- the complete successor relation to the declared predecessor (§9).

Evidence matches the claim. Source success does not prove packaged or
installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic
behaviour; artifact presence does not prove usability unless presence is
the exact claim (P6, P1; EVALUATION §1 is the generic claim law).

A cut is accepted only when the required exact-cut review and operator
checks are complete and the human authority accepts that exact subject. If
review requires a qualifying-byte change, the verdict stays on its original
subject and the applicable successor rule is used. Acceptance does not move
an immutable tag or create another final carrier (P6, P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FExact-cut%20qualification","start_line":375},{"end_line":719,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Acceptance criteria

A release cut may be accepted when (P6, P3):

- proportionate prepublication qualification passed for the declared subject;
- independent exact-cut review passed where required;
- required operator review is complete;
- the intended release scope and successor relation are stable;
- release-scoped assets accurately describe the exact cut;
- all release-blocking gaps, including the findings that block promotion
  under [EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion),
  are closed or the claimed scope is explicitly narrowed; and
- the human Product authority accepted the exact immutable cut identity.

Each criterion is a mandatory gate in the sense of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse):
it applies irrespective of any selection of checks after a change, and
retained evidence satisfies it only under the validity conditions stated
there (P6).

Acceptance attaches to that immutable cut identity. It neither advances
nor rolls back the version-line selector. Consumer adoption separately
evaluates the exact latest target presented by the channel and mutates
only after its digest-bound plan is accepted (P6, P3; EVALUATION §5 is
the generic acceptance law).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F8.%20Acceptance%2FAcceptance%20criteria","start_line":695},{"end_line":733,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### External qualification dependencies

Some claims depend on external backends, transports or operator-facing
services outside the local carrier. Such a dependency may remain out of
Product for carrier and migration classification while still blocking the
dependent release claim (P6, P5).

A clean skip caused by an unhealthy external dependency is an evaluation
not performed, which has no result
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed). It may
preserve correct Product classification, but it cannot establish that the
dependent capability passed. The claim is either qualified against a
healthy dependency or narrowed before acceptance (P6, P5).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F8.%20Acceptance%2FExternal%20qualification%20dependencies","start_line":721},{"end_line":797,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"## 9. Successor baseline conservation (STDO-UP-015)

A successor identifies the exact predecessor immutable cut whose semantic
claims it evolves. That origin remains immutable for the candidate. Every
predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor receives one semantic
disposition (P4b, P3, P6):

- conserved: the successor retains the claim;
- superseded: an accepted successor relation replaces it;
- intentionally removed: current Product authority removes it; or
- not applicable: it has no successor effect, with a bounded reason.

Evidence for a disposition is retained or reassessed under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse):
a `conserved` reading made on an earlier successor text applies to a later
one only where the owning text and the consumer bindings that carry it
are unchanged, or the change is shown not to affect the claim (P3, P6).

An unresolved disposition blocks qualification of the affected claim.
Conservation is semantic: patch absence does not prove loss when a
successor-native realisation preserves behaviour, and naming or code
similarity does not prove conservation without relevant evidence (P6,
P1). The comparison that decides `conserved` is made on the same material
case, scope and authority: what must happen, what may happen, what is
prohibited, and what follows when a trigger, exception or required
premise is absent, in the owning text and in the consumer bindings that
apply it, with the counterexamples that would expose a changed decision.
Modal wording is judged by that meaning: indicative wording can state a
binding law, and rewriting "must" or "shall" is neither conservation nor
supersession by itself; an obligation stays obligatory, a preference
stays a preference, and every permitted exception and scope condition
survives, or the claim is not conserved. A statement that a whole
package's wording is equivalent establishes none of this for any claim
(P6, P1). A `conserved` disposition recorded
before this test applied is re-evaluated under it before the affected
claim qualifies; until then its standing is `unresolved`.

Each disposition is a claim the successor makes about one predecessor
claim ([EVALUATION §1](EVALUATION.md#1-claims)), not a result value; its
predicate is its value's wording above. It is distinct from the decision
owner's disposition of an assessed candidate
([ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition)), which is an
acceptance result. Qualification evaluates each
disposition on evidence and records a value of the core result algebra
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) with that predicate.
An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result: in the
qualification of the affected claim it is a planned assessment without a
closed result, which is why it blocks that qualification
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Gaps). Purpose and material relation: a recorded disposition establishes
nothing until it is evaluated, so no disposition stands as a result (P6,
P5).

Where a maintenance or support line may affect retained claims, the
release basis identifies the watched source, observation boundary,
inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive
semantic disposition at material integration and exact-cut qualification.
The consumer owns its record, branch strategy, comparison and proof
mechanism (P4b, P6).

[EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance) states what acceptance
requires of the disposition record; it applies this section and is not
part of it (P4b, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F9.%20Successor%20baseline%20conservation%20%28STDO-UP-015%29","start_line":735}],"statement":"Acceptance requires the selected exact-cut properties, applicable operator and qualification evidence, and owning acceptance of the exact Product subject. Retain external qualification dependencies and unresolved claims. A byte change leaves old verdicts on their old subjects and requires a new immutable cut with affected reassessment. Successor support demonstrates conservation of predecessor capabilities or explicit lawful replacement/withdrawal dispositions; labels and inventories alone establish none of those claims.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Acceptance requires the selected exact-cut properties, applicable operator and qualification evidence, and owning acceptance of the exact Product subject. Retain external qualification dependencies and unresolved claims. A byte change leaves old verdicts on their old subjects and requires a new immutable cut with affected reassessment. Successor support demonstrates conservation of predecessor capabilities or explicit lawful replacement/withdrawal dispositions; labels and inventories alone establish none of those claims.

The issuer checks activation identity, exact subject/basis, result variant,
evidence scope and invalidators before relying on the return. It acquires
only the return projection its own frame permits; a link to a full artifact
does not authorize reading it. A digest authenticates bytes, not their claims.

Reconcile an effect whose completion or end remains unknown before retry or
any dependent action (`ACTIVATION` §3 Effects and §5). A timeout, missing
message or lost context is not evidence that no effect occurred. Retain valid
progress; do not replay a step merely because its actor changed.

Apply the governing result/disposition relation and determine whether the
exact candidate requires independent review. Issue `stdo-review` separately
where required. Reviewer severity remains its technical assessment; the
decision owner assigns priority and boundary effect within its grant
(`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §12 steps 4–7). Do not turn a closed result into implicit
authority to repair, accept, publish or start the next stage.

A proposed next action is not an executable activation. Before calling it
already authorized or issuing it, bind the actual operation grant and the
settled subject/pass grouping required by that contract. If either is missing,
return the proposal and exact unresolved binding; do not presume a Writer grant
or combine unsettled passes. This checks the existing intake, not a new gate.

For an admitted sequence, each continuation uses the previous closed result
and current bindings. Retain the boundaries the contract actually declares:
neither a new human check-in at every pass nor review only at the end is a
universal rule. Refresh affected bindings on material change, not every
unchanged status observation (`ACTIVATION` §1 Roles and delegation; §7).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FEvaluate%20The%20Return","start_line":169}],"statement":"Acquire only the return projection allowed to the consumer; a full-artifact link is not a read grant. Bind the actual operation grant and settled subject/pass grouping before calling a next action already authorized. Refresh material changes; impose neither an extra human check-in every pass nor review-only-at-end as universal rules.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

A context exists only through owning-authority declaration of stable identity, owner, selected basis and semantic scope; a consumer defines inside it only through explicit owner relation. Resolve by scope/nearest explicit context, then exact basis/applicable authorities, then admitted local definitions/imported refs, then all applicable authorized overrides/disambiguations, admitting only one remaining concept. Equal spelling/capitalization/shape/location/nesting/actor/implementation establishes no equal meaning, identity, equivalence, inheritance or authority; differing spelling proves no difference. Filename, heading, index, glossary, schema value, URI, repository, prompt, actor or proximity cannot accidentally declare context. Relations require the semantic address or explicit authorized relation.

clauses.statement: Workspace, ledger and evaluator attention: The governed work pair comprises mutable workspace W and immutable ledger L of closure-relevant work over W, anchored and ordered by immutable event spine E. Evaluator work Ev evaluates declared L snapshots. L records admitted callout basis, observed deltas, file refs, digests, execution evidence, touched obligations, claims, evaluator inputs/outputs and admission status, rather than copying W. Ledger attention is a structural analogy: typed, immutable, lineage-constrained, policy-bounded and replayable, without a transformer-attention implementation dependency.

The alternate §17 row records a shared label, a use locator and owning clause. A locator only identifies where to look. Owner clause plus selected basis identifies candidate meaning; the occurrence supplies governed scope. Unresolved context or owning clause makes a row invalid and cannot be repaired by the index.

clauses.statement: ODD domain product: Configured GTL/ABG domain product whose published graph functions construct typed domain assets. clauses.statement: Every accepted atom declares its admitted domain and governs every admitted instance within it. Later use composes/parameterises it, never locally forks, shadows, specialises or reinterprets it. An in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and re-enters its design boundary, not feature-local replacement. An undeclared domain leaves the atom a candidate unable to supply Prime acceptance/conformance. Atomic-function Prime is not established until the complete candidate family is contracted.

clauses.statement: Module role taxonomy: Recommended module roles: carrier modules define typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells perform emission, publication, network, subprocess, persistence or delivery effects; projections derive read models or reports from authoritative truth; bindings/adapters translate external boundaries to internal carriers without inventing law; constructors/materialisers write generated or built artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Module boundaries constrain traversal reasoning under finite context, attention and time, expose ownership, consumption, emissions and sufficient proof, and make recurrence visible for library consolidation.

These are work conditions, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. The cited actor-change premise permits reacquisition of declared sources, not private memory.

It is not a rewritten operating procedure, newly invented decision algorithm or self-validating authority.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":131,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Issue

1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
   execution contract for every question.
2. **Project the admitted unit.** The packet is a reference/verbatim projection
   of that unit, not a rewritten operating procedure. Use the compact bindings
   below or their equivalent in the existing carrier. Each binding points to
   an exact admitted source clause; any inlined grant or condition is quoted
   verbatim with its origin. The recipient applies the same skill to those
   bindings. Do not rewrite the skill or derive a new decision algorithm.

   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
   |---|---|
   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
   | Unresolved required binding | Missing source, verification or capability; return its cause and required re-entry instead of an executable packet |

   Preserve conditional grants as conditions. Do not add inferred conditionals,
   read/effect grants, retry permissions or closure rules. An effect grant alone
   does not grant acquisition of its output. For example, project these as
   separate existing clauses, without filling a missing clause by inference:

   ```text
   Effect and its condition: <exact admitted clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Output acquisition: <exact permitted output clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Retry / result / stop: <exact admitted clause references or verbatim quotes>
   ```

   Put any proposed new interpretation outside the execution packet and return
   for its required re-entry. Calling it a derivation or a safety rule does not
   make it an inherited grant.

   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence
   tools, use those contracts and retain their actual receipts. Do not replace
   required computation with a hand-written claim or invent tool success. A
   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces
   source/semantic judgment. Tooling availability creates no new dependency.
3. **Check the acquisition the packet prescribes.** Consider command output,
   diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded context as well as direct reads.
   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames
   that command prints is a contradiction. Resolve it before dispatch using
   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.
4. **Bind the host and dispatch.** Apply [Host Binding](#host-binding) and send
   the packet to the selected actor with the instruction to invoke this same
   skill as its recipient. Do not transfer ambient conversation by default
   where the frame excludes it. Record the dispatch/activation identity and
   actual mechanism in the existing carrier through its authorized Writer.
   If no available authorized mechanism meets the required boundary, retain
   the packet and return “not dispatched” with the missing capability. A
   prepared packet is not an active Worker or a work result.

Keep packet readiness separate from returning a response. If a required
control/source verification or capability is unavailable, return the missing
binding and the applicable incomplete/refused outcome; do not issue an
executable intake or label it ready, complete or closed. “Prepared, not
dispatched” applies only when the packet is sufficient and dispatch remains
unperformed; its consumer still checks the exact intake before using it.

The issuer remains in its coordinating frame. It acquires no mutation grant
by arranging the work. Where one same-actor role transition is sufficient and
permitted, bind and record that transition explicitly; do not pretend it
cleared information already acquired (`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §6 and §17).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FIssue","start_line":49}],"label":"Projection of an admitted unit"}}}

clauses.statement: Projection of an admitted unit: A handoff packet is an exact reference or verbatim projection of an already admitted unit and grants, with source provenance and recipient-eligible content. It is not a rewritten operating procedure, newly invented decision algorithm or self-validating authority.

That intake binds permitted inputs, operations, exclusions, Product basis, actual host limits and result consumer before subject discovery or effects. Issuer and recipient access are separate.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":47,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Control Intake

This is the first path for **issuer, recipient and direct work**. The issuer's
access is its own grant, not the Worker's. A coordinator cannot inspect the
subject merely because its Worker may do so.

1. Read the exact own contract/intake named in the request first. Bind its
   role, allowed control inputs, excluded information, operations and return
   route. Do not begin with directory listings, recursive discovery, memory
   search or neighbouring files. If the request supplies only a packet, its
   authorized control routes are the initial limit; check them against their
   authoritative grant before dependent acquisition. If no exact control
   route is supplied, use only the request's authorized discovery boundary;
   an unresolved boundary returns for clarification rather than being guessed.
2. Read the named Product Definition, accepted frame basis and applicable
   grant/admission through those control routes. An exact definition path
   removes the need to inventory surrounding directories. Verify it with the
   [compact source reader](#compact-source-acquisition) or the already-declared
   equivalent tool; do not print the manager's complete member inventory into
   the actor context. Retain the actual verification identity/result.
3. Check the active host binding before relying on an acquisition exclusion:
   what context is already supplied, which tools and scopes are actually

For each directed relation, the `relation` authority and referenced `contracts`
state, directly or by exact reference:

1. Source and target Product identities and roles; the consumed capability,

2. The existing owners and grants for each material operation: acquisition,

   role label records no grant by itself.

   obligations and evidence; restrictions on implementation material and derived
   information where applicable.
4. The acting principals or binding rule, task/phase scope, permitted delegation,
   return consumer, stop/refusal conditions and revocation/invalidation route.

clauses.statement: Required representative observations cover every claimed function/failure relation: declare derives a frame set from governed workspace, outcome, practices, capability envelopes, evaluation inventory, authority and residual boundary, refusing missing authority/evaluation basis; activate succeeds on exact subject/basis and capable actor, while stale, ambiguous, topology-mismatched, unauthorised or capability-incompatible cases refuse or return applicable closed pressure; evaluate exhibits satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, material sensitivity and established irrelevance stability; conjoin decides compatible closed results by declared rule, returns conflict for conflict, indeterminate for mandatory indeterminacy, invalid_basis for basis mismatch, and cause-appropriate declared veto/deferral outcomes without flattening frame meaning; translate preserves coordinates/provenance, states loss and refuses identity/basis/authority/equality mismatch; audit_coverage maps evaluation, interaction, semantic/operation/decision authority, failure, capability and required independent/assurance-independent coverage to capable frames or explicit residuals, never closing by artifact/actor count; revise produces declared deltas for historical failure, topology/evidence/capability changes and identifies every affected prior activation/result/conjunction/coverage claim; result consumption needs no hidden context or authority, otherwise output insufficiency is reconstructability failure; material composition declares composition, material order, closure, failure and authority conservation, while cases needing none stay uncomposed.
