{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:e6ecd7b7f58c276e143d2ee5d1b991d2"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:7643c339894a358dbd9b069d7796feda","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":218,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### Foundation to law

This member is material family F9, the `a_c` calculus. The table below
shows which of its rules follow from which premises, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
which also states the standing of the consequences. Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) model applications may construct values or proposed successors as
  well as decide predicates; some operations are determined by closed
  computation, while others need bounded probabilistic processing or
  explicit human adjudication.

| Premises, with standing | Consequence that follows | Rule in this member that states it | Added domain or policy choice, and its owner | Pillar |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 (independent), P6 (independent); (i) | By P1 a model is a representation of its subject, by P6 encoding and interpreting are separate authorities, and by (i) a governed system is represented by a finite model, so the calculus is derived one way from the method's principles and is separate from its application: interpreting a subject and encoding a model are distinct relations, and no model, carrier, proof tool or successful application amends the calculus or the principles | [§1](#1-position), [Derivation provenance](#derivation-provenance) | the concept identity, its bounded context and the name `a_c`: this member | 6, 10 |
| P2 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P2 the calculus serves only the form a model needs, and by P6 a status needs its own proof, so the calculus governs the form of a symbolic model and claims no status that a separately identified proof has not established; it chooses no subject vocabulary or materiality, supplies no semantic acceptance, selects no carrier and executes nothing | [§1](#1-position), the claims it does not make; [Scope](#scope); [Exclusions](#exclusions) | none | 10 |
| P3 (independent), P5 (derived from P0 and P6); (i) | By P3 every element binds one identity and basis, by P5 an unclosed population would leave results undecided, and by (i) the model is finite, so every model belongs to one closed, finite signature; every record occurs once in one population of eight fixed record families, every identity resolves once, locally or through one declared external relation, and an unknown, hidden, duplicated or dangling element refuses | [§2](#2-signature), [§3](#3-typed-records), [AC-001](#ac-001-closed-signature), [AC-003](#ac-003-reference-closure) | the eight core record kinds and the fields of each record: this member; a model family's sorts, value domains, reference domains and admissible kinds: the owning signature | 3, 10 |
| P3 (independent), P4a (independent) | By P3 identity is declared and scoped, and by P4a relations compose only by the types they declare, so identity is scoped, so equal spelling, payload, position or carrier establishes none; a relation is lawful only between the sorts its kind admits, with its required qualifiers, and its direction is material unless declared symmetric | [AC-002](#ac-002-scoped-identity), [AC-004](#ac-004-relation-typing) | each relation kind's sorts, qualifiers and any declared symmetry: the owning signature | 2, 3, 10 |
| P6 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2), P3 (independent) | By P6 authority is not transferred by handling a record, by P3 every record binds its basis, and by P4b recorded facts persist, so copying, interpreting, encoding, evaluating or transporting a record transfers no authority, and every record, model and result binds an exact basis, mixed bases only under an owned composite-basis relation | [AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation), [AC-006](#ac-006-basis-coherence) | each composite-basis relation: the owner it names | 9, 10 |
| P5 (derived from P0 and P6), P6 (independent) | By P5 a value decides only what its evidence establishes, and by P6 a judgment is separate from its acceptance, so a constraint's judgment and every outcome of an operation of this member read as exactly one core value for a named predicate; no failed, missing or undecided result and no stop becomes success; a refusal's cause is part of its value, a demonstrated violation it names mapping to falsified and a condition of the basis the operation acts on to invalid_basis | [AC-007](#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal); [§5](#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds), the stop algebra | the cause of a refusal that names both a demonstrated violation and a condition of the basis, `refusal(constraint)`, with the basis condition reported beside it as its own invalid_basis result: this member, in AC-007; the predicate language and judgment of each constraint kind: the owning signature; further stop values and their refinement: the signature's stop contract; the stop mapping of one traversal: its record, under §5 | 3, 9, 10 |
| P1 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P1 a difference in representation is not a difference in meaning unless declared, and by P6 latitude is granted only by its owner, so two values differ only through a declared latitude or transformation relation; silence is not latitude, and latitude grants no authority beyond its owner, scope, basis and invalidation law | [Latitude](#latitude), [AC-008](#ac-008-explicit-latitude) | each latitude record: its owner | 6, 10 |
| P4b (derived from P0 and P2), P6 (independent) | By P4b an unresolved condition persists until disposed, and by P6 only an authority disposes it, so a material uncertainty stays in the model until an authorised disposition; no projection, compression, interpretation or encoding erases a residual, and absence from a projection is not resolution | [Residual](#residual), [AC-009](#ac-009-residual-conservation) | each residual kind's domains: the owning signature; each disposition: the competent authority | 9, 10 |
| P0 (recovered), P2 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2) | By P0 an actor holds a bounded set of records, by P2 it needs those its task requires, and by P4b established records persist, so material closure is the least lawful record closure, defined only on exact inputs and claiming no minimal size or cost; a projection contains the closure, records its seams and never silently trims a required member to fit a carrier or capability budget | [AC-010](#ac-010-material-closure), [AC-011](#ac-011-projection) | the seed set and the relation family: the evaluation that applies them, for a step [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) | 7, 10 |
| P3 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P3 a basis is immutable once bound, and by P6 a change to its meaning needs an owned relation, so an overlay adds records without mutating its basis; override, disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation or translation exists only as a typed relation with its authority | [AC-012](#ac-012-overlay) | each overlay relation: its owner | 2, 10 |
| P4b (derived from P0 and P2), P3 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P4b a transformation's effects are facts that persist, by P3 they bind exact records, and by P6 their classification is accountable, so a transformation proves a closed delta over local records and external resolutions, each classified once as preserved or removed, with preservation shown by byte or typed equality; its result is a proposed successor that admits nothing | [AC-013](#ac-013-transformation) | each transformation, with its operation authority and preservation relation: the owner of the transformation record | 3, 4, 10 |
| P6 (independent), P3 (independent) | By P6 judgment and promotion are separate authorities, and by P3 a judgment binds its exact subject, so a judgment points to an unchanged subject, and promotion is a separate relation between that subject and its admission or acceptance judgment | [AC-014](#ac-014-judgment-separation) | none | 9, 10 |
| P4a (independent), P3 (independent), P6 (independent); (iii) | By P4a a traversal composes only through its declared contract, by P3 it binds one functor kind, by P6 its authority is separate, and by (iii) applications include construction and judgment under different processing conditions, so a traversal is a typed contract applied under exactly one functor kind; total deterministic processing, bounded probabilistic construction and human adjudication are distinct kinds, each distinct from actor, executor and domain operation, and the name asserts no categorical functor; traversals compose only under typed composition, which keeps both identities and every intermediate fact | [§5](#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds), [AC-015](#ac-015-functor-classification), [AC-016](#ac-016-typed-composition) | F_D purpose extending to deterministic construction, its total-domain requirement and the unchanged-subject evaluation profile: §5; the functor kinds permitted for each traversal: the owning signature; the order of kinds in an application: that application | 4, 8, 10 |
| P1 (independent), P6 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2); (ii), (iii) | By P1 an interpretation is a proposal about meaning, by P6 its acceptance is separate, by P4b its provenance persists, and by (ii) and (iii) models are interpreted from exact subjects and partly checked mechanically, so an interpretation proposes a model that its construction does not accept; every admitted record has exact provenance or is identified as model-local, every evaluated subject declaration has a disposition, structural success is evidence for semantic review and never a substitute, and a valid model satisfies every applicable law | [§6](#6-interpretation-and-models), [AC-017](#ac-017-interpretation-fidelity), [AC-018](#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation), [AC-019](#ac-019-valid-model) | the interpretation contract and the semantic selection and acceptance authority: the downstream authority of the subject; a decision contract for a semantic subset: the model that supplies it | 6, 10 |
| P3 (independent), P6 (independent); (ii) | By P3 the calculus, a model and a carrier are distinct objects, by P6 each has its own proof obligation, and by (ii) a model may be encoded in several carriers, so the calculus, an interpreted model and an encoded carrier have separate identities, judgments and proof obligations; encoding needs an accepted judgment over the unchanged model, and a downstream success ratifies no upstream layer | [§7](#7-layers), [AC-020](#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation) | Product status of a layer: the external authority that selects and releases it | 6, 10 |
| P3 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P3 an edition binds its exact published bytes, and by P6 its identity record is a separate authority, so an edition's identity is an external record over its published bytes and its derivation clauses, created after the bytes exist; interpreted and encoded identities bind their upstream identities, and judgments stay outside the identities they judge | [§8](#8-calculus-identity) | the record shape, RFC 8785 canonicalisation, SHA-256 and the order of principle references: this member; the record grammar and issuance authority for interpreted and encoded identities: the owning Product; issuance of this edition's record: its release, under [RELEASE](RELEASE.md) | 2, 10 |
| P2 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P2 the calculus serves applications without choosing for them, and by P6 selection and release belong to their owners, so the calculus selects, constructs, accepts or releases no concrete interpretation or carrier, and an application's import, translation or specialisation stays external to it | [Application boundary](#application-boundary), [External imports and specialisations](#external-imports-and-specialisations) | each application's subject, interpretation, carrier and imports: the downstream authority that owns the application | 1, 10 |
| P0 (recovered), P2 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2), P6 (independent); (i), (iii) | P0 bounds what an actor can hold and P2 fixes the task's destination, so an actor needs the constraints of one task, not the whole model, and the material closure and projection of AC-010 and AC-011 supply them as a constraint surface. P4b keeps every residual until an authorised disposition, so unresolved conditions travel with the surface and block the work that depends on them; P6 keeps authority, evidence and acceptance apart, so a surface grants no authority and its validity, fidelity and sufficiency for a task are separate claims | [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces) | the interpretation used and which one is current: the downstream authority of the subject; the seed set and relation family of a task: the activation that applies them, for a step [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope); a mechanical projection: a separately selected checking contract | 7, 10 |
| P6 (independent) | By P6 a claim about this member holds only on evidence that tests each law, so a review or qualification of this member covers each law with positive and refusal cases, and no example, checker, model or carrier qualifies a law beyond the claim it evaluates | [§10](#10-conformance-obligations) | the ten obligations as the minimum coverage: this member; a policy of this member: each law is covered by positive and refusal cases | 9, 10 |

Consumers of these rows, where an actor enters them (FOUNDATIONS §3
Foundation to law, Consumers), one list per row, each consumer linked to
its own locus:

- Row 1, position and derivation provenance: [§8 Calculus identity](#8-calculus-identity), whose `derivation_basis` names the governing clauses identified under Derivation provenance and keeps their premise role distinct from the published calculus member; the family tables of [ODD](ODD.md#foundation-to-law), [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#foundation-to-law) and [WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md#foundation-to-law), whose rows import F9.
- Row 2, scope and exclusions: [SPEC_METHOD §11 Build-tenant binding](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding), rule 6, where a representation in a_c prescribes no executor and establishes no execution conformance by itself; otherwise no separate consumer applies: the claims the calculus does not make are limits on this member's own rules, and what an application selects, accepts or executes is that application's under [Application boundary](#application-boundary), traced in row 17.
- Row 3, closed signature, typed records and reference closure: [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE Imported calculus boundary](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#imported-calculus-boundary), which instantiates its signature over `RecordKind_ac` and `Population_M` unchanged and refuses hidden records and ambiguous references, [Closed semantic-object sorts](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#closed-semantic-object-sorts), where every `_ref` resolves exactly once under AC-003, and [Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds), where a dangling reference refuses under AC-003; [AC-007](#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal), whose `refusal(constraint)` names a missing record family and a dangling reference; [AC-019](#ac-019-valid-model), clause 2.
- Row 4, scoped identity and relation typing: [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), whose objects carry identity under AC-002 and whose predicates and dependencies include the typed relations of AC-004; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminator 22. IDENTITY's lead records that AC-002 applies the scoped identity of IDENTITY §2 and applies nothing of AC-002.
- Row 5, authority conservation and basis coherence: [AC-007](#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal), whose `refusal(basis)` names mixed bases with no composite-basis relation; [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), where the surface grants no authority and binds the calculus basis as a separate coordinate; [AC-019](#ac-019-valid-model), clause 2; [§5](#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds), the kind-specific no-authority application of AC-005. No section of another member applies them: the generic rules they bind to a_c records are FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds', RF-005's and RF-006's, each applied by its own consumers.
- Row 6, constraint judgment and the stop algebra: [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds), which maps its stops under AC-007 and refines them under the parent-value rule of §5; [AC-010](#ac-010-material-closure), [AC-011](#ac-011-projection), [AC-013](#ac-013-transformation), [AC-015](#ac-015-functor-classification), [§6 Interpretation and models](#6-interpretation-and-models) and [§7 Layers](#7-layers), each of which takes the core value of its stops or judgments under AC-007; [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), required results and condition 2.
- Row 7, latitude: [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), permitted freedom and condition 1; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminators 17 and 18. The generic rule over any two values is FOUNDATIONS §4 Algebra, Latitude's, which cites AC-008 as provenance only.
- Row 8, residual conservation: [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), unresolved conditions and condition 2; [AC-013](#ac-013-transformation), where material residuals remain in the successor unless an authorised disposition is in the transformation evidence; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminator 16.
- Row 9, material closure and projection: [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope), steps 1 and 2, and [§3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation), `closure_unresolved`; [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), whose surface is the projection over the material closure of a task's seed set; [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#traversal_occurrence), its lead, which keeps its `Projection` record apart from an AC-011 projection. The rule that no reference trims a required member is FOUNDATIONS §4 Algebra, Reference versus body's, which AC-011 applies.
- Row 10, overlay: [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#5-bounded-context-semantic-resolution), which relates its four semantic-resolution kinds to the typed relations AC-012 names; [AC-019](#ac-019-valid-model), clause 3.
- Row 11, transformation: [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Conservation accounting; [REFERENCE_FRAME §6 Evidence or coordinate translation](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#evidence-or-coordinate-translation), where a translation represented in a_c is recorded in the fields of AC-013; [SPEC_METHOD §11 Build-tenant binding](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding), rule 7; [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), admissible operations.
- Row 12, judgment separation: [Constraint surfaces](#constraint-surfaces), evidence; [§7 Layers](#7-layers), where the acceptance judgment is over the unchanged model and neither judgment enters the identity of its subject; [§8 Calculus identity](#8-calculus-identity), where the semantic-acceptance and carrier-admission judgments point to unchanged identities and are embedded in neither. No section of another member applies it; EVALUATION §5 Acceptance states that a disposition is over an unchanged subject as its own rule and cites AC-014 as provenance only.

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ad5a9991023c1d724ad6a0df331b12ca"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:7715fec956660f5223e30edda07d78cd","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"An evaluation profile does not perform the domain construction it judges. This is the first path for **issuer, recipient and direct work**. The issuer's
access is its own grant, not the Worker's. A coordinator cannot inspect the

   role, allowed control inputs, excluded information, operations and return
   route. Do not begin with directory listings, recursive discovery, memory
   search or neighbouring files. If the request supplies only a packet, its
   authorized control routes are the initial limit; check them against their
   authoritative grant before dependent acquisition. If no exact control
   route is supplied, use only the request's authorized discovery boundary;
   an unresolved boundary returns for clarification rather than being guessed.
2. Read the named Product Definition, accepted frame basis and applicable
   grant/admission through those control routes. An exact definition path
   removes the need to inventory surrounding directories. Verify it with the

   equivalent tool; do not print the manager's complete member inventory into
   the actor context. Retain the actual verification identity/result.
3. Check the active host binding before relying on an acquisition exclusion:
   what context is already supplied, which tools and scopes are actually
   enabled, how new reads are confined or supervised, and how results return.
   Use exposed capabilities and the admitted run binding, not exploration of
   home/configuration files. A fresh session is not a read boundary. If the
   required capability is absent, unknown or already violated, stop the
   dependent activation with its cause; do not claim a clean frame and
   continue. The [host binding](#host-binding) states the specific limits.
4. Enter only the branch required by that bound role. Issuer follows Issue;
   recipient follows Receive; a sufficient direct task uses the ordinary
   skill. Read additional sources only for a material question and through
   the admitted routes. clauses.statement: Every performed evaluation returns one core value or exactly mapped refinement and records its evaluated predicate, core value and original domain outcome. Domain meaning remains with the defining member/profile/Product; consumers needing its distinctions read the domain outcome. Result standing concerns the predicate and differs from commitment standing: only satisfied establishes it, falsified establishes failure with its counterexample, and the other three establish neither and identify deciding evidence, missing relation/capability and its given owner, or basis repair. No mapping or refinement raises standing: failed/falsified or undecidable outcomes cannot become success; non-performance maps to no core value; unknown effect completion cannot become no effect or completion. Actors cannot report evaluations they did not perform. Failed, indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope and invalid-basis outcomes keep their declared outcomes rather than being coerced to satisfied.

Target project: The project built with an installed ODD product owns its business domain; one stdo_<label>.json definition per distinct product WHAT locating constitutional, local/collective reference-frame basis, realisation, work and composition surfaces; constitutional surfaces; one or more how.build_tenants realisation roots; domain outputs and evidence. Software examples include design, code, tests, documents and proof surfaces; other domains name their own artifacts.

Bounded design frame: A material design frame records governing frames and accepted relations, bounded affected relations, inherited invariants, crossing authority/composition seams and subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions. Global and local are relative to the selected frame. Governing frames form a constraint network and may be multiple rather than a mandatory hierarchy.

Source Project: Source Project, urn:stdo:concept:recursive-product-taxonomy:source-project, owned by FOUNDATIONS §2 in urn:stdo:bounded-context:recursive-product-taxonomy: a mutable workspace building the next release cut. PRODUCT.md is its product-definition surface, not a released Product.

The `stable-v1` profile publishes an immutable release directly as
`refs/tags/<project>/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Each numeric component is a
nonnegative decimal integer, with no leading zero except the single digit
`0`. The tag is annotated, targets a commit and contains exactly one
standalone annotation line (P3):

```text
STDO-Release-Profile: stable-v1
```

Its exact release declaration names the same stable cut, declared payload,
source selection and predecessor. The installed manifest records
`release.profile = "stable-v1"` alongside the complete identity of

An RC manifest retains its prior shape; adding stable support must not
change the canonical bytes of a historical release manifest (P3, P4b).

The stable coordinate is available only on a fresh version line with no
same-version RC tag in either the historical or project-qualified namespace
and no historical unqualified bare-version tag. The stable tag itself is
create-only. A same-line collision or a missing, duplicated or different
profile marker refuses stable acquisition; bare spelling or annotation alone
cannot turn an RC selector into an immutable cut (P3, P5).

There is no separate version-line selector or RC branch for this profile.
A channel `stdo://channels/<major>.<minor>.<patch>` may discover that exact
immutable stable tag; its cut ordinal is absent (`null`), and resolution
must verify the stable profile and complete identity. That channel route
creates neither another tag nor mutable alias semantics. Consumer adoption
still follows §4 (P3, P6).

A published stable tag never moves. Any change to its qualifying bytes
requires a new version and a new immutable cut, not an RC added to the
already stable line. Historical RC lines keep their selector semantics,
refs, objects, peels and URIs; this profile neither finalises nor renames
them. {"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:7273eee8de3f5344e030eac0d2fd8c38"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:814e0ce702aa1648a05b59502de64dbf","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":131,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Issue

1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
   execution contract for every question.
2. **Project the admitted unit.** The packet is a reference/verbatim projection
   of that unit, not a rewritten operating procedure. Use the compact bindings
   below or their equivalent in the existing carrier. Each binding points to
   an exact admitted source clause; any inlined grant or condition is quoted
   verbatim with its origin. The recipient applies the same skill to those
   bindings. Do not rewrite the skill or derive a new decision algorithm.

   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
   |---|---|
   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
   | Unresolved required binding | Missing source, verification or capability; return its cause and required re-entry instead of an executable packet |

   Preserve conditional grants as conditions. Do not add inferred conditionals,
   read/effect grants, retry permissions or closure rules. An effect grant alone
   does not grant acquisition of its output. For example, project these as
   separate existing clauses, without filling a missing clause by inference:

   ```text
   Effect and its condition: <exact admitted clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Output acquisition: <exact permitted output clause reference or verbatim quote>
   Retry / result / stop: <exact admitted clause references or verbatim quotes>
   ```

   Put any proposed new interpretation outside the execution packet and return
   for its required re-entry. Calling it a derivation or a safety rule does not
   make it an inherited grant.

   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence
   tools, use those contracts and retain their actual receipts. Do not replace
   required computation with a hand-written claim or invent tool success. A
   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces
   source/semantic judgment. Tooling availability creates no new dependency.
3. **Check the acquisition the packet prescribes.** Consider command output,
   diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded context as well as direct reads.
   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames
   that command prints is a contradiction. Resolve it before dispatch using
   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.
4. **Bind the host and dispatch.** Apply [Host Binding](#host-binding) and send
   the packet to the selected actor with the instruction to invoke this same
   skill as its recipient. Do not transfer ambient conversation by default
   where the frame excludes it. Record the dispatch/activation identity and
   actual mechanism in the existing carrier through its authorized Writer.
   If no available authorized mechanism meets the required boundary, retain
   the packet and return “not dispatched” with the missing capability. A
   prepared packet is not an active Worker or a work result.

Keep packet readiness separate from returning a response. If a required
control/source verification or capability is unavailable, return the missing
binding and the applicable incomplete/refused outcome; do not issue an
executable intake or label it ready, complete or closed. “Prepared, not
dispatched” applies only when the packet is sufficient and dispatch remains
unperformed; its consumer still checks the exact intake before using it.

The issuer remains in its coordinating frame. It acquires no mutation grant
by arranging the work. Where one same-actor role transition is sufficient and
permitted, bind and record that transition explicitly; do not pretend it
cleared information already acquired (`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §6 and §17).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FIssue","start_line":49}],"statement":"Check recipient eligibility for command output, diagnostics, logs, file lists and embedded information as well as direct reads. Resolve contradictions before dispatch through permitted alternatives or return to the owner; redaction after exposure does not undo acquisition. Use declared context/preflight/dispatch/evidence tools and retain actual bounded receipts when required. Bind the actual authorized host mechanism and actor; absent capability means not dispatched. Prepared-not-dispatched means packet sufficient but dispatch unperformed, never an active Worker result. Issuer stays in its own frame; a separately bound same-actor transition does not erase prior exposure.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Fix the same subject/basis and reports `X={S,F,I}`. Qualified records are
`H={hS,hF,hI}` and views `V={vS,vF,vI}`. Policy readouts are
`D={advance,block_falsified,block_indeterminate}`. The complete functions are:

| X | `build:X→H` | `view:H→V` | Both `j:H→D` and `h:V→D` read out |
|---|---|---|---|
| S | hS | vS | advance |
| F | hF | vF | block_falsified |
| I | hI | vI | block_indeterminate |

The three rows prove pointwise `j=h o view`. Arrow equality here is pointwise
finite-function equality; composition is ordinary composition and identities
return their inputs. The constant subject-only projection cannot factor j:
hS and hI share its output but require different readouts.

The following is a finite mathematical argument and executable structural
check, not a qualified categorical demonstration under FOUNDATIONS.
For the structural counterexample, take the finite chain category with
objects X,H,V,D and exactly the displayed generated function for each ordered
pair in that chain, including all identities and composites. There are ten
arrows; equality compares their endpoints and pointwise action. The target
terminal category has object `*` and only `id_*`. Send every source object
to `*` and every arrow to `id_*`: identities and composition are preserved,
yet that map cannot recover j's distinct readouts. The program exhausts
identity and associative composition checks for this bound fragment and
the terminal map. Those structural checks and the explicit counterexample
support their finite claims, not consumer adequacy of an arbitrary functor.
The full categorical demonstration still requires the applicable a_c
representation and supporting assessment under FOUNDATIONS; these executable
tables do not replace those obligations or discharge unresolved H1.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FFinite%20maps%20and%20consumer%20adequacy","start_line":155},{"end_line":209,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md","quote":"## Migration and comparison

conditions of RELEASE's first row within their exact domains and profiles;
this is author evidence, not independent acceptance. The transition and
reference-acquisition functions are finite mathematical fixtures, not additional
adopted a_c operations. An old evaluator with an undeclared clock dependency or missing
termination evidence fails new-kind qualification despite preserving its
subject. It takes the pending-evidence or unresolved row of
[RELEASE's migration relation](../RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration),
retaining its exact old edition. A future fuel-bounded repair has a distinct
traversal and exhaustion meaning. A kind never grants broader writes.

clauses.statement: Three inseparable duties concern one governed outcome. Attention management retains exact outcome/basis, Product-role map, evaluation inventory, dependencies, unresolved frontier, actor envelopes, mandate, triage policy and residual boundary, selecting the smallest dependency-ready set sufficient for the next decision within finite envelopes. Orchestration activates capable Workers/Reviewers/specialists, preserves exact subject/basis and consumes only closed results or declared translations. Action selection assigns priority/boundary effect, applies existing disposition and issues only already-authorised next actions. Executive need not hold the whole workspace or perform every evaluation; its role grants no Product meaning, implementation, mutation, acceptance, publication or other operation authority. Material effects remain with actors holding exact operation grants.

{"family":"relations","record":{"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:896c451b8821799c40dfc293b37ec770","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:relation-kind:governing:imports","owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","qualifiers":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":384,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"### Probabilistic compute

Probabilistic compute in this profile is bounded constructive work over
one declared vector or edge traversal, where the graph or runtime does not
fully determine the worker's internal solution path. One vector or edge
traversal is the bounded unit of probabilistic compute (P0).

Binding of the bounded step. FOUNDATIONS P0 lets a
profile bind the bounded step to its own traversal unit and names
[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this profile,
as the keeper of that binding. Direction: from the step of
FOUNDATIONS P0 to one declared ODD vector or edge traversal. Preserved
meaning: the step's selected context fits the actor's envelope, the
actor's internal path within the step is its own, and the traversal is
the admissible external space. Narrowed scope: one declared vector or edge
traversal of a published graph. Invalidation: a change to FOUNDATIONS P0,
to the vector's declaration or to the selected basis invalidates the
binding until it is evaluated again (P0, P1).

The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
states. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it
does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal
boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM
reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local
execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).

The classifications of work inside one traversal bind two profile
specialisations and one common import. Equal spelling alone establishes
none of those relations (P1, P3):

- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the
  bounded probabilistic worker turn. It specialises substrate-neutral
  lawful probabilistic processing: it keeps bounded non-human construction
  under declared policy and narrows that meaning to one graph traversal
  contract.
- `F_D` imports `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d` from
  [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
  in the exact complete STDO release selected by the application, including
  its immutable calculus edition. It adds the graph traversal's operation
  contract, scope and authority, not another definition of the kind.
  Existing evaluation and proof operations retain the unchanged-subject
  evaluation profile; admission and construction operations retain their
  own evidence contracts and grants. Use of the common kind is conditional
  on the total-domain eligibility assessment in
  [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). Domain-local
  optimization or validation moves no domain HOW into GTL, ABG or the
  framework and grants no broader consequences.
- `F_H` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`) is the shorthand for
  explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared
  authority and ambiguity policy. It specialises the substrate-neutral
  human-adjudication concept and grants a human no ambient traversal,
  semantic or closure authority.

F_P and F_H are the two declared specialisations that PROFILES §1 requires. The F_P
specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`; the F_H specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`. The source concepts and their
context are owned by
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle); this
profile owns the targets in the graph-native ODD context (P1, P6).

Both relations preserve the source meaning and authority, narrow scope to
a declared ODD traversal, and add graph-contract and runtime-control
coordinates. They exclude processing or adjudication outside that
traversal, refuse ambient worker or human authority, and have no implied
inverse. Their source and target basis is the selected complete STDO
release, their governed scope is ODD traversal, and this clause is their
provenance carrier. A change to either concept or context, to the basis,
to the scope, to the preserved or narrowed meaning or to the control
contract invalidates the affected specialisation until it is evaluated
again (P1, P3, P6).

The F_D import runs from the common concept to its use under this profile,
preserves the common total deterministic contract, and narrows each use to
its declared ODD operation. Its source and target basis is the exact
selected complete release; a change to that edition, traversal contract,
material dependency, termination evidence or authority invalidates the
affected eligibility claim. The former
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d` remains a historical concept on its
legacy edition. It is not an unconditional alias: only the explicit
[migration mapping](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration) licenses a
successor use, preserving the original evidence, permissions and results.

and its control truth. It does not make the framework the executor of the

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:a8cafeeacc2f8bc2deda01690eaaf31b"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:8ad20b6ea7b88b3d9f0c34afac671c8d","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"Bind actor, executor, domain operation, functor kind, grant and invocation separately. A kind label or total algorithm supplies no right to acquire, disclose, use, execute, mutate, assess, admit or dispose. The selected operation still needs its exact existing owner grant and all applicable admission conditions.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

The selected operation still needs its exact existing owner grant and all applicable admission conditions.

IACS, subordinate payloads, promotion and inflation: IACS is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family needed for a boundary's functionality and authority flow. Subordinate Payload is internal payload detail, not top-level by default. Promotion Test is the explicit prerequisite for elevating it to a top-level type. Boundary Inflation is promotion into peer types without irreducible need. Example carrier roles are source truth, admission, execution, yielded/recovery, effect plan and public projection.

1. From the verified definition and installed basis, read Goals, Intent,
   Product, affected requirements, accepted design, ticket bindings, and
   relevant existing work. Acquire owning sections under the selected basis's
   `ACTIVATION.md` section 2, Acquisition; intake triage and change classes
   are `SPEC_METHOD.md` section 4, ticket fields `TICKETS.md` section 4.
2. Confirm explicit authority to create or update ticket state. Without it,
   return proposed triage and stop without writing.
3. Create or update a durable ticket only when the work or an open obligation
   needs independent identity, handoff, dependency, reopening, repricing, or
   closure beyond its admitted sprint or, when no sprint applies, beyond the
   current run, or when the user explicitly requests that durable record. Do
   not create a ticket merely because execution needs a run-scoped contract.
4. Identify the affected Product boundary and first changed layer.
   Consume source-bound computed owner/layer routes, complete relevant Public
   membership/value comparison and accepted-design trace coverage where
   available. Keep absent mappings or evidence explicitly unknown. Reuse a
   still-applicable classification judgment; record any residual judgment and
   its supporting facts once in this carrier. A nonconforming candidate can
   require repair under unchanged law; it does not itself select requirement
   repricing.
5. Select the smallest lawful change class: `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`,
   `product_reprice`, `requirement_reprice`, `design_reframe`, or
   `realization_refactor`.
6. Select type and category from the exact Product policy. Under base
   TICKETS, types are `feature`, `bug`, `spike`, or `chore`; categories are
   `ordinary` or `implementation_migration`.
7. Resolve the Product-bound lanes. Create or update one unique durable ticket
   with the exact base fields:

   - `id`, `title`, `type`, `ticket_category`, `status`, `goal`,
     `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`, `triaged_at`,
     `created_at`, and `updated_at`.

   For execution admission also bind `target_truth`, relevant
   `superseded_truth`, `closure_law`, `evaluation_criteria`,
   `non_closure_conditions`, and `proof_surface`. Record the affected boundary,
   governing authority, dependencies, source ticket, or build tenant where
   applicable.

8. Treat the ticket as an execution-contract source candidate, never as its own
   admission evidence. Report the derived execution-contract state as `drafted`
   unless deterministic admission or an exact human override of that contract
   is independently evidenced. Ticket creation, lane placement, and `active`
   status do not change that state.
9. Keep commentary and generated summaries subordinate to the ticket. Assign
   priority only under Product-owned policy and decision authority. When the
   Executive baseline profile is adopted, do not turn Reviewer technical severity
   directly into Executive Product priority.

For review findings, use [the selected review flow](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#review-flow-from-the-selected-basis)
and the actual selected TICKETS clauses. Bind one authorized report to the
issuing work item; no findings means no report. Keep the original assessment
in that report and the triaged Bug items on the reviewed work item. Preserve
severity, priority reason, cause/owner, source link and actual open/fixed/verified
state with repair and verification identities. A test result is not labelled
independent review. Report naming, lane or metadata edits confer no access;
preserve withheld evidence across every projection. Reuse a sufficient direct
carrier instead of minting a redundant ticket.

For an authorized state update, evaluate the ticket's actual closure condition:
satisfied obligations, valid applicable evidence, required judgments and owner
rulings, and no active non-closure condition. Review checks that evidence when
required; occurrence of review is not the closing event. Record reusable
judgments with their question, subject/basis, support, actor/authority,
conclusion, uncertainty and revising observation. Preserve an owner's original
ruling separately from interpretation and invalidate only affected support,
under the invalidators of `ACTIVATION.md` section 7.
Use this ticket's existing proof/result routes; do not create a judgment registry.
When repricing, give each affected obligation a retained, superseded, deferred
or withdrawn disposition with its owner and applicable evidence. Preserve
surviving work and changed dependencies without duplicating unaffected history.
Present a short consequence delta for the owner decision; a general instruction
to continue does not accept undisclosed architecture or scope changes.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-ticket/SKILL.md#STDO%20Ticket%2FProcedure","start_line":54},{"end_line":136,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-ticket/SKILL.md","quote":"## Return

point, scope, target truth, closure law, non-closure conditions, proof surface,
derived execution-contract state and evidence, and next decision. Do not edit
requirements, design, code, or tests unless the user separately authorizes
execution.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-ticket/SKILL.md#STDO%20Ticket%2FReturn","start_line":130}],"statement":"Triage observed need through current authority and first changed layer before selecting a carrier. Avoid duplicate work records. A review report preserves original severity and visibility; its reviewed work-item ledger holds owner priority/repair/verification decisions. Recording the carrier neither starts implementation nor supplies work admission. Return changed carrier identities, authority, state/evidence and lawful next route.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

An actor's selected context must satisfy both permission and adequacy for its
engagement. Permission covers the source information and permitted derivations,
not only paths or filenames. The boundary identifies eligible source classes,
exports and tool outputs, material provenance, intended use, later acquisitions
and the effect of prior exposure. An allowed file location or a fresh summary
does not sanitize prohibited information.

A target owner may authorize an export, but clean-room eligibility additionally
requires that the engagement's information policy admits that export and its
provenance. The actual delivered/acquired material must be recorded to the extent
required by the claim. An uncertain or prohibited exposure follows the declared
hold/re-entry rule; it cannot be repaired by deleting its receipt or relabeling
the same actor fresh. Prior actor knowledge and external acquisition channels are
part of the declared limits.

Adequacy retains the distinctions required for the task's decisions and
continuations, including unresolved obligations, result standing, currentness and
authority. If the permitted material is insufficient, acquire an authorized
extension, narrow the task with the owner, use a suitable actor or return the
unresolved outcome. Permission is not evidence of sufficiency, and a budget is
not permission to omit a deciding condition. This applies [FOUNDATIONS Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assurance-relations)
and its scoped preservation law; it supplies no general optimal context selector (P1, P2, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-05%20%E2%80%94%20Context%20construction%20and%20clean-room%20conditions","start_line":939}],"statement":"Construct context under both information eligibility and claim sufficiency. {"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:fb42a8b9db1ba218cdb616fb7361239d"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:9a4f7578abbba7e9639eeeb64557e10a","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1562,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"### 11.7A Conforming agentic development

This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
graph-native worksite. An agentic coder produces governed work by
following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).

Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
to admit (P6).

The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
requirement, design and ticket chain, the constructive evaluation loop of
§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
constitutional process (P0, P6).

The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the
packet carries only the smallest declared authority sufficient to decide
the step, with its source refs, and that conformance is enforced by
admitting the produced artifact rather than by enlarging what the agent
must hold. Compression is prompt input and never the deciding authority
(P0, P6). What a derived surface may decide is owned by
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition and Standalone scope; this section adds only the ODD limit
that follows. A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The walkthrough proves at two levels. The work it produces must be lawful:
correct change class, traceable, admitted. A point where the walkthrough
cannot proceed is a method defect only when a competent agent, correctly
configured and using the declared authority, still cannot decide because
of ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or an undecidable
change class in an owning surface. That defect is repriced into the owning
authority surface, as a failed manual traversal is a graph defect under
§11.7 (P6, P5).

An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

This proof is independent of any automated runtime. A live lane that
depends on external execution conditions, such as an overloaded model API
or a flaky transport, cannot prove the constitutional process sound,
because it conflates process validity with runtime availability. The
walkthrough proves the process; the runtime only executes it (P6, P5).

The validator is the conformance gate. The constitutional process is an
interface contract, and interface conformance is enforced by validating
artifacts against the contract, not by the conformer holding the contract.
This profile does not declare the artifact rules again: tickets,
change-class declarations, design-module derivations and execution
contracts are admitted under SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS, which already require
a drafted classification to be admitted or rejected against deterministic
criteria rather than taken as automatic truth. This profile requires only
that agentic development pass through that admission. The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,
fail-closed and naming the violated rule, exactly as a typed asset is
enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

This keeps the F_P and F_D split at the method layer. The agentic coder is
F_P: it reasons, drafts and proposes within the declared packet. Admission
uses F_D only when the §5 total-domain contract is established, and its own
contract and authority determine what artifact-conformance decision it may
make. An unresolved eligibility assessment stays open under the migration
relation; an unchanged-subject evaluator still preserves that subject. The walkthrough
establishes that the process can be followed; admission establishes that
each act of following it conforms (P6, P0).

Conformance is not approval by usage. A passed admission and a completed
walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification. Shared method
change still follows §9: repeated agentic execution does not make grey
work constitutional. The agentic coder conforms to the method; it does not
amend the method by acting (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F11.%20Core%20law%2F11.7A%20Conforming%20agentic%20development","start_line":1474}],"statement":"Agents use the smallest sufficient source-linked authority packet with context, role, input/output contract, evaluator regime and provenance. Compression is prompt input, never deciding authority. Produced classification, design, ticket and execution-contract artifacts retain current source trace and pass their actual SPEC_METHOD/TICKETS/Product admission contracts; fail closed with violated rules rather than treating drafted classification as truth. Product admission decides Product facts; ABG owns its typed evidence and evaluate_action closure fold. F_D eligibility grants neither role. A walkthrough and admitted artifacts provide conformance evidence but do not ratify method changes.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}
