Selector and consumer adoption

An RC-profile version-line selector answers only (P6, P3):

> Which highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut currently exists on
> this version line?

It never answers:

> Which exact STDO cut governs this consumer?

A Product Definition may retain `stdo://channels/<version>` as its
discovery selector, but its operative basis is the exact
`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/` or stable
`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/` URI and installed-manifest digest,
the installed release basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4. Moving the Git
version-line selector does not update any consumer. Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable cut. RC resolution requires an
annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled
selector ref fails closed and cannot be interpreted as a lightweight
selector whose tag object is its commit (P6, P3, P5).

For an RC line, channel resolution enumerates the published RC tags for the selected
Project Release Namespace, including preserved unqualified historical cuts
during a namespace transition, selects the greatest positive ordinal,
requires that cut and the current selector to be annotated tags peeling to
the same commit, and fails closed when the selector lags or points
elsewhere. Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal
is below the Product Definition's current exact basis. A consumer that
intentionally retains an older cut names that immutable RC URI and digest
explicitly and uses exact-basis operations such as `sync`; it does not
express that choice through the latest-version channel (P5, P6).

For a stable line, channel resolution returns its verified stable-v1 cut
without ordinal comparison or a separate selector. A legacy bare selector is
never admitted as a stable exact basis; an ambiguous profile is refused. The
same digest-bound adoption operation applies to either profile (P3, P5, P6).

Presentation and mutation are separate invocations. The read-only plan,
the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest. Mutation requires that exact digest as the
operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product
Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the
acceptance. A fleet uses the same law with one aggregate digest over all
exact per-definition plans. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not
external presentation and cannot authorise itself. The plan's hashing rule
and the manager's command boundaries are PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4 (P6, P3).

This split lets operators refer to `v<version>` for the latest published
RC without repeatedly incrementing the version line, while every governed
project retains reproducible exact-cut authority and changes only through
explicit adoption (P2, P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F4.%20Selector%20and%20consumer%20adoption","start_line":428}],"statement":"Resolve and present the exact target, install and verify it, and bind current Definition bytes/basis, target tag/peel/tree/manifest and the deterministic plan digest. Obtain acceptance of that exact plan and rederive it before mutation; changed subject or target invalidates acceptance. Preserve prior basis if preconditions fail. RC discovery must verify annotated selector and greatest ordinal; stable discovery must return an exact profile-verified stable cut. Neither discovery nor shared version labels silently adopts a successor.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Resolve and present the exact target, install and verify it, and bind current Definition bytes/basis, target tag/peel/tree/manifest and the deterministic plan digest. Obtain acceptance of that exact plan and rederive it before mutation; changed subject or target invalidates acceptance. Preserve prior basis if preconditions fail. RC discovery must verify annotated selector and greatest ordinal; stable discovery must return an exact profile-verified stable cut. Neither discovery nor shared version labels silently adopts a successor.

Lineage and release

Software is recursive and compositional. A released product may build the
next released version of itself, a dependent product, or downstream project
artifacts. The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities,
substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product,
install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2
(product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler
analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense
surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be
running the build (P3).

The only exact operative release identifier is an immutable release-cut
tag under the selected [RELEASE profile](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities):
an RC cut or an explicit stable cut (P3). That cut is a
point-in-time release identity, a boundary over the feature set accepted
for that cut, and part of release metadata and release-process evaluation;
it is not part of the live project specification. On an RC line the mutable
`v<version>` tag is a discovery selector to the highest published ordinal; it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional
basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection. How an active
constitutional surface uses version labels is the
[§2 Specification surface rule](#specification-surface-rule); shared
realisation surfaces should likewise describe current truth by role,
boundary and status rather than by release-line version labels. Release criteria, immutable
release-cut publication, selector advancement and the process for cutting a
release belong to [RELEASE §2 to §8](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities)
.

Successor baseline conservation is
[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(P3, P6).

Layer and release separation holds
([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §7](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation)):
a calculus, its interpretation of a subject and its carrier encoding keep
independent content identities, judgments, supersession relations and
proof obligations, and none is automatically an independently released
product. One constitutional surface and its version boundary for a project
are
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F6.%20Lineage%20and%20release","start_line":1240}],"label":"Method release lineage"}}}

1. Establish applicable upstream work authority under the verified definition
   and immutable basis. Without it, stop before
   selecting a carrier; a ticket cannot substitute for that authority. Then
   select the first applicable source for one run-scoped execution contract:

   - reuse an exact admitted durable ticket when it covers the work;
   - otherwise require one authorized durable ticket only when work or an
     obligation needs independent state beyond its admitted sprint or, outside
     a sprint, beyond the current run;
   - otherwise use the admitted sprint plus one manifest-local iteration entry
     when the work ends by sprint close; or
   - otherwise use an intake draft for work that ends in the current run.

   Do not invoke `stdo-ticket` automatically. Absence of a ticket neither
   requires nor authorizes creating one.
2. Bind the contract's current Goal or exact work instruction, `change_intent`,
   change class, re-entry point, `target_truth`, relevant `superseded_truth`,
   `closure_law`, governing requirement and accepted design, checkpoint,
   affected relation set, write territory, evaluation criteria, non-closure
   conditions, proof surface, and one Product-bound durable result/evidence
   surface. If that result surface is unavailable or unauthorized, admission
   must refuse.
3. Validate and admit or reject that exact contract. Drafting, admission, and
   execution may occur in the same invocation, but ticket presence, `active`
   status, a generic work request, or the model's own draft cannot supply
   admission. Continue only after deterministic admission or an exact human
   override of the bounded contract. Record the Product-bound admitting
   mechanism and authority, exact contract identity or digest, decision, and
   evidence. If those coordinates are absent, return the missing authority and
   stop.
   Consume an existing exact owner instruction or admitted grant when it
   already covers this contract; cite it instead of requesting the same
   authorization again. Record the binding, not another approval round.
4. Re-enter at the first changed layer and flow forward:

   - requirement change: establish the successor/current requirement as the
     sole operative truth; supersede or withdraw a published live domain
     artifact instead of mutating it in place;
   - design change: admit the structural decision before implementation relies
     on it; or
   - realization change: prove upstream Goals, Intent, Product, requirements,
     and accepted design remain unchanged.
5. If work discovers an obligation that needs state beyond its local carrier
   boundary, do not claim closure or create a ticket without authority. Persist
   it only when the current exact grant already includes ticket-state mutation
   for that obligation. Otherwise retain it in the contract's named durable
   result/evidence surface or an already-authorized enclosing carrier, mark
   closure withheld, and return the required re-entry plus an explicit
   `stdo-ticket` route without invoking it. A conversation return alone is not
   durable evidence.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md#STDO%20Work%2FEstablish%20The%20Work%20Basis","start_line":87}],"statement":"Establish the selected authorized outcome and smallest adequate carrier: an exact admitted ticket when sufficient, a durable ticket for independently surviving state only under state authority, a sprint-local iteration for work ending there, or a run contract for authorized run-local work. {"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:62c03e6b02ba6e5c63e0e2e4c0dad571"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:b8a92f83eccfb161aac84ec5499a3d8a","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":350,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis
is the pair (P3):

```text
(immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)
```

The URI identifies one immutable annotated release cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status
and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8
JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line
endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path
order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible
rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).

The STDO Toolchain Manager is the bounded executable realisation that (P2,
P3):

- installs each immutable cut once in a shared, versioned release store;
- resolves logical `stdo://releases/...` URIs to verified installed bytes;
- inventories and verifies complete installed distributions;
- synchronises the exact basis already selected by a Product Definition;
- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a release-profile discovery
  route and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly
  accepted;
- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and
- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product
  Definitions.

The store may live at any machine-local path. Its registry maps logical
release URIs to installed paths and manifest digests and owns neither
Product selection nor method meaning. A consumer repository therefore needs
no project-local standards copy and no prescribed folder structure, and
several Product Definitions on one machine may select different installed
cuts concurrently (P3, P6). Every manager-owned component from the
configured store root downward is a physical directory or regular file of
its declared type; a symlink, junction, reparse point, device, socket or
other redirection or special entry fails closed. Verification inventories
every filesystem entry type, directories included, rejects any entry not
derived from the manifest's exact file paths, and never follows an
unmanifested alias (P5, P3).

`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.
`constitution.stdo.selector` is a `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery
route whose profile semantics are owned by [RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption).
An RC line resolves its mutable selector; a stable line resolves its exact
immutable cut without a second selector. Neither discovery nor the transport
source is operative authority.
`constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256`
are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).

The manager observes these command boundaries (P6, P5):

- `install` admits one explicitly named immutable release cut without changing
  any Product Definition;
- `sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by
  the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector;
- `adopt --dry-run` resolves the selected release profile and immutable cut, and
  presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest,
  current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic
  adoption-plan digest, without mutation;
- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit
  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound
  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes
  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses
  mutation;
- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with
  respect to Product Definitions; and
- fleet adoption emits, and requires explicit acceptance of, one aggregate
  plan digest over every per-definition plan; all fleet writes require
  explicit whole-selection authorisation and infer no composition or
  inheritance from directory nesting.

Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag-to-commit mismatch, manifest-digest
mismatch, missing, extra or changed installed members, ambiguous Product
Definition discovery, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, URI escape,
physical store redirection, undeclared filesystem entry types and malformed
bootstrap markers fail closed (P5). Every `stdo:` schema locator is parsed
before schema loading under URI scheme case-insensitivity and names the
same immutable cut as `constitution.stdo.basis`; spelling variation cannot
cross that basis. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias,
schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the
Product Definition (P6, P3).

`constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one
basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such
as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the
manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative
path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent
traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail
closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its
explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the
first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced;
the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay
project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all
existing bytes as an exact prefix. The bootstrap routes agents to the
applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning
sources; it can neither restate nor override them (P6, P3, P5).

Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as
version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals:
`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`,
`site-packages`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `target`, `.gradle`, `.tox`,
`.nox`, `.cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`,
`__pycache__`, `.genesis` and `.stdo`. A discovered Product Definition may
not itself be a symlink. These exclusions are discovery law, not evidence
that an excluded tree lacks another independently governed Product (P5,
P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F4.%20Shared%20installed%20release%20basis%20and%20toolchain%20manager","start_line":225}],"statement":"agent_bootstrap selects one basis-qualified entrypoint and only marker-managed discovery blocks; it embeds no second constitution. Landing, closure, release and explicit Product gates have one owner,
[EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#landing-closure-and-release). For this profile,
an admitted step lands its candidate after its selected work and fix pass.
Where review is required or selected, one bounded QA review covers that exact
declared subject and may run beside the next authorized step. It is not a
standing permission for another review of every local change. The Executive
records review size and its reason in the existing work carrier; any ratio is
Product-selected, and none is imposed here (P6, P2).

Sizing does not shrink a declared claim. Preserve the exact evaluated
population and conjunction; a sample supports its stated scope and leaves
uncovered required coverage explicit. A budget or ratio cannot turn that
residual into a completed whole-subject review (P6, P5).

Each test-reproducible repair binds a reproduction that fails on the faulty
subject and passes on the repaired subject, with the full suite declared for
that repair scope passing. A repair without a reproduction states that gap and
requires the independent recheck below; a green total does not fill the gap.
Tests may verify a repair without becoming independent assessment. A fix pass
closes on that evidence and its other applicable conditions unless independent
recheck is required by one of these conditions (P6, P5):

1. the candidate reaches a boundary whose governing basis requires or claims
   independent review, including any Product, release, qualification, risk or
   admitted-work addition;
2. the pass repairs a hard stop or a capture whose source-fidelity claim is
   material to the outcome;
3. a repair has no reproducing test; or
4. a selected review left part of its declared subject uncovered.

For a required recheck, activate one fresh Reviewer for the bounded fix pass,
with its affected claims, prior findings, reproductions and remaining coverage.
Fresh means a new bounded assessment activation with the independence of
EVALUATION §3, not independence inferred from a new context or actor name.
Partitioning follows the declared conjunction, not extra serial rounds. The
covered fixes remain unresolved for the dependent closure claim until that
report arrives and the required predicates are satisfied; tests alone cannot
substitute for this required review. A later material finding is a new input
to the next bounded disposition, not an unbounded review loop (P6, P2).

The Executive preserves Reviewer severity, assigns priority under the selected
policy and hands the linked items to the lawful repair Writer. Pending review
alone holds no landing. An open required review holds its dependent closure,
and release retains all its selected conditions. Downstream use and later
invalidation follow EVALUATION §5; access and artifact-effect grants remain
unchanged (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#EXECUTIVE_BASELINE%2F12.%20Complete%20engagement%20transition%2FQA%20cadence%20and%20repair%20rechecks","start_line":1384}],"statement":"Recheck when the selected boundary requires or claims independent review; when repair changes a hard stop or material source-capture/authority condition; when no exact failing-before/passing-after reproduction verifies the repair; or when the declared subject remains uncovered. Otherwise exact reproduction plus declared relevant suite evidence may verify the bug under the selected policy. Tests remain construction/verification evidence, not independent assessment. Retain subject changes and uncovered scope, and do not automatically rereview every repair.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Recheck when the selected boundary requires or claims independent review; when repair changes a hard stop or material source-capture/authority condition; when no exact failing-before/passing-after reproduction verifies the repair; or when the declared subject remains uncovered. Otherwise exact reproduction plus declared relevant suite evidence may verify the bug under the selected policy. Tests remain construction/verification evidence, not independent assessment. Retain subject changes and uncovered scope, and do not automatically rereview every repair.

For each directed relation, the `relation` authority and referenced `contracts`
state, directly or by exact reference:

1. Source and target Product identities and roles; the consumed capability,
   outcome, purpose, selected basis and currentness policy.
2. The existing owners and grants for each material operation: acquisition,
   disclosure, use, execution, mutation, assessment and disposition. A kind or
   role label records no grant by itself.
3. Admissible inputs and exports; material assumptions, effects, failures,
   obligations and evidence; restrictions on implementation material and derived
   information where applicable.
4. The acting principals or binding rule, task/phase scope, permitted delegation,
   return consumer, stop/refusal conditions and revocation/invalidation route.

These coordinates may be supplied by source-linked prose. The relation locates
and constrains lawfully granted authority; it cannot manufacture the target's
permission or the source's admission. Missing material authority or an unresolved
conflict withholds the dependent action. The execution-scoped activation remains
the place where a particular actor, input, effect and return are bound.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-03%20%E2%80%94%20The%20edge%27s%20contract%20and%20authority%20record","start_line":895}],"kind":"requires","meaning":"A lawful composed claim requires the actual directed edge and its authority/information conditions."},"scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"],"source":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:bcb769c763230c0182097d3cc494c488","target":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:756ca08136ac3f65c9ee22f41d76ac8c"}}

A successor that adopts the total deterministic kind of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
preserves each existing evaluation operation's unchanged subject, admissible
reads, witness/log outputs, permitted writes, stops/results, authority and
invalidation conditions. That profile alone does not
establish the new kind's totality, closed dependencies or declared outcomes.
The old deterministic evaluation/proof definition supplies no general
termination argument. Assess each proposed use against this relation (P3, P6):

| Evidence and declared migration status | Successor disposition |
|---|---|
| Establishes the new totality, closed-dependency and outcome contract | Map to common F_D plus the unchanged operation profile and exact traversal binding. Preserve the evidence and grants. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished, and the owner has identified the missing evidence or a separately declared bounded successor and its remediation obligation | Keep that identified migration pending. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while it remains applicable; it gains no successor F_D standing. A narrower domain or fuel-bounded implementation has its own contract, identity, exhaustion outcomes and affected preservation evidence; it does not retrospectively prove the old operation total or preserve every old continuation. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished and no supported remediation or successor classification has been selected | Retain the exact legacy meaning and evidence with an explicit unresolved successor-classification obligation until its owner disposes it. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while applicable. Grant neither new F_D standing nor an automatic F_P label; the affected successor claim stays open. |

An old deterministic evaluator with unestablished termination or an
undeclared material dependency takes the second or third row, even if it
preserves the judged subject: the second row requires an identified evidence
gap/remediation or selected bounded successor; absent that, the third records
the unresolved classification. Evidence alone need not choose the owner's
remediation. This relation imposes no general decision procedure for totality.
These eligibility/remediation cases are not additional semantic dispositions
under this section. Generic role descriptions and schematic traversal contracts are not concrete
operations with an implementation to qualify; their use still binds the
kind and operation contracts when instantiated.

ODD admission and closure retain their named operation owners under
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5's authority boundary](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds).
Exhaustion
retains the evaluated predicate and its signature/traversal stop mapping,
as [the conformance examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish.

Immutable consumers keep their selected edition's meaning. New consumers
explicitly select the complete successor and operation profiles. A stable
concept URN is not its immutable calculus edition
([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §8](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#8-calculus-identity)). Migration
records the old release, manifest, member and clauses and the applicable row
above. Current URN lookup never reinterprets history. A versioned import or
alias records its justified supersession and grants no broader permission.
Disposition and qualification retain the separate obligations of this
section; unresolved mappings block the affected successor claim.

Broadening operation purpose while strengthening totality, dependency and
evidence requirements is a substantive semantic change. A patch-shaped
version label by itself promises no compatibility. The release's version
assessment identifies the selected predecessor, affected consumer mappings
and remaining obligations. This relation settles no general version-line
policy and waives no acceptance gate.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F9.%20Successor%20baseline%20conservation%20%28STDO-UP-015%29%2FDeterministic-kind%20migration","start_line":799}],"statement":"If totality, dependency closure and declared outcomes are established, migrate to common F_D while retaining the operation purpose, unchanged-subject evaluation profile where applicable, and exact grants. If new-kind eligibility is unestablished and the owner has identified the evidence gap/remediation or selected a separately declared bounded successor and its remediation obligation, retain pending-identified migration. Either alternative suffices; an identified termination-proof gap/remediation does not require selecting a bounded successor. When neither supported remediation nor successor classification has been selected, retain unresolved classification; do not relabel automatically as F_P or claim common F_D. A bounded successor has its own identity, contract, exhaustion outcomes and preservation obligations and does not retrospectively prove the legacy operation total. Old evidence remains valid only for its exact legacy basis/claims until the required preservation relation is established; patch naming does not promise semantic compatibility.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: If totality, dependency closure and declared outcomes are established, migrate to common F_D while retaining the operation purpose, unchanged-subject evaluation profile where applicable, and exact grants. If new-kind eligibility is unestablished and the owner has identified the evidence gap/remediation or selected a separately declared bounded successor and its remediation obligation, retain pending-identified migration. Either alternative suffices; an identified termination-proof gap/remediation does not require selecting a bounded successor. When neither supported remediation nor successor classification has been selected, retain unresolved classification; do not relabel automatically as F_P or claim common F_D. A bounded successor has its own identity, contract, exhaustion outcomes and preservation obligations and does not retrospectively prove the legacy operation total. Old evidence remains valid only for its exact legacy basis/claims until the required preservation relation is established; patch naming does not promise semantic compatibility.

|---|---|---|---|

ODD keeps the actual operations, evidence and grants. | AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5; ODD §11.5D A4a–A8 | M-D301-01: three constructor results; L-D301-01: authority boundary, no executable authorization claim |

Tier 3. The Outcome-Driven Development profile: graph-native product
authoring over a declared asset graph. It imports the families that
[§1 Foundation to law](#foundation-to-law) lists by reference under
[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of them. Inside
its bounded context it uses its own terms freely: graph, node, asset,
vector, edge, graph function, traversal, worksite, ledger, event log, GTL,
ABG, F_P and F_H (P0, P1). `F_D` is the exact-edition common import below.

Two definitions are used here and owned elsewhere. The a_c traversal record
and the functor kinds are
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds);
the core result algebra is [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results).
This profile's graph traversal and its F_P and F_H shorthands are its
own concepts and are not those records by spelling. Its F_D use imports
the common kind through [§5](#probabilistic-compute), without inheriting
any operation authority. The Executive, Worker
and Reviewer of [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) are roles, and roles
are relations over steps in which no role name confers an operation
([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)); the actor, the
executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are different
coordinates (AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5) (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD","start_line":1},{"end_line":215,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"## 2. Method role

[SPEC_METHOD](SPEC_METHOD.md) is the general constitutional method: the
baseline for goals, intent, product, requirements, design and lawful
re-entry. This profile is the graph-native ODD product-authoring method
whose primary constructive carrier is GTL-defined graph functions. It holds
two kinds of law: constitutional law for graph-native traversal governance
(assets, vectors, traversal, graph functions), and product-authoring law
for building an ODD product correctly over that substrate (P1, P6).

The profile does not replace a product-specific domain method such as the
world-model profile (WORLD_MODEL, tier 3). Where a product is both ODD and
world-model-driven, this profile governs graph-native structure and ODD
product shape and the world-model profile governs world-model semantics,
publication and composition law. The two compose (P1, P4a).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F2.%20Method%20role","start_line":201},{"end_line":239,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"## 3. Method composition

This profile alone does not suffice for domain-correct product work. It
gives the structural law for how a graph-native ODD product should be
built. It does not give the product's domain semantics, its current intent
and product-definition line, its local capability and constraint
requirements, or its currently ratified design surfaces (P1, P2).

The composition rule: this profile says how to build the product as a
graph-native ODD product; domain methods say what semantic law the product
must honour; the local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design say
what the currently ratified local line is. For a graph-native
software-development ODD product, this profile provides the substrate and
structural law and the product's local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
requirements, design records and GTL surfaces provide the local line. For
a world-model product, this profile provides the substrate and structural
law, the world-model profile provides the semantic law, and the product's
local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design provide the local
line (P1, P2).

An agent that reads only this profile should understand the paradigm.
To build one concrete product correctly it must then read the
product-specific method and the local authority surfaces (P1, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F3.%20Method%20composition","start_line":217}],"label":"Current graph-native ODD profile"}}}

A preservation checkpoint under an exact grant names parent/predecessor, included territory, concurrent-writer disposition and durable evidence location; it is neither acceptance, promotion nor publication. Restart from less than retained work states why repair is insufficient, surviving obligations/evidence and changed causal assumptions; reconstructability alone does not choose restart. Negative evidence invalidates the real authority-bearing input on the supported path and demonstrates refusal before prohibited effect; manufactured refusal/event/gap/verdict proves nothing about that path, and source/package/install/runtime absence are distinct claims. Decisive proof uses an installable development form where one exists; isolation/proving-lane provisions remain recommendations. Refined inner chains close enclosing carriers only if outer contract survives fold-back and zoomed/unzoomed views agree. A live requirement without a proof witness keeps the enclosing carrier open until realised or owner-deferred/repriced out of the active branch. Scenario bundles should clarify boundary, assets, vectors, paths and closure evidence; products choose scenarios and appropriate witnesses.

Determinism on observed samples alone is insufficient; the declared domain need not be finite.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"label":"F_D eligibility"}}}

clauses.statement: F_D eligibility: Eligibility requires an exact basis, closed domain including material state and dependencies, declared outcome contract, and established totality. Determinism on observed samples alone is insufficient; the declared domain need not be finite.

The reviewed work item’s authoritative Bug items ledger records owner decisions, priority, cause, repair and verification state with links to that report; it does not overwrite or duplicate the assessment as new authority.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":577,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md","quote":"### Review findings and bug items

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FReview%20findings%20and%20bug%20items","start_line":536}],"label":"Finding report and Bug items ledger"}}}

clauses.statement: Finding report and Bug items ledger: The review report preserves the original exact-subject technical assessment and severity. The reviewed work item’s authoritative Bug items ledger records owner decisions, priority, cause, repair and verification state with links to that report; it does not overwrite or duplicate the assessment as new authority.

Acquire the selected basis's `EVALUATION` §5, `TICKETS` §4 and §7, and, where
adopted, `EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §5 and §12. Use their actual clauses. A loaded
3.0.4 skill cannot amend an older Product-selected method or silently adopt
the candidate's review cadence or optional priority policy.

Where that basis contains **Landing, closure and release**, **Declared Product
acceptance gates**, **QA cadence and repair rechecks**, and **Review findings
and bug items**, route the next decision as follows:

1. Name which decision is requested: authorized candidate landing, work
   closure, or release. Keep its actual conditions separate. A pending review
   alone is not a landing hold; no operation, access or hard-stop waiver follows.
2. Bind the exact QA subject, coverage, size and reason. Use the owning recheck
   triggers; do not automatically request a new review after every repair or
   set a review ratio. Keep test verification distinct from required independent
   review, and retain any uncovered subject.
3. Return unchanged Reviewer severity. The Executive decides priority and
   ownership directly when clear, or delegates bounded grouping/proposals to a
   triage Worker when volume warrants it; that Worker changes no assessment.
   If the basis selects the 1 highest–5 lowest convention, apply its qualitative
   anchors and explicit severity-3 downstream/blast-radius assessment. Material
   dependent impact normally calls for repair; contained local deferral needs
   a reason and owner. Keep severity 3 distinct from priority P3 and retain old
   or alternative scales on their own identities.
4. If findings need a durable carrier, use `stdo-ticket` under the exact report
   or item-update grant. Bind report ID/path, source linkage and visibility
   before the effect. No findings means no bug report; sufficient direct work
   gains no redundant ticket. A Reviewer records only its granted report and
   makes no candidate repair. The reviewed work item's ledger holds decisions
   and repair/verification provenance, not a new copy of the assessment.
5. For provisional downstream use, retain exact dependencies and uncertainty.
   Check only explicitly declared Product gates; a later material finding
   invalidates affected dependent results before further reliance. Keep other
   valid work. If a policy or boundary decision is genuinely missing, return
   that material choice rather than inventing numeric meanings or a gate.

Example: a granted Writer lands candidate C while its selected QA runs. QA
reports finding F in the named restricted report R. The Executive retains F's
severity, assigns priority and links item B on the reviewed work carrier. A
repair returns C2 with its failing-before/passing-after reproduction and
declared suite evidence. The Executive applies the selected recheck conditions:
tests may verify B when no independent recheck is required; otherwise B awaits
that exact report. Neither outcome by itself authorizes release or adopts C2
at an explicitly gated downstream boundary.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FReview%20Flow%20From%20The%20Selected%20Basis","start_line":200}],"statement":"Acquire actual selected-basis EVALUATION, TICKETS and adopted Executive clauses. For ticketed work, admitted ticket and triage path are immediate authority; expected results derive from lawful re-entry and cited constitutional/realisation law, never current implementation behaviour. Direct source unit/helper/module-integration tests cannot alone close user acceptance or be called UAT. Harnessed UAT proves composition, orchestration, control, projection, archive and scenario wiring with deterministic reproducibility; live UAT proves the same scenario crosses the actual external probabilistic boundary and returns evidence through result, evaluation, provenance and projection surfaces. Live-dependent claims require more than necessary semantic/unit/integration/harnessed green results. Unit denotes conformance scope, integration breadth rather than authority, sandbox composed acceptance, harnessed/fake/recorded/deterministic non-live execution, and live actual external execution; a projection merely named live is insufficient. Every local lane label maps to this taxonomy before closure.

Standards requires a member-set SHA-256; auxiliary requires plugin member inventory, LICENSE and release-note identity. Closed objects refuse undeclared fields; member lists are unique and paths/hashes obey declared syntax. Structural schema validation alone cannot prove inventory bytes, counts, digest algorithms or cross-field semantic equality.

When the cause and consequence are sufficiently clear, the Executive decides
priority and ownership directly. Where finding volume would overwhelm its
bounded attention, it may activate a triage Worker to group causes, identify
duplicates and propose priorities and responsible owners from the admitted
findings. The assistant neither grades nor changes Reviewer severity and
decides no priority or disposition. The Executive consumes its evidence and
records its own decision; unsupported cause relations stay uncertain. The
assistant adds no read authority, and this profile requires no extra actor
for a small or clear result (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#EXECUTIVE_BASELINE%2F5.%20Profile%20terms%2FTechnical%20triage%2C%20severity%2C%20priority%20and%20boundary%20effect%2FProportional%20triage%20assistance","start_line":501},{"end_line":532,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md","quote":"#### Optional P0–P5 response policy

An adopting Product may explicitly select the following response policy in its
frame basis. The labels have no numeric meaning outside that adoption; the
Product supplies its ordering/assignment criteria and any finer distinctions.
This is priority policy, not a Reviewer severity scale (P6, P2).

| Selected priority | Response and boundary effect |
|---|---|
| P0–P2 | Include in the next bounded fix pass; hold the affected outcome's closure and release, not candidate landing merely because of this priority. |
| P3–P5 | Repair before release/go-live; hold that release, while bounded work may close with the item durably retained or transferred with its disposition. |

This policy never waives applicable hard stops, mandatory claims, acceptance
conditions, access restrictions or operation grants. Those owners may require
an earlier hold at any priority. A P3–P5 item may outlive a local work claim's
closure only when that claim does not require the unfixed behaviour; assigning
that priority cannot satisfy a false mandatory claim. No review-to-work ratio or additional
capture-review landing hold is selected by adopting this example. Durable
items and their actual verification state are owned by

Constitutional-set sufficiency

A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1):

- axioms: irreducible starting truths, invariants and refusal conditions;
- ontology: the kinds of things treated as real and their material
  identities, relations, boundaries and lifecycle;
- epistemology: how claims become knowable or acceptable, including
  admissible evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification and
  decision authority;
- taxonomy: the classifications and kind distinctions that prevent
  category collapse; and
- semantics: the governed meaning of terms, relations, states, operations
  and outcomes.

These are sufficiency dimensions of the complete set, not filename classes,
required folders or a one-document-per-dimension partition. One document
may cover several dimensions and one dimension may be distributed across
several owning documents (P2).

`constitution.stdo.basis` locates the complete selected STDO constitutional
set; `constitution.additional_authorities` locates every additional
constitutional set or source. The STDO basis identifies one complete
immutable release cut and its exact installed-release manifest, never a
hand-selected subset. Each `constitution.entrypoints[]` member names the
basis against which its URI resolves. Entry points are derived navigation
and can neither narrow nor replace a complete selected constitution (P3,
P6).

This rule promotes no concrete design ontology into constitutional WHAT.
Product-level ontology that fixes Product meaning belongs in, or is cited
by, the bound WHAT. An accepted design ontology of a realisation boundary
(the design profile's) stays semantic-design authority for that boundary,
derives from constitutional WHAT and the applicable domain methods, and
cannot invent missing Product meaning (P6, P2).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F3.%20Constitutional-set%20sufficiency","start_line":187}],"statement":"The complete governing set collectively recovers axioms, ontology, epistemology, taxonomy and semantics for its scope. Bind every additional authority and resolve each entrypoint against its named basis. Product-meaning ontology belongs in or is cited by the selected WHAT. Accepted realization design has semantic-design authority only within its derived boundary and cannot invent absent Product meaning. A selected installed basis is a complete cut, never a chosen subset of favorable members.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

A selected installed basis is a complete cut, never a chosen subset of favorable members.

{"family":"relations","record":{"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ceb3153a383d5158244d9eb1007f200c","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:relation-kind:governing:requires","owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","qualifiers":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":937,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"### PC-04 — Recursive authority and information eligibility

A permitted A → B use does not entail A's access to B's dependencies. Neither
A → B plus B → C nor two routes to a shared leaf imply a union of their grants.
Each onward acquisition, disclosure or delegated effect needs authority for that
actor, purpose and path, including any permitted onward use of returned material.
Existing delegation may authorize a chain explicitly; its scope cannot expand
silently at a recursive step.

A provider may encapsulate internal dependencies behind an adequate contract.
Consumers need not flatten every implementation dependency into a direct edge.
Where an outer claim materially relies on a far-side contract, assumption,
evidence item or acquisition, that reliance and its applicable authority must be
preserved through the boundary. Unknown impact is not evidence of encapsulation.

Durable Product consumption and bounded authorized inspection are different
relations. A Reviewer or diagnostic Worker may inspect a larger causal cone under
an explicit access grant without thereby adopting those internals as a runtime
dependency or gaining a write grant. If findings become a continuing construction
constraint or dependency, their producer, applicability and governing relation
must be retained.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-04%20%E2%80%94%20Recursive%20authority%20and%20information%20eligibility","start_line":917},{"end_line":962,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"### PC-05 — Context construction and clean-room conditions

An actor's selected context must satisfy both permission and adequacy for its
engagement. Permission covers the source information and permitted derivations,
not only paths or filenames. The boundary identifies eligible source classes,
exports and tool outputs, material provenance, intended use, later acquisitions
and the effect of prior exposure. An allowed file location or a fresh summary
does not sanitize prohibited information.

A target owner may authorize an export, but clean-room eligibility additionally
requires that the engagement's information policy admits that export and its
provenance. The actual delivered/acquired material must be recorded to the extent
required by the claim. An uncertain or prohibited exposure follows the declared
hold/re-entry rule; it cannot be repaired by deleting its receipt or relabeling
the same actor fresh. Prior actor knowledge and external acquisition channels are
part of the declared limits.

Adequacy retains the distinctions required for the task's decisions and
continuations, including unresolved obligations, result standing, currentness and
authority. If the permitted material is insufficient, acquire an authorized
extension, narrow the task with the owner, use a suitable actor or return the
unresolved outcome. Permission is not evidence of sufficiency, and a budget is
not permission to omit a deciding condition. This applies [FOUNDATIONS Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assurance-relations)
and its scoped preservation law; it supplies no general optimal context selector (P1, P2, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-05%20%E2%80%94%20Context%20construction%20and%20clean-room%20conditions","start_line":939}],"kind":"requires","meaning":"The edge’s information contract must establish both permission and sufficient context for the recipient operation."},"scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"],"source":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:756ca08136ac3f65c9ee22f41d76ac8c","target":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:ab3073f9f0478efc40930f0df76d88be"}}

A declared stable cohort may select an exact `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` suffix
instead of the RC-profile suffix. Its contract names the complete required
Product and component set, current-source relationships and qualification
obligations. The historical RC-profile member set above does not limit an
explicitly selected successor cohort. Product identity and independent
third-party version pins remain distinct from the shared cohort version.

When a native package must include its derived documentation, tools or proof
views, construction first freezes the exact semantic source independently of
those generated bytes. The source record inventories every authoritative
member and native contract, classifies derived routes, and names all generated
exclusions with their owners. No authoritative source may be excluded merely
to make a digest agree. Derived candidates bind that source record, its exact
member digests and the intended cut URI. Generated frames remain projections
of their exact owners, not independent semantic authorities (P3, P5, P6).

All required installed assets are built and qualified before the native cut
is frozen. After its annotated tag and installed manifest exist, an external
cohort record binds the source freeze, complete native cut and every derived
Product subject without modifying embedded payload bytes. No asset must
embed its own containing manifest's digest. Source drift invalidates affected
derivations; generation may add only the declared auxiliary bytes. This
source-freeze construction preserves the same exact-subject, complete-ref,
atomic publication and public verification obligations below (P3, P4b, P5).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FSource%20freeze%20and%20stable%20cohort%20construction","start_line":592},{"end_line":665,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Two-commit construction and one publication transaction

Exact installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object,
so a same-commit carrier containing both that identity and derived child
bytes would be self-referential. The original RC-profile cohort, whose
derived assets are outside the native package, uses this bounded two-commit
construction. A stable cohort with embedded derived assets uses the source
freeze above and retains the same external final binding (P3, P5):

1. commit A freezes the exact STDO corpus, plugin, release record and
   their qualification bytes;
2. the annotated STDO cut tag is created locally over commit A but is not
   pushed;
3. that exact local cut is installed and verified, producing the manifest
   identity used by every derived Product and index;
4. the Axiom Indexer, STDO Representation, semantic-index bytes and cohort
   record are derived and frozen in commit B;
5. prepublication qualification evaluates commit B against the exact
   local STDO tag before child immutable tags are created;
6. annotated child cut tags and every Product-local RC branch,
   version-line selector and optional release branch are prepared
   locally;
7. a mandatory post-tag, pre-push gate re-runs qualification over every
   local annotated tag object and peel, selector, RC and release branch,
   normalised version mapping, target commit and the exact closed ref
   set; it also fetches and binds the expected remote object ID or
   required absence for every destination ref; and
8. one transport transaction atomically publishes only that qualified
   carrier branch and complete Product ref set.

If the remote does not support atomic ref publication, publication
refuses. The process has no sequential-push fallback. Every immutable cut
tag is create-only and therefore requires bound remote absence. Every
mutable carrier, RC branch, selector and release branch uses an explicit
per-ref compare-and-swap lease, such as
`--force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-oid>`, in that same atomic
transaction. A missing expected ref, unexpected existing tag or changed
remote object ID stops publication; the operator refetches and repeats
complete content and local-ref-graph qualification before constructing
another push. A lease mismatch never falls back to an unguarded force, a
partial push or an in-place expectation update (P5, P3).

Remote verification fails closed when any required cohort ref is absent,
lightweight, differently versioned, points to the wrong Product commit, or
has a selector or release branch that does not match its immutable cut.
Post-publication bookkeeping may use a later commit, but it cannot move
any immutable cohort tag (P5, P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FTwo-commit%20construction%20and%20one%20publication%20transaction","start_line":619},{"end_line":691,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Qualification and recovery

Prepublication content qualification binds the exact commit-A STDO tag
and manifest, commit-B source tree, all Product-local target refs, version
markers, Product member inventories, semantic-index bytes and complete
source-corpus digest closure. It proves that the frozen candidate can be
tagged without changing a qualifying byte. After tag and mutable ref
creation, local-ref-graph qualification binds their annotated objects,
peels, target commits, exact push set, and every fetched remote expected
object ID or required absence to that unchanged content result.
Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation from remote refs
and refuses a partial cohort (P6, P3, P5).

A historically published source cut may be the basis of a later
same-version backfill only when separately authorised recovery law names
that exception. Every recovered asset still binds the exact historical cut
and same cut name, and remote completeness remains mandatory. Recovery
cannot move the historical tag, add bytes to its Product subject, or be
represented as an atomic cohort that existed at the original publication.
Normal successor publication uses the atomic cohort process above (P3,
P6).

Adding or changing this cohort law changes qualifying bytes of this
member. It governs only an immutable successor that contains those bytes
and cannot retroactively make an earlier cut a coordinated cohort (P3).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FQualification%20and%20recovery","start_line":667}],"statement":"Assemble complete native cut A including all selected current derived and installed payloads, then record final cohort binding B outside the embedded payload. The profile has no mutable version-line selector or RC branch and does not reinterpret older same-shaped selectors.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":243,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"### Stable cuts

The `stable-v1` profile publishes an immutable release directly as
`refs/tags/<project>/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Each numeric component is a
nonnegative decimal integer, with no leading zero except the single digit
`0`. The tag is annotated, targets a commit and contains exactly one
standalone annotation line (P3):

```text
STDO-Release-Profile: stable-v1
```

Its exact release declaration names the same stable cut, declared payload,
source selection and predecessor. The installed manifest records
`release.profile = "stable-v1"` alongside the complete identity of
[Project-subtree release identity](#project-subtree-release-identity).
An RC manifest retains its prior shape; adding stable support must not
change the canonical bytes of a historical release manifest (P3, P4b).

The stable coordinate is available only on a fresh version line with no
same-version RC tag in either the historical or project-qualified namespace
and no historical unqualified bare-version tag. The stable tag itself is
create-only. A same-line collision or a missing, duplicated or different
profile marker refuses stable acquisition; bare spelling or annotation alone
cannot turn an RC selector into an immutable cut (P3, P5).

There is no separate version-line selector or RC branch for this profile.
A channel `stdo://channels/<major>.<minor>.<patch>` may discover that exact
immutable stable tag; its cut ordinal is absent (`null`), and resolution
must verify the stable profile and complete identity. That channel route
creates neither another tag nor mutable alias semantics. Consumer adoption
still follows §4 (P3, P6).

A published stable tag never moves. Any change to its qualifying bytes
requires a new version and a new immutable cut, not an RC added to the
already stable line. Historical RC lines keep their selector semantics,
refs, objects, peels and URIs; this profile neither finalises nor renames
them. An RC-labelled published release remains a proper release (P3, P4b).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities%2FStable%20cuts","start_line":206}],"label":"Stable-v1 immutable release profile"}}}

clauses.statement: Bounded realisation design: The profile concerns realisation design and implementation shape. Its goals are reduced ambiguity, entropy, avoidable debt, hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift; increased refactorability; and preserved evidence for audit and reconstruction. clauses.statement: Contracts are neither a rival backlog nor a second planning surface. The described loop selects the smallest lawful carrier for the required lifetime, drafts one run contract, deterministically validates/admit-or-rejects its classification, records admitted work basis on the selected durable carrier including an event log when required, assembles applicable prompts from admitted work law rather than raw phrasing, and checks closure against the same criteria. Conjunction of results: Combination of component results into one result for a composite predicate, a decision over evaluations, or the outer contract of composed steps. Its three distinct inputs are returned closed results with predicates and domain outcomes; planned assessments lacking an applicable closed result; and required coverage R minus coverage C admitted by planned assessments. Missing applicable results include non-performance, absence, staleness, another subject or basis, or inability to establish the required claim.
