It never silently changes an incomplete task into satisfied.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1679,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md","quote":"### Resource limits

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

- Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
  declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
  frame and its owning scope
  ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
  A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
  measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
  No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
- Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
  where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
  outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
  the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
  context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
  the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
  counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
  reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
  selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
  questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
  reported separately.
- Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
  truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
  exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
  reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
  applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
  bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
  ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
  owner of the grant or binding that set it.
- Values. The value of each limit, and the units and boundaries the
  selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
  binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
  one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
  A value is stated before the activation it limits.
- Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
  adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
  invariant (P2, P6).

Purpose and material relation: the configuration (§1), context
construction (§2) and frame qualification
([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource
limits, so the law for declaring, measuring and honouring them is stated
once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.
The material relation is whether an undeclared, unmeasured or exceeded
limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. The rule applies
RF-014's prohibition of silent omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a
resource control applies only through a selected frame, and UP-014's
selection rule.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F6.%20Cost%20and%20proportionality%2FResource%20limits","start_line":1627},{"end_line":634,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-007 Constraint and refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

Operation outcomes. A closure (AC-010), a projection (AC-011), the
structural admission of a record, model or carrier, the application of a
transformation (AC-013) and an interpretation (§6) each end in their
declared result or in one of the stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` that
this member writes. Where this member says that a condition refuses, the
operation returns `refusal` naming the condition; the record, model or
carrier is not admitted, and nothing is dropped silently. Each outcome
maps for the predicate "the operation yields its declared result on the
exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| declared result | satisfied | the closure, the projection with its boundary, the admission, the proposed successor `M_b_prime*` or the proposed model `M_subject*` is returned on the exact basis; a proposed successor or model establishes that it is available, never its acceptance or admission (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
| `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |
| `gap` | invalid_basis | the result needs a member, reference, resolution or declaration whose resolution on the basis is still open: the declared relation that resolves it has not yet decided it, as for an external resolution not yet evaluated; the result is undefined on this basis until it is supplied. A reference evaluated to no target is dangling and refuses (AC-003): a local reference with no record in the model's closed population, and an external reference whose declared resolution has been evaluated and yields no target |
| `refusal(constraint)` | falsified | every refusal that is not `refusal(basis)`: the refusal names a demonstrated violation of a declared law of this member or a constraint of its signature by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment, including a missing record family (AC-001), a dangling reference (AC-003) and an application without its traversal (AC-015), or it names no condition of the basis; the violation or other defect it names is the counterexample |
| `refusal(basis)` | invalid_basis | the refusal names one or more conditions of the basis the operation acts on and no demonstrated violation of a declared law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment: a seed set, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis or scope that is not exact; a fixed point that is not finite and unique; an input model, subject or carrier whose exact identity, basis or admission is not established; or mixed bases with no composite-basis relation (AC-006) |

The cause is part of a refusal's value, because a refusal would otherwise
map to falsified or to invalid_basis according to its cause, and a refined
value maps to exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Refinements). A refusal that names a demonstrated violation of a declared
law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or
application under judgment is `refusal(constraint)`, whatever condition of
the basis it also names. The basis condition is recorded with the refusal
and reported beside it as its own `invalid_basis` result, which names the
basis repair and answers the predicate of the evaluation that the
condition leaves without a supporting basis, never the operation-outcome
predicate that the refusal answers
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Predicates travel). A refusal that names only conditions of the basis is
`refusal(basis)`. A violation inside an input that the operation acts on
as its basis is a condition of the basis for that operation, not a
violation by what it judges, as the projection below shows. Purpose and
material relation: a demonstrated violation is a known failure, which
survives every join only as a `falsified` result, so a basis condition
named beside it neither hides the failure nor discards its counterexample,
and the basis repair stays named (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results,
Survival; P5, P6). A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.
One defect can bear on two predicates: a model that violates AC-001 is
`refusal(constraint)` in the structural admission that judges it and
`refusal(basis)` in a projection over it, and each outcome answers its own
predicate. An operation that was not applied has no outcome. A stop `gap`
is a closed result with the value invalid_basis; it is not the absence of
a result that
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
records as a gap. A signature's stop contract and a traversal record map
stops of their own under §5.

Purpose and material relation: a
constraint result or an operation's stop combines with results of other
members only through the one core, so a refusal, a hold or a gap is
neither read as success nor mistaken for another case; and a closure or
projection that is not established has the value invalid_basis here, as
the activation outcome `closure_unresolved` of
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) has for its own
predicate (P5, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-007%20Constraint%20and%20refusal","start_line":536}],"label":"Predicate-relative exhaustion"}}}

clauses.statement: Observation and admitted checking relation: A checker has observation map π: Ω → O and admitted evaluation relation T ⊆ O × R, where R is the core result domain. Deterministic checking is a functional special case; human or probabilistic checking may admit different conclusions for identical observations. Universal soundness covers every admitted conclusion: for every s in Ω, (π(s), sat) in T implies q_t(s), and (π(s), fal) in T implies not q_t(s). sat and fal denote judgments about q_t, not execution states.

A declared stable cohort may select an exact `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` suffix
instead of the RC-profile suffix. Its contract names the complete required
Product and component set, current-source relationships and qualification
obligations. The historical RC-profile member set above does not limit an
explicitly selected successor cohort. Product identity and independent
third-party version pins remain distinct from the shared cohort version.

When a native package must include its derived documentation, tools or proof
views, construction first freezes the exact semantic source independently of
those generated bytes. The source record inventories every authoritative
member and native contract, classifies derived routes, and names all generated
exclusions with their owners. No authoritative source may be excluded merely
to make a digest agree. Derived candidates bind that source record, its exact
member digests and the intended cut URI. Generated frames remain projections
of their exact owners, not independent semantic authorities (P3, P5, P6).

All required installed assets are built and qualified before the native cut
is frozen. After its annotated tag and installed manifest exist, an external
cohort record binds the source freeze, complete native cut and every derived
Product subject without modifying embedded payload bytes. No asset must
embed its own containing manifest's digest. Source drift invalidates affected
derivations; generation may add only the declared auxiliary bytes. This
source-freeze construction preserves the same exact-subject, complete-ref,
atomic publication and public verification obligations below (P3, P4b, P5).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F7.%20Coordinated%20release-matched%20asset%20cohorts%2FSource%20freeze%20and%20stable%20cohort%20construction","start_line":592}],"statement":"Freeze exact semantic source member identities before dependent representation and proof generation. Use this reference when issuing work to another activation or receiving its
packet. A direct invocation with sufficient context and authority follows the
skill's ordinary procedure. The active frame and grant decide the branch;
writing “Executive”, “Worker” or “receive” in a prompt grants nothing.

Start with your own [Control Intake](#control-intake), then resolve only the
needed owner sections through [Product Basis Selection](PRODUCT_BASIS.md)
on the Product's exact basis. `REFERENCE_FRAME` §11 owns the packet;
`ACTIVATION` §1–3, §5 and §7 own admission, acquisition, effects and reuse;
`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §6, §12–13 and §19 apply where that profile is adopted.
This reference supplies their interaction route, not replacement authority.
A missing owner route is unresolved; do not substitute a neighbouring cut.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff","start_line":1},{"end_line":354,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md","quote":"## Invocation Examples

These are requests to the skill, not substitutes for their referenced grants.
Use the host's installed skill invocation syntax or open its exact entrypoint.

```text
Use stdo-work as issuer for the admitted W1 entry in <carrier at exact identity>.
Keep my Executive frame. Issue its permitted packet and evaluate the return.
```

```text
Use stdo-work as recipient of <packet at exact identity>.
Check its control bindings before subject reads, execute its authorized unit,
and return through the packet's result relation.
```

```text
Use stdo-review to issue the required review of <exact candidate> under
<assessment grant>. Preserve its independence conditions and return boundary.
```

For direct work, “Use stdo-work for <authorized bounded change>” continues to
use the ordinary direct path when the accepted configuration permits it.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#Coordinated%20Skill%20Handoff%2FInvocation%20Examples","start_line":332}],"statement":"Issuer, recipient and review invocation examples request the relevant same-skill branch under an already identified grant. A model `M_b` is a valid model of `a_c` under signature `Sigma`, written
`M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma]`, only when (P6, P1):

1. `Sigma` and the exact `a_c` basis resolve;
2. every record satisfies AC-001 through AC-009;
3. every claimed closure, projection, overlay, transformation, judgment
   and composition satisfies its applicable law, and every claimed functor
   application satisfies AC-015 and its bound kind's §5 contract;
4. interpretation fidelity and residual dispositions bind the exact
   subject;
5. structural evaluation and semantic acceptance remain distinct and both
   required where claimed; and
6. all evidence, provenance, invalidation and re-entry coordinates
   resolve.

the semantic or authority subset unless the model supplies an exact lawful
decision contract for it (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F6.%20Interpretation%20and%20models%2FAC-019%20Valid%20model","start_line":1170},{"end_line":1168,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-018 Structural and semantic separation

rule that structural success is evidence for semantic review and no
substitute for it, are [EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation)'s,
which owns them for every review. This law binds them to `a_c`: the
structural conformance of a model covers its closed syntax, types,
identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates, and
the semantic fidelity of an interpretation covers its meaning and
materiality (P1, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F6.%20Interpretation%20and%20models%2FAC-018%20Structural%20and%20semantic%20separation","start_line":1159}],"statement":"Resolve the exact signature/basis and satisfy AC-001–009 for every record plus every applicable closure, projection, overlay, transformation, judgment and typed-composition law. A Product identifies one coherent WHAT and its owning authority. Alternative
realizations of that WHAT are build tenants. A decomposition into Products names
which distinct outcomes and authorities each constituent owns, and which outer
outcome the composition owns.

Under the identity and ownership laws (P3, P6), within a declared decomposition scope, a leaf has no further constituent Product
boundary exposed by that decomposition. It may contain modules and declared
external dependencies. A composite relates two or more constituent capabilities
or an outer capability to its constituent capability; its own capability may in
turn be consumed as a constituent. The same definition, contract and authority
laws apply at every depth. Shared constituents keep one identity and their
separately bound uses; a hierarchy view may show several references to one leaf.

Decomposition, capability/data dependency, inspection permission, authority and
work prerequisites are distinct relations. A directory tree establishes none of
them. A named composition view states its root, participating identities,
selected boundaries and relation kinds rather than treating all reachable edges
as one hierarchy.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-01%20%E2%80%94%20Recursive%20Product%20boundaries","start_line":857},{"end_line":893,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"### PC-02 — Independent entry and the integrated outcome

A Product offered as a standalone constituent must be enterable through its own
Product Definition and a Product-authorized applicable frame basis, with the
dependency closure and capabilities its contract declares. Entry must not require
an enclosing composition's activation unless that enclosing capability is itself
an explicit prerequisite. Such a prerequisite is disclosed as a limit on the
standalone claim. Shared or externally located frame documents are permitted
where adoption, scope and availability are established; file ownership alone is
not the deciding test.

Standalone does not imply dependency-free, separately deployable or able to
supply every host itself. The claim names which construction, evaluation or use
can be performed independently and its required inputs. The composition owner
separately establishes interface compatibility, material joins and its complete
outcome. Successful constituent checks do not establish that outer predicate.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-02%20%E2%80%94%20Independent%20entry%20and%20the%20integrated%20outcome","start_line":878}],"statement":"Bind the smallest coherent Product outcome and owner, preserve each shared leaf identity and each separate use relation, and distinguish alternative build tenants from composition. A component can be qualified for standalone scope without establishing a parent outcome. Composition acceptance evaluates its actual joins, assumptions and integrated claim; all local green results are insufficient when a join fails.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

Each cross-boundary use binds the actual selected sources and material execution
basis, including uncommitted bytes where relevant. A moving selection identifies
how advancement is detected and which reliance must be reassessed. Git is one
possible carrier, not a mandatory identity system.

Changes and new counterexamples propagate through material assertion, execution
and evidence-use dependencies under [FOUNDATIONS Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse). Historical
evidence remains about its original subject. Reuse on a changed subject needs an
established applicability or preservation relation; rereading alone does not
establish it. A new release does not invalidate a still-selected older release,
and a changed hash alone establishes neither semantic incompatibility nor
continued validity. Unknown impact holds the dependent assurance or widens
assessment; it does not require unrelated work to restart.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-07%20%E2%80%94%20Change%2C%20evidence%20and%20reliance","start_line":980}],"statement":"Select actual authoritative source bytes, including admitted uncommitted source where applicable. Context and position

This member owns the release-publication bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication` under the selected complete
STDO basis. It owns the identities and transitions used to qualify,
publish and select released cuts. It does not own Product meaning or
consumer adoption; the consumer side of adoption is PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4
(P6, P3).

Release process is distinct from live project specification. Live
specification defines the current constitutional truth of the project.
Release process defines how one published point-in-time cut is evaluated,
bounded, named, published and made discoverable (P3).

The release authority selects one of two disjoint cut profiles (P3, P6):

- RC: product-local `v<version>-rc.<n>`, with a mutable `v<version>`
  version-line selector naming the greatest published positive RC ordinal;
- stable-v1: product-local `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, with no RC suffix and
  no separate mutable selector at that ref, under
  [§2 Stable cuts](#stable-cuts).

Both profiles identify immutable published releases. The RC suffix does not
make a published release provisional or require a second final cut. The
stable profile is an explicit naming and discovery choice, not stronger
semantic qualification. Equal product-local names do not collapse different
Products. A mutable RC selector remains discovery, never an exact
constitutional, dependency, evidence or replay basis (P3, P6).

Release handling is downstream of intake triage. A bug, feature,
regression or release blocker first receives its change class, lawful
re-entry point, affected scope, downstream proof obligations and
version-line disposition
([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#universal-intake-triage)). The existence
of an RC window does not authorise untriaged mutation (P0, P6).

Results. This member defines no result values of its own. Where it says
that an operation is refused, stops or fails closed, the operation does
not complete; its intended effect, with any part of it that began, is
reported under [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects), never as
`completed`.
Where it calls a release state invalid or a cohort incomplete, or says
that a verification fails, the condition named is a counterexample to the
predicate that check evaluates, and the check returns its value under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). What the disposition
values of §9 are, §9 states. Purpose and material relation: release
outcomes combine with every other result in the one core, so a refused
publication or a failed verification is never read as a published or
qualified cut (P5, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F1.%20Context%20and%20position","start_line":32},{"end_line":313,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md","quote":"## 3. Phases

The release process has three phases (P0, P3, P6):

1. mutable candidate construction;
2. immutable publication under the selected profile, with RC selector
   advancement only for an RC line; and
3. exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.

An accepted RC needs no second final cut. RC publication immediately makes
the new highest ordinal discoverable through its selector. Stable publication
makes its one exact tag discoverable under the stable profile. Acceptance is
a verdict over the exact immutable subject, not a second carrier. A change
to qualifying bytes requires a higher RC on an applicable RC line or a new
version after a stable cut (P3, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases","start_line":299}],"label":"Release publication and acceptance"}}}

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:62c03e6b02ba6e5c63e0e2e4c0dad571"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:f8581de2520c99aae4837dede0f90a61","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":350,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","quote":"## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis
is the pair (P3):

```text
(immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)
```

The URI identifies one immutable annotated release cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status
and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8
JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line
endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path
order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible
rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).

The STDO Toolchain Manager is the bounded executable realisation that (P2,
P3):

- installs each immutable cut once in a shared, versioned release store;
- resolves logical `stdo://releases/...` URIs to verified installed bytes;
- inventories and verifies complete installed distributions;
- synchronises the exact basis already selected by a Product Definition;
- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a release-profile discovery
  route and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly
  accepted;
- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and
- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product
  Definitions.

The store may live at any machine-local path. Its registry maps logical
release URIs to installed paths and manifest digests and owns neither
Product selection nor method meaning. A consumer repository therefore needs
no project-local standards copy and no prescribed folder structure, and
several Product Definitions on one machine may select different installed
cuts concurrently (P3, P6). Every manager-owned component from the
configured store root downward is a physical directory or regular file of
its declared type; a symlink, junction, reparse point, device, socket or
other redirection or special entry fails closed. Verification inventories
every filesystem entry type, directories included, rejects any entry not
derived from the manifest's exact file paths, and never follows an
unmanifested alias (P5, P3).

`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.
`constitution.stdo.selector` is a `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery
route whose profile semantics are owned by [RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption).
An RC line resolves its mutable selector; a stable line resolves its exact
immutable cut without a second selector. Neither discovery nor the transport
source is operative authority.
`constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256`
are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).

The manager observes these command boundaries (P6, P5):

- `install` admits one explicitly named immutable release cut without changing
  any Product Definition;
- `sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by
  the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector;
- `adopt --dry-run` resolves the selected release profile and immutable cut, and
  presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest,
  current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic
  adoption-plan digest, without mutation;
- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit
  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound
  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes
  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses
  mutation;
- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with
  respect to Product Definitions; and
- fleet adoption emits, and requires explicit acceptance of, one aggregate
  plan digest over every per-definition plan; all fleet writes require
  explicit whole-selection authorisation and infer no composition or
  inheritance from directory nesting.

Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag-to-commit mismatch, manifest-digest
mismatch, missing, extra or changed installed members, ambiguous Product
Definition discovery, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, URI escape,
physical store redirection, undeclared filesystem entry types and malformed
bootstrap markers fail closed (P5). Every `stdo:` schema locator is parsed
before schema loading under URI scheme case-insensitivity and names the
same immutable cut as `constitution.stdo.basis`; spelling variation cannot
cross that basis. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias,
schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the
Product Definition (P6, P3).

`constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one
basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such
as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the
manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative
path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent
traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail
closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its
explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the
first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced;
the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay
project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all
existing bytes as an exact prefix. The bootstrap routes agents to the
applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning
sources; it can neither restate nor override them (P6, P3, P5).

Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as
version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals:
`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`,
`site-packages`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `target`, `.gradle`, `.tox`,
`.nox`, `.cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`,
`__pycache__`, `.genesis` and `.stdo`. A discovered Product Definition may
not itself be a symlink. These exclusions are discovery law, not evidence
that an excluded tree lacks another independently governed Product (P5,
P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F4.%20Shared%20installed%20release%20basis%20and%20toolchain%20manager","start_line":225}],"statement":"Missing exact-plan acceptance or fleet whole-selection authorization is missing operation authority: admission_refused(authority) maps to out_of_frame and names the owner. F_P may reason and propose; F_D may implement eligible deterministic checks, but kind alone does not make a semantic or authority admission decision.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1562,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"### 11.7A Conforming agentic development

This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
graph-native worksite. An agentic coder produces governed work by
following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).

Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
to admit (P6).

The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
requirement, design and ticket chain, the constructive evaluation loop of
§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
constitutional process (P0, P6).

The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the
packet carries only the smallest declared authority sufficient to decide
the step, with its source refs, and that conformance is enforced by
admitting the produced artifact rather than by enlarging what the agent
must hold. Compression is prompt input and never the deciding authority
(P0, P6). What a derived surface may decide is owned by
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition and Standalone scope; this section adds only the ODD limit
that follows. A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The walkthrough proves at two levels. The work it produces must be lawful:
correct change class, traceable, admitted. A point where the walkthrough
cannot proceed is a method defect only when a competent agent, correctly
configured and using the declared authority, still cannot decide because
of ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or an undecidable
change class in an owning surface. That defect is repriced into the owning
authority surface, as a failed manual traversal is a graph defect under
§11.7 (P6, P5).

An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

This proof is independent of any automated runtime. A live lane that
depends on external execution conditions, such as an overloaded model API
or a flaky transport, cannot prove the constitutional process sound,
because it conflates process validity with runtime availability. The
walkthrough proves the process; the runtime only executes it (P6, P5).

The validator is the conformance gate. The constitutional process is an
interface contract, and interface conformance is enforced by validating
artifacts against the contract, not by the conformer holding the contract.
This profile does not declare the artifact rules again: tickets,
change-class declarations, design-module derivations and execution
contracts are admitted under SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS, which already require
a drafted classification to be admitted or rejected against deterministic
criteria rather than taken as automatic truth. This profile requires only
that agentic development pass through that admission. The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,
fail-closed and naming the violated rule, exactly as a typed asset is
enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

This keeps the F_P and F_D split at the method layer. The agentic coder is
F_P: it reasons, drafts and proposes within the declared packet. Admission
uses F_D only when the §5 total-domain contract is established, and its own
contract and authority determine what artifact-conformance decision it may
make. An unresolved eligibility assessment stays open under the migration
relation; an unchanged-subject evaluator still preserves that subject. The walkthrough
establishes that the process can be followed; admission establishes that
each act of following it conforms (P6, P0).

Conformance is not approval by usage. A passed admission and a completed
walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification. Shared method
change still follows §9: repeated agentic execution does not make grey
work constitutional. The agentic coder conforms to the method; it does not
amend the method by acting (P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F11.%20Core%20law%2F11.7A%20Conforming%20agentic%20development","start_line":1474}],"label":"Conforming agentic development"}}}

clauses.statement: Conforming agentic development: Agentic conformance distinguishes a source-grounded process-followability walkthrough from artifact admission under existing Product and method rules. F_P may reason and propose; F_D may implement eligible deterministic checks, but kind alone does not make a semantic or authority admission decision.

   Reference-Frame Basis.

   section under the selected basis's `ACTIVATION.md` section 2,
   Acquisition, from that exact basis only.
2. Read the smallest relevant project surface: Goals, Intent, Product, affected
   requirements, accepted design, work carrier, then the owning standard.
   Start from available source routes, exact computed status and still-valid
   recorded judgments. Load additional context only for a material unknown or
   applicable evaluation. An installed-basis verification establishes that
   basis's integrity; it does not establish work completion or companion readiness.
3. If no Product Definition exists and setup is authorized, point to
   [`../../references/GETTING_STARTED.md`](../../references/GETTING_STARTED.md)

Explain the next functional outcome in the user's terms. Determine whether
they need orientation, construction, evidence assessment, an owner ruling,
continuation, recovery, adoption or conclusion; route only the affected part.

frame basis permits it. Do not add a coordinating activation, ticket or review merely to
answer a help request. Ask for a missing owner choice only when the next action
depends on it; reuse a sufficient existing ruling.

For review, repair, landing or closure questions, use
[the selected review flow](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#review-flow-from-the-selected-basis).
Do not infer a review ratio, P0–P5 meanings or a particular Product gate from
this skill. Ask only for a missing policy choice that affects the requested
next action; preserve direct work and any already sufficient ruling.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-help/SKILL.md#STDO%20Help%2FEstablish%20The%20Basis","start_line":56},{"end_line":98,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/plugins/spec/skills/stdo-help/SKILL.md","quote":"## Return

Evidence includes entry invocation, observed semantic path/authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, transitions, outputs, claimed replay/reconstruction, installed identity and negative paths. Capability requires observing the complete path without changing it, distinguishing rivals and reproducing material state/failure relations.

{"family":"constraints","record":{"applies_to":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:c0fabfe466142ed2e89ce7e0b9e7bcc2"],"basis":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:basis","context":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:context:source-first-proposal","id":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:record:fd4604dcc67a3569f95175e9dcb61b97","judgment_kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:judgment-kind:external-semantic-review","kind":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:constraint-kind:authored-source-statement","latitude_ref":[],"owner":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:actor:f-p-author","predicate":{"conditions":[],"exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":384,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md","quote":"### Probabilistic compute

Probabilistic compute in this profile is bounded constructive work over
one declared vector or edge traversal, where the graph or runtime does not
fully determine the worker's internal solution path. One vector or edge
traversal is the bounded unit of probabilistic compute (P0).

Binding of the bounded step. FOUNDATIONS P0 lets a
profile bind the bounded step to its own traversal unit and names
[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this profile,
as the keeper of that binding. Direction: from the step of
FOUNDATIONS P0 to one declared ODD vector or edge traversal. Preserved
meaning: the step's selected context fits the actor's envelope, the
actor's internal path within the step is its own, and the traversal is
the admissible external space. Narrowed scope: one declared vector or edge
traversal of a published graph. Invalidation: a change to FOUNDATIONS P0,
to the vector's declaration or to the selected basis invalidates the
binding until it is evaluated again (P0, P1).

The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
states. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it
does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal
boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM
reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local
execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).

The classifications of work inside one traversal bind two profile
specialisations and one common import. Equal spelling alone establishes
none of those relations (P1, P3):

- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the
  bounded probabilistic worker turn. It specialises substrate-neutral
  lawful probabilistic processing: it keeps bounded non-human construction
  under declared policy and narrows that meaning to one graph traversal
  contract.
- `F_D` imports `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d` from
  [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
  in the exact complete STDO release selected by the application, including
  its immutable calculus edition. It adds the graph traversal's operation
  contract, scope and authority, not another definition of the kind.
  Existing evaluation and proof operations retain the unchanged-subject
  evaluation profile; admission and construction operations retain their
  own evidence contracts and grants. Use of the common kind is conditional
  on the total-domain eligibility assessment in
  [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). Domain-local
  optimization or validation moves no domain HOW into GTL, ABG or the
  framework and grants no broader consequences.
- `F_H` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`) is the shorthand for
  explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared
  authority and ambiguity policy. It specialises the substrate-neutral
  human-adjudication concept and grants a human no ambient traversal,
  semantic or closure authority.

F_P and F_H are the two declared specialisations that PROFILES §1 requires. The F_P
specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`; the F_H specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`. The source concepts and their
context are owned by
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle); this
profile owns the targets in the graph-native ODD context (P1, P6).

Both relations preserve the source meaning and authority, narrow scope to
a declared ODD traversal, and add graph-contract and runtime-control
coordinates. They exclude processing or adjudication outside that
traversal, refuse ambient worker or human authority, and have no implied
inverse. Their source and target basis is the selected complete STDO
release, their governed scope is ODD traversal, and this clause is their
provenance carrier. A change to either concept or context, to the basis,
to the scope, to the preserved or narrowed meaning or to the control
contract invalidates the affected specialisation until it is evaluated
again (P1, P3, P6).

The F_D import runs from the common concept to its use under this profile,
preserves the common total deterministic contract, and narrows each use to
its declared ODD operation. Its source and target basis is the exact
selected complete release; a change to that edition, traversal contract,
material dependency, termination evidence or authority invalidates the
affected eligibility claim. The former
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d` remains a historical concept on its
legacy edition. It is not an unconditional alias: only the explicit
[migration mapping](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration) licenses a
successor use, preserving the original evidence, permissions and results.

The profile governs the traversal contract, its evidence, its provenance
and its control truth. It does not make the framework the executor of the
domain's internal solution strategy (P0, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F5.%20Graph%20model%2FProbabilistic%20compute","start_line":294},{"end_line":1061,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"## 5. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"Current ODD uses the exact common F_D definition and its declared deterministic operation profile; it does not unconditionally alias the historical urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d meaning to the current kind. Keep F_P probabilistic construction and F_H adjudication specializations and their grants distinct. A deterministic operation may construct or evaluate, but its totality/dependency contract and operation authority must be established independently. Neither this import nor equal names makes runtime operations identical.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

clauses.statement: Bind a sufficient direct Writer path and material conditions requiring coordination. Direct entry requires exact work authority, admission, operation scope and closure conditions, without adding an inapplicable ticket, coordinating appointment or review. Coordinated topology is existing authority → basis/outcome lock → exact Worker/Reviewer/specialist activation → closed result plus applicable Reviewer triage → Executive or declared conjunction → priority/boundary effect → authorized disposition and next activation, stop or re-entry. Construction by the same actor requires separately bound Writer activation inheriting the exact grant; changing role creates neither authority nor independence.

clauses.statement: The three layers retain independent content identities, judgments, supersession and proof obligations. Calculus qualification tests internal coherence against its complete declared laws; interpretation proves fidelity to exact X; carrier qualification proves faithful canonical encoding of the accepted model. Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5-rc.1/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"The source-level contract is represented, but no arbitrary downstream algorithm, infinite-domain termination proof or runtime dependency closure is established by this representation."}}}
